text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ year old patient with a history of seizure disorder who presented from patient's rehab facility with questionable seizures and fevers. . # Altered mental status/encephalopathy: Pt was initially admitted with unresponsiveness with concern for seizure given patient's seizure disorder. Neurology was consulted and EEG was performed that did not show seizure activity. patient was found to have a UTI, urine culture grew klebsiella. patient was treated with ceftriaxone that was later changed to meropenem given concern for possible angioedema (see below). patient was then found to have fungal UTI and was started on fluconazole (see below). Mental status returned to baseline. patient was continued on patient's home dose of phenytoin then uptitrated as patient was subtherapeutic (see below). . # Seizure disorder: Patient initially presented with concern for seizures. Neurology was consulted and EEG did not show seizure activity. Patient continued on patient's home dilantin dose. On ___ patient had seizure x3. Dilantin level was checked and was undectable. Patient was reloaded with IV fosphenytoin. Patient's home dilantin dose was increased to 125 mg BID. Dilantin level at time of discharge was 14.9 when corrected for hypoalbuminemia. Please recheck patient's dilantin dose in three days and adjust dilantin dosing; target dilantin level is 16. . # UTI, bacterial, and UTI, candidal: Pt initially had klebsiella UTI treated with meropenem. patient had repeat UA after seizure with 150 WBCs. Urine culture grew yeast x3. Discussed with ID, started fluconazole for 10 days. Last dose for fluconazole is ___. Please follow up with a repeat UA at the end of fluconazole course. . # Respiratory distress: Upon presentation to ED, concern was high for seizure and pt received benzodiazepines. In this setting, patient developed hypoxia and required intubation. patient required minimal ventilatory support and was able to follow commands without need for much sedation. Extubation was attempted on ___ but patient required re-intubation within 3 hours due to respiratory distress. patient had a large amount of laryngeal edema that was felt to be responsible for patient's failed extubation and patient was placed on IV steroids to reduce swelling. patient had several allergies to antibiotics with adverse reaction being angioedema. Given concern that patient's ceftriaxone may be causing angioedema, patient was switched to meropenem. Extubation was attempted again on ___ patient once again developed respiratory distress and hypoxia within 6 hours and required re-intubation. A large amount of edema was again noted. ENT was consulted regarding tracheostomy. They recommended CT neck to evaluate size of patient's large multinodular goiter. They brought patient's to the OR on ___ for subtotal thyroidectomy and extubation was again performed on ___. While in the ICU, patient's total body balance was positive 14 liters and crackles were appreciated on lung exam and patient had edema of patient's limbs. Patient was given lasix and patient's edema improved along with patient's lung exam. Please monitor patient's fluid status and respiratory status and give diuretics as needed. Extra fluid in patient's body should mobilize and be excreted in urine. . # s/p Subtotal thyroidectomy: Pt was noted to have large multinodular goiter. TFTs were within normal limits. patient had been on methimazole as outpatient; this was not continued in ___. CT neck showed large goiter and pt was seen by ENT who recommended thyroidectomy as the goiter was compressing patient's trachea and may have been the reason for patient's failed extubations. Thoracic surgery was also called regarding possible tracheomalacia seen on CT scan. Thoracic surgery felt that this was not tracheomalacia but rather compression of trachea from thyroid mass. patient underwent thyroidectomy on ___. Right thyroid lobe was left; parathyroids were left in place. Calcium was monitored carefully postoperatively. patient had JP drain in place after surgery which was removed. patient should follow up with patient's endocrinologist 3 weeks after discharge and Dr. ___ to follow up with outcome of surgery. . # Volume overload / upper extremity edema: Patient's total body fluid balance during patient's ICU stay was positive 14 liters. patient required several doses of IV lasix as patient developed pulmonary edema. patient's upper extremities were noted to be swollen (L>R). Bilateral upper extremity ultrasound was obtained and showed no-occlussive thrombi in right and left IJ. No anti-coagulation was initated as there is no clear evidence of benefit in non-occlussive thrombi. Please continue to monitor patient's upper extremities and reevaluate as needed. . # Transitional issues: 1) Follow up with ENT in 2 weeks; must call to schedule appointment 2) Follow up with endocrinology in 3 weeks; must call to schedule appointment 3) Follow up with PCP regarding this hospitalization 4) Recheck dilantin level in 3 days (must correct for hypoalbuminemia) and consider readjusting dosing; target level is 16. 5) Notable labs on last check here: Hct 27.4, Cr 1.5, ALT 47, AST 31, phenytoin (Dilantin) level 11.3. These can be followed-up after discharge.
summary: You were admitted to the medicine service for workup and management of your confusion. Your confusion was likely multifactorial as outlined below. You were given lorazepam because there were concerns of seizures, but EEG monitoring did not reveal any evidence of seizure. As a consequence, your breathing was suppressed and had to be sedated and intubated to help you breath better. After successful removal of your breathing tube, you had a seizure and was found that your dilantin level was subtherapeutic secondary to propofol withdrawal and malabsorption of dilantin due to the tube feed you were receiving while intubated. You received loading doses of dilantin and your maintenance dose was increased to 125mg twice daily from 100mg twice daily. On the day of discharge, your dilantin level adjusted for hypoalbuminemia was 14.9.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ y/o man with a history of HIV/AIDS (CD4:6, VL:157,941 on ___ on HAART, HIV myosititis, gout, depression, mesentry thrombosis on coumadin, recently d/c'd from ___ w/ CNS lesions and high ___ virus titer, thought to be consistent with PML, presents from rehab after unwitnessed fall. Acute issues: # Fall: In the setting of recent diarrhea and what appears to be poor PO intake it was felt that the patient's fall was most likely the result of orthostatic syncope in the setting of dehydration. He was given IV hydration. However, given his increasing confusion (see below) it was difficult to assess his symptomatic response. The patient had difficulty describing the event but did initially endorse symptoms such as shaking and incontinence concerning for seizure activity. Neurology was consulted and felt this episode was most likely the result of orthostatic syncope versus micturition related syncope, as the patient was going to the bathroom at the time of the fall. Given his known intracranial pathology they did recommend a routine EEG which did not show seizures but did have abnormalities concerning for risk of seizure. Therefore the patient was started on seizure prophylaxis with Keppra. The patient was monitored on telemetry for several days to rule out arrhythmia without event. EKG was at unchanged from previous and there was no suggestion of a cardiac etiology of his syncope. The patient did not have another episode of syncope during this admission, though he was only minimally ambulating throughout the course of his hospitalization. . # Leukocytosis/ Fevers: The patient was noted to have a leukocytosis on admission in the setting of diarrhea. Extensive work-up of possible infectious etiologies for his leukocytosis were negative. This work-up included blood cultures and urine cultures showing no growth, chest xray x 2 that showed no pneumonia, exam that was not suggestive of a soft tissue infection, stool w/u negative for cyclospora, Cryptosporidium/Giardia, C. diff x 2, O+P x2 , salmonella and shigella, and negative CMV PCR. At the time of discharge microsporidia stain and MAC blood culture were pending. Initial exam was not concerning for a second CNS infection on top of the known PML and as such a lumbar puncture was not performed. The patient's white blood cell count trended downward without intervention. However, he remained intermittently febrile with temperatures to ___ F. Infectious Disease was consulted and upon further history taking from the patient's wife determined that he had not been taking his HAART previous to his last admission 2 weeks prior. They therefore felt that given the negative infectious work-up, his fevers were likely central in nature and possible representative of ___. A repeat CT scan of his head was consistent with either worsening of his PML related edema or ___. There was discussion of increasing his prednisione dose and ultimately his prednisone was increased to 60 mg daily for one week and then tapered back to 10 mg daily over several weeks. Additionally, infectious disease did not feel that his fevers were due to an acute infection that required therapy or further diagnostic work-up. At the time of discharge the patient continued to have intermittent fevers. . # Acute Mental Status Changes: The patient was essentially at his baseline mental status at the time of admission and was oriented to both self and place but not date. However in speaking with his family it became clear that this has only been his baseline for the past few months. Additionally, his mental status continued to decline over the course of the hospitalization and he became increasingly confused. He also noted new frontal headaches and repeat imaging of his head showed progression of previously noted edema of the white matter consistent with either progression of PML or ___. Given there was an explanation for his confusion it was not felt an LP would have diagnostic value and therefore it was not done. His outpatient ID doctor, with whom he has had a relationship for the past several years, visited him as an inpatient. patient noted a marked decline in his mental status over the past few months and felt as though he was entering into end stage disease. patient was of the opinion that he should be made comfort measures only and that he would not benefit from rehospitalization. The inpatient ID service agreed that prognosis was extremely poor and that the patient likely did not have long to live. This was communicated with the patients wife in several family meetings, palliative care was also consulted to provide support and information regarding end of life decisions as below. . # ___: Patients creatinine was elevated to 2.5 at the time of admission. FeNa was 0.5% consistent with a pre-renal etiology due to dehydration in the setting of diarrhea. Creatinine trended down to 1.6 with administration of IVF. However creatinine remained 1.6 throughout the remainder of admission. Differential for his acute renal failure includes ATN or AIN related to his medications and glomerular disease related to either his HIV or hepatitis B. At the time of discharge his creatinine was 1.6. . # Abdominal pain: Patient reported predominantly left sided abdominal pain. He had CT a/p in the ED that was unremarkable. As work-up of his abdominal pain did not isolate an infectious source. He was therefore managed symptomatically with tylenol for pain, IVF and Maalox. . PML: As above repeat imaging showed either progression of disease or ___ and patients clinical presentation worsened over the course of admission. The patient has extremely resistant HIV and it was felt his HAART was already optimized. Therefore he was continued on his home regimen. Due to the concern for ___ he was continued on low dose steroids initially which were then increased as as above. It was felt that given his poor prognosis steroids would likely not greatly effect the course of his PML and might provide some symptomatic relief. As above, infectious disease ultimately felt that there was no further intervention for his PML and that his prognosis was very poor. . #Thrombocytopenia: Over the course of the the admission the patients plt count has trended down to a nadir of 66. It was felt that this possibly due to a viral infection though as stated above a CML PCR was negative. Additionally, given deteriorating liver function platelet production was potentially playing a role. DIC was less likely given lack of schistosytes on blood smear and a normal T.bili. Also less likely was HIT though the patient was exposed to heparin on last admission. . #Transaminitis: The patient was noted to have elevations of his LFTs which trended upward over this admission. It was unclear if this was representative of his known hepatitis B or reflective of generalized multi-organ dysfunction. Given his poor prognosis as detailed above no further diagnostic work-up was undertaken. . # HIV: Patient was continued on home medications. On admission these medications were renally dosed however he was returned to his home regimen once kidney function improved. . #Goals of Care: Given the serious nature of the patients illness and his rapid decompensation, palliative care was consulted to help facilitate a dialogue with the patient's wife regarding goals of care. The wife vocalized understanding of the serious nature of patient's husbands condition and that he would likely not recover. patient expressed that patient's husbands last wish was to have his mother come visit from ___. patient was referred to ___ for assistance in obtaining an emergency visa for the patient's mother. In terms of code status patient ultimately felt that the patient would want to be full code pending the possible arrival of his mother but after his mother arrived he would not want invasive interventions such as intubation and CPR. . # Rectal prolapse: The patient was noted to have one instance of a small amount of bright red blood per rectum. On exam at that time it was noted that he had prolapse of approximately 1 cm of rectum. The area was very tender to palpation but was easily reduced. He did not have any further instances of blood in his stools or complain of further rectal pain. . #Wrist pain: The patient noted L wrist pain in the setting of a recent fall. The wrist did have an area of ecchymosis and a small amount of swelling however xrays did not indicate a fracture. The patient was managed symptomatically with scheduled tylenol. . #Thrush: Patient was noted to have white oral plaques on exam consistent with oral thrush. He was started on oral clotrimazole with improvement. . Stable Issues . # Mesenteric Thrombosis: Patients INR was supratherapeutic on admission. His coumadin was initially held. It was restarted at a dose of 3 mg. At the time of discharge his INR was 2.1. He will need INR monitoring at rehab. . # HIV myositis: Patient was continued on home prednisone. . # Depression: Patient was continued on home celexa and mirtazipime. . summary: You were admitted after you had a fall at the rehab facility. We think you were likely dizzy because you had not been drinking enough fluids and were having diarrhea. We tested you for infections to explain your diarrhea but did not find any source. You were given IV fluids to help to hydrate you and your diarrhea seemed to improve. You were also more confused. We got a CT of your head which showed the infection in your brain has gotten worse. The infectious diease doctors also feel your immune system might also be making you sicker as it tries to fight infections in your body. There was also some concern that you might be having a seizure. A test was done to look at brain activity and did not show seizures. However, it did show a pattern that may put you a high risk for seizures so you were started on a medication to help prevent this from happening. Both your kidneys and liver are having difficulty functioning correctly.

text: Brief Hospital Course: HOSPITAL COURSE This is a ___ year old patient with a past medical history significant for depression/anxiety, spinal stenosis, fibromyalgia and lupus on steroids and methotrexate who presents with 2 weeks of low back pain. MRI consistent with new compression at fracture at L2. patient was discharged with a lidocaine patch, ultram and follow up in both pain clinic and PCP. . ACTIVE ISSUE # BACK PAIN. Etiology most consistent with radicular pain associated with MRI findings of compression fracture of the L2 vertebral body, new since ___, with mild retropulsion and mild spinal canal narrowing. Symptoms of radiation of pain from lateral left spine to lateral thigh worsening with leaning forward and positive straight leg raise consistent with classic sciatic pain. While no recent trauma, new degenerative changes apparent on outpatient MRI when compared to prior MRI ___ years ago. Chronic prednisone use puts patient's at increased risk for degenerative disease as evidence by patient's history of osteoporosis, spinal stenosis and chronic prednisone injections for patient's right hip place patient's at increased risk for spinal degenerative disease. No neurological deficits, urinary incontinence, or motor weakness and inconsistent sensory exam with ED. No evidence of discitis, osteomyelitis, epidural collection or paravertebral collection on total MRI spine. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old male with complex past medical history notable for hypertension, diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea (intermittently compliant with CPAP at home) atrial fibrillation on rivaroxiban, presented with traumatic left hallux blister and altered mental status, with full and benign work-up for altered mental status, lengthy hospital course complicated by severe delirium. Patient was significantly agitated on HD1 requiring multiple doses of IM haloperidol. Infection of his left hallux injury was ruled out by podiatry and vascular as below. There were no other possible sources of infections with negative blood/urine cultures and CXR, and patient manifested no GI or neurologic symptoms outside of delerium. TSH, B12, and RPR were all normal. After receiving multiple doses of haloperidol, lorazepam, and quetiapine for agitation. Patient was obtunded on evening on ___ and transferred to MICU. CT head was negative for acute pathology. Due to a report of twitching, two separate EEGs were performed, both showing diffuse slowing, but no evidence of seizure activity. Obtundation resolved when sedating medications were held. Neurology was consulted for continued mental status with unclear etiology. They recommended lumbar puncture which was negative for infection. Geriatrics was consulted to assist with delirium treatment. Restraints and tethers were minimized and eliminated. Home medications were adjusted to limit polypharmacy. His statin and ezetimibe were stopped. Allopurinol was dose reduced. Olanzapine was started and titrated to 5 mg as needed for agitation. Mr. ___ continued to yell out intermittently, become agitated, and refuse medications at times. However, as his course continued, he became more redirectable and required less frequent administration of olanzapine. He was most compliant and relaxed when his wife visited, so patient's presence was encouraged. Any other sedating medications were held. Vital sign checks were limited to encourage sleep/wake cycle. He was re-oriented by staff frequently. # Respiratory failure: MICU COURSE ___: Patient presented to MICU with hypercarbic respiratory failure. He was intubated on ___. He was extubated on ___. The patient was on low dose dopamine from ___ to maintain blood pressure. Head CT & MRI obtained without acute process. Mental status still confused at time of transfer to floor on ___, but patient was less agitated. ___ EEG no evidence of seizure. No antibiotics were given. His hypercarbic respiratory failure was beleived to be secondary to the addition of valproate to his medication regimen on top of chronic retention of CO2. # Left hallux injury with left foot pain: Patient was seen by vascular surgery in the ED who felt no intervention was needed. X-ray ruled out fracture and osteomyelitis. He was initially followed by podiatry, who unroofed his blister and provided wound care recommendations. Though patient was initially covered with vancomycin and piperacillin/tazobactam, which were discontinued on HD2 due to low suspicion for infection as above. Wound swab grew pan-sensitive Staph aureus though antibiotics were not restarted given absent signs of infection. Blood cultures were negative. The wound healed well. # Hip Pain: given the history of acute onset inability to ambulate and recent falls at home, as well as the exam findings of extreme pain with passive range of motion of the right hip, there was concern for occult fracture. Hip x-ray was negative for fracture. Hip CT was negative for fracture, but did show extensive osteoarthritis in hips and SI joint, and also showed a small amount of fluid in psoas consistent with musculoskeletal injury. Physical therapy worked with the patient throughout his hospitalization. # Right upper extremity deep venous thrombosis: patient had a PICC placed for blood draws during hospitalization. He was noted to have new right arm swelling on ___ and right upper extremity ultrasound showed DVT in the axillary vein, likely in setting of poor compliance with rivaroxaban. Patient was noted to have normal bowel movements. Patient was empirically started on famotidine and Maalox. His pain improved and his abdomen was benign by discharge. # Pseudomonas in urine culture: Initially treated with cefepime, but primary team ultimately felt Pseudomonas was a contaminant from the condom catheter it was collected from. Cefepime was stopped and infectious signs/symptoms did not arise. Condom catheter was removed to avoid tethering. # Hypertension: Patient initially became hypertensive after refusing POs. He was maintained on IV hydralazine when refusing PO valsartan with acceptable pressure control. Toward the end of his hospitalization, he was taking his medications more regularly and SBPs were in the 150s-160s range. # Acute on chronic kidney disease: creatinine at recent baseline 1.0-1.2 on admission. It slightly uptrended to 1.3 on admission to the MICU, with hypernatremia secondary to lack of PO intake while obtunded. Furosemide was held. IVF were given and electrolytes normalized. Furosemide was restarted given evidence of accumulation of edema. # Pulmonary edema: CXR demonstrated mild-moderate pulmonary edema on admission of unclear acuity. He was continued on his home furosemide initially, but this was later stopped due to dehydration. He was given a low-salt diet. Furosemide was restarted near the end of his hospitlazation. # Hypernatremia: At times during his hospital stay, the patient was hypernatremic with a max of 148. Patient was rate controlled without beta blockade, and has a history of bradycardia with nodal agents. # Obstructive sleep apnea: Patient refused CPAP overnight for much of his admission, though it was offered. He is noncompliant with CPAP at home, per wife. # Pulmonary hypertension: Stable respiratory status as above. # Gout: Allopurinol was dose reduced at the recommendation of geriatrics to avoid medication side effects. # Hyperlipidemia: Atorvastatin and ezetimibe were discontinued at the recommendation of geriatrics to avoid polypharmacy and medication side effects. # Non-insulin dependent diabetes mellitus: Last HbA1C 6.1, not on POs pre-admission. text: Brief Hospital Course: BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE ===================== patient. ___ is a ___ patient with h/o iron deficiency anemia and past opioid abuse and regular alcohol use, now on suboxone, who presented to the ED with first-time seizure after ___ days of nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, with last alcoholic drink >24 hours prior to admission. patient was admitted to the ICU for concern regarding withdrawal seizures. patient did not experience any epileptic events, and was transferred to the medical floor. ACTIVE ISSUES ============= # Seizure: This was patient's first convulsive episode and was witnessed by patient's husband. On admission, highest on differential was alcohol withdrawal, in the setting of poor PO intake (due to gastroenteritis) precipitating a seizure. Pro-dromal vision changes were likely related to pre-seizure aura. patient denied high fever, cough, or urinary symptoms suggestive of non-GI infectious seizure etiology. Urine and serum tox screens were negative. patient received benzos for presumed alcohol withdrawal in the ED. On admission to ICU, patient's CIWA was tapered and discontinuedl. patient was restarted on patient's home clonazepam with holding parameters and transferred to the medical floor. On the floor, patient denied a significant alcohol history and states patient drinks approximately ___ times week, ___ drinks at a time (corroborated with husband). As it was not entirely clear that this seizure was related to alcohol withdrawal, MRI and EEG were ordered to rule out other causes of patient's seizure such as structural brain abnormality. patient was unable to fully tolerate a ___ MRI but the images that were able to be obtained showed no mass lesion although did show some cerebellar irregularity that could suggest Chiari malformation. EEG preliminary showed some slowing consistent with mild encephalopathy but no seizure activity. patient was discharged home feeling at patient's baseline and recommended to follow-up with neurology urgent care in the next several days. patient was advised not to drive for at least 6 months. text: Brief Hospital Course: Patient is ___ yo F with aortic stenosis (0.8cm2 on ___, recurrent UTIs and T2DM who presented after an episode of anxiety and dyspnea most consistent with pulmonary edema and dysuria. . #Dyspnea/Aortic stenosis with pulmonary edema: Patient's chest x-ray demonstrated increased haziness consistent with mild pulmonary edema. summary: You were admitted for shortness of breath. We evaluated your heart and lungs extensively with a CT scan of your chest and an ultrasound of your heart, which did not show an obvious cause of your breathing difficulty. We think your breathing difficulty may be due to extreme fatigue related to excessive prednisone causing very high blood sugars. Although we think your blood sugars will probably come down as your steroid dose decreases, based on our blood work, your sugars have been high for some time.

text: Brief Hospital Course: Summary: ___ YO F w/ longstanding Crohn's disease on Imuran, w/ fevers and respiratory distress x 2weeks, fulminant liver failure, influenza A and mycoplasma IgM +. Cytomegalovirus hepatitis: While in the MICU, the patient developed fulminant hepatic failure and was subsequently transferred to the surgical ICU and placed on the transplant list. The patient was noted to be briefly encephalopathic and started on lactulose. On biopsy, the patient was confirmed to have a CMV hepatitis and started on gancyclovir. Tests for hepatitis A/B/E, ___, HSV, ferritin, ceruloplasmin, adenovirus, varicella were within normal limits. The anti-smooth muscle antibody was high. The patient was placed on Ursodiol for hyperbilirubinemia. patient's INR was elevated, so patient was given vitamin K. On the gancyclovir treatment, the patient's liver enzymes steadily improved, however, they started to rise towards the end of patient's admission. There was concern that the gancyclovir was possibly hepatotoxic and patient was therefore changed to valgancyclovir for an induction period of one week post-discharge followed by a maintenence period. On the valgancyclovir, patient's liver enzymes improved and will be followed as an outpatient. Since patient had liver damage, patient's home wellbutrin and testosterone will be held on dischare until patient's followup GI appointment. Crohn's disease: The patient has a history of Crohn's disease and had known fistulas in the terminal ileum. patient's Imuran was stopped, since its use predisposed patient's to CMV infection. The patient continued to have abdominal pain with diarrhea. The abdominal pain was controlled with dilaudid. There was concern that patient's diarrhea was related to CMV colitis, however a simoidoscopy with biopsy showed no concerning infection. A small bowel followthrough was done to see if patient's Crohn's was flaring. The followthrough was normal and showed known fistulas. The patient continued treatment with mesalamine and was not discharged on an immunomodulator. patient will have outpatient followup to decide further treatment. Respiratory distress: The patient was transferred with respiratory distress. patient was found to have bilateral pleural effusions and infiltrates. patient was influenza A positive (records not available) and finished a course of Tamiflu. patient was also found to have Mycoplasma IgM, however, infectious disease thought it might have been a false positive. Despite ID concerns, the patient was given a 5 day course of azithromycin. patient needed to be intubated for patient's respiratory distress and had an uncomplicated extubation. Normocytic anemia: The patient developed a normocytic anemia and was found to have guiaic positive stool. patient was transfused 4 units of blood. There was concern for a transfusion related reaction (fever), so the patient was given leuko-reduced transfusions. A pathology consult thought a transfusion reaction was unlikely saying "although the patient experienced oxygen desaturation, had a low arterial PO2, and developed crackles at the time of the transfusion, it is difficult to separate these from the findings from the symptoms patient is experiencing due to patient's underlying condition. The lack of diffuse infiltrates on CXR and the lack of hypotension temporally associated with the transfusion make transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI) unlikely. In addition, an anaphylactic reaction is unlikely because patient did not experience other systemic manifestations of such a reaction, such as erythema, urticaria, hypotension, flushing, or GI symptoms. It was unclear whether bronchospasm was directly associated with the transfusion. However, it is known that bronchospasm was suspected many hours after the transfusion, making it more likely that it was due to patient's underlying lung infection than the transfusion. Finally, as the patient has been experiencing fevers throughout patient's hospitalization, and given that leukoreduction significantly decreases the incidence of febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reactions, the patient's fever is most likely due to patient's underlying illness and not the transfusion." Upon transfer to the medical floors, the patient had a stable hematocrit without signs of bleeding. Papilledema: The patient developed papilledema in the setting of fulminant liver failure and intubation. Neurology evaluated the patient and thought "The patient is at risk for cerebral edema due to liver failure, poor synthetic function, and difficulty holding fluid in the vascular space. patient is hypocoagulable and at risk for bleeeding due to patient's poor synthetic function; however, patient is simultaneously hypercoagulable and at increased risk for thrombosis due to patient's history of Crohn's disease and prior spontaneous abortion. patient is also at risk for meningitis and encephalitis due to patient's prior infection and unknown cause of patient's liver failure." text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ with ETOH cirrhosis, h/o MCA stroke with residual right-sided deficits, who p/w worsening mental status and jaundice, found to be severly anemic secondary to spontaneous RP bleed secondary to consumptive coagulopathy. Treated with blood product support as well as Amicar IV then PO for fibrinolysis stabilization. Acute liver failure thought to be secondary to alcoholic hepatitis and patient was felt not to be a transplant candidate. Hospital course also complicated by ___ requiring temporary dialysis (resolved) and respiratory failure requiring temporary intubation (resolved). The patient was in the ICU twice, once for respiratory and kidney failure and once for aminocaproic acid (amicar) initiation. . # Hypotension/Hemorrhage/Coagulopathy: The patient was admitted from liver clinic to the ED with altered mental status where patient was found to be severly anemic. Admitted to the MICU where CT scans revealed a spontaneous abdominal bleed, RP bleed, and right thigh bleed. Unclear precipitant, though patient's husband did report that the patient fell the day prior to admission. patient required frequent blood transfusions (44 PRBC, ___ FFP, 19 platelet, 22 cryo through hospitalization) which was attributed to a consumptive coagulopathy as well as suspected hemolysis from liver disease. The patient was eventually transferred to the floor, however continued to bleed and required frequent transfusions. patient did not respond to steroids for possible hemolytic anemia. Rheumatologic testing did not return positive. A workup of patient's hematologic problems demonstrated low fibrinogen but normal factor VIII levels, which showed that the patient was not in disseminated intravascular coagulation. A repeat CT scan demonstrated enlarging bleeds but no evidence of extravasation that would have been amenable to interventional radiologic embolization. Hematology recommended starting Amicar for stabilization of fibrinolysis, for which patient was transferred back to the MICU. patient's Hct stabilized and patient no longer required daily transfusions and was transferred back to the floor. patient was continued on PO amicar with much more stable Hcts. patient was transfused with PRBCs to keep patient's Hct greater than 21 and platelets greater than 50 during active bleeding. patient received cryoprecipitate with goal of keeping patient's fibrinogen greater than 100. # Decompensated Cirrhosis/alcoholic hepatitis: Most likely secondary to EtOH. Hepatitis B and C serologies negative. EBV/CMV IgG positive but IgM nebative. Per hepatology, the patient is not a transplant candidate considering patient's history of CVA, alcohol abuse, and coagulopathy. patient was treated with lactulose and rifaximin and on discharge, was mildly encephalopathic with intermittent confusion. patient did respond well to extra lactulose when patient was encephalopathic. patient is grossly fluid overloaded peripherally for which patient is getting IV lasix, with good reponse. # Hypercalcemia: Unclear etiology, thought to be secondary to prolonged immobilization and increased bony resorption. PTH low normal, though would expect PTH to be undetectable given persistently elevated Ca levels, and therefore endocrinology believed that there was some degree of hyperparathyrodism. SPEP/UPEP negative. patient had no overt symptoms of hypercalcemia, and no EKG changes. Per Endocrine, patient was treated with fluids initially, then diuresis and calcitonin. patient was also loaded with vitamin D in preparation for IV bisphosphonate therapy as IV bisphosphanates can precipiatate hypocalcemia ___ days after initiation without adequate vitamin D, however as patient's calcium is decreasing, may not need IV bisphosphonate. While at the long-term acute care rehab, patient will continue to need frequent monitoring of patient's calcium. patient was discharged on subcutaneous calcitonin twice daily, which may be stopped if patient's calcium returns to normal or worsens despite its continued administration, as it may have ceased being effective. # Respiratory Failure: Sputum culture positive for Klebsiella pneumonia. Patient was treated with a course of vanc/zosyn/cipro for HCAP, however repeat sputum cultures continued to be positive for Klebsiella, so the patient was started on vancomycin/cefepime as well as micafungin for empiric fungal coverage. Respiratory failure was also thought to be due to pulmonary edema in the setting of aggressive fluid resuscitation (32L positive in the ICU), however this improved with diuresis and fluid removal with CVVH. patient was briefly extubated on ___, however was reintubated on ___ for worsening respiratory distress. patient was subsequently extubated a few days later without incident. # ___: Patient with worsening renal function due to ATN from poor perfusion in the setting of hypotension. A temporary HD line was placed and the patient was started on CVVH with normalization of patient's renal function. patient's HD line was pulled on ___, however patient was again noted to have worsening renal function with Cr climbing to about 2.0 prior to returning to baseline by the time of callout. patient's creatinine remained stable once on the floor, the patient was urinating well with diuretics. At time of discharge, it had returned to baseline. # Nutrition: The patient was initally on TPN which was then transitioned to tube feeds once a Dobhoff was placed in post-pyloric position. Dobhoff was repeatedly pulled out by patient in ICU or otherwise unable to be placed post-pyloric. Poor PO intake otherwise. Nutrition consult recommended encouraging PO, boost glucose control, MV, vitamin C, zinc supplement. Once patient's mental status improved, a post-pyloric Dobhoff tube was placed and bridled and the patient was continued on tube feeds with PO supplementation (nectar thickened liquids with soft diet with 1:1 supervision while feeding). # Hypothyroidism: Patient was on levothyroxine while taking Pos, however this was changed to IV formulation when tube feeds were intitiated over fears of decreased absorption during tube feeds. At discharge, patient was on 100mcg of IV levothyroxine daily and will need thyroid function tests repeated ___ year post discharge. # Hypernatremia: Patient experienced intermittent hypernatremia requiring free water replacement with tube feed flushes as well as D5W boluses. Sodium was stable on the floor once tolerating POs along with tube feeds. # Diabetes - Sugars controlled on lantus and sliding scale. #. Goals of Care Patient was seen by Palliative Care in the MICU ___ who followed to give family support because patient is not a tranpslant candidate. The patient's husband ___ is very involved and understanding of the issues. The patient was made DNR but ok to reintubate. Multiple family meetings were held given the patient's advanced illness, and it was made clear that should the patient have another complication of patient's illness, patient's prognosis would be extremely poor and a decision on whether to continue further invasive interventions would have to be made. In the case of a decompensation, the patient may always return to ___ for more aggressive care; however, if the goals of care switched to comfort then hospice involvement would be most appropriate. Transitional Issues - daily monitoring of Hct, chem 10, fibrinogen - Transfuse for Hct > 21, platelets > 10, cryo for fibrinogen < 100 - follow up appointments made with Hematology, Hepatology, Endocrinology. - If tube feeds held, then patient's lantus should be stopped - Please check vitamin D levels in 3 weeks - Please check thyroid function tests in 1 week's time.

You were started on lovenox, an anticoagulant to treat this clot.
original_text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ woman with stage IIB adenocarcinoma of the head of the pancreas, status post Whipple on ___, s/p vaccine adjuvant therapy on trial ___ (now off trial), gemcitabine ___, recent cholangitis and local recurrence who presents with nausea and vomiting. Brief review of history to present admission: Of note, she was admitted to ___ from ___ for ascites, paracentesis performed w/ 1.6L of chylous fluid removed with improvement in her abdominal discomfort; treated for C. diff colitis with Vancomycin. She was admitted again ___ for fever and dyspnea, presumably from restrictive ventilatory defect secondary to ascites, started on diuretics, with no infectious source found. This admission she presented w/ nausea and nonbloody vomiting X 2 days, found to be febrile to 100.9 in ED. Started on cefepime and vancomycin. Blood and urine cxs negative, CXR showed likely atelectasis. As pt was not neutropenic, w/ no localizing infection, abx discontinued. Echo was performed as pt had been persistently tachycardic and dyspneic, negative for effusion, EF>55%. Pt continued to spike cyclic low-grade fevers (average 100.5). Paracentesis revealed 1078 WBC, 79% polys, diagnostic of SBP; gram stain neg w/ cytology neg for malignant cells. Pt started on ceftriaxone 2 mg IV Q24, albumin on days 1 and 3. Diuretics held temporarily, but restarted within 72 hours per hepatology recs. SAAG still >1.1 suggestive of portal hypertension. RUQ US w/ doppler revealed thrombosis in central, R and L hepatic portal vein, pt started on lovenox 70 mg BID. CT scan performed which again revealed soft tissue mass encasing the celiac artery, SMA, SMV and compressing the main portal vein, extending into the retroperitoneum, concerning for disease recurrence, also enlarging L pleural effusion. On HD 10, pt had been afebrile for >48 hours and was tolerating lovenox well; diarrhea had also decreased significantly. She was discharged in stable condition to follow up with her outpatient oncologist and to finish out a course of PO vancomycin for C. diff. colitis. Transitional issues: 1. Last day of ceftriaxone ___, PO vancomycin to be extended 2 weeks beyond this date; final day of vanc ___. However, this is empiric -- IDSA guidelines give no specific recommendation regarding time course for C. diff treatment beyond discontinuation of other antibiotic therapy (practice is ___ weeks). 2. Results of CT scan can be followed up as outpt, correlated w/ clinical picture to evaluate for recurrence of disease.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ASSESSMENT & PLAN: ___ h/o chronic back pain and anxiety presenting with acute pancreatitis. # Acute pancreatitis: ___ was admitted with epigastric pain. patient was found to have lipase elevation, fat stranding with pancreatic edema on abc CT consistent with acute pancreatitis. patient was treated with NPO, IV fluids, and IV dilaudid (0.5-1 mg Q4h) and antiemetics. Over time, patient was able to advance patient's diet and tolerate a regular diet on the day of discharge. patient was also able to rely on oxycodone alone for control of pain. The cause of the acute pancreatitis is unclear. patient has no significant alcohol use or gallstones on MRCP or CT scan. Ca, trig, IgG4 werer normal here. There was no FH of CF. MRCP did not showed any CBD stones or ampullary stenosis. MRCP, however, did reveal extensive pancreatitis with peripheral foci of necrosis. There was no significant fever or persistent leukocytosis to warrant abx use. To avoid the possibility of medication assocated pancreatitis, patient was advised to discontinue Cymbalta and neurontin (both of which caused significant side effects). For further workup, a CFTR gene may be checked as an outpt to r/o CF gene as etiology. Sphincter of Oddi dysfunction also remains in the differential. # UTI: patient. ___ had reports of dysuria, urinary frequency. patient received 3 day course of bactrim DS BID although urine cxs ultimately returned negative. # Constipation: e/o constipation on CT scan - aggressive bowel regimen # Chronic low back pain: - continue home methadone # Anxiety: - continue home alprazolam # Home safety concerns: ___ initial RN report, some concern regarding safety at home, but no evidence of danger. patient described merely, very distant, poor relationship with father - who reportedly feels patient is making up these pain symptoms. No evidence of physical abuse, however. ___ provided housing resources for patient. ***** OTHER **** #FEN: NPO, maintenance IVF, replete electrolytes prn # ACCESS: very difficult access. ___ need to order PICC line if additional procedure (e.g. ERCP is planned). #PPX: home PPI, bowel regimen prn, heparin sq #Code: confirmed full #Communication: ___ (mother) ___ ___ ___: ___ #CODE STATUS: [X]full code []DNR/DNI .
summary: ___. As you know, you were admitted with abdominal pain and was found to have significant acute pancreatitis. You were placed on intravenous fluids along with pain medications and antinausea medications. You had several tests - including CT scan and MRI which both showed significant pancreatitis, but no clear cause for it. After a number of blood tests, the cause of your pancreatitis is unclear. The one possibility is medications, and we recommend holding from taking the neurontin and Cymbalta. Your primary care doctor may also consider checking the gene for cystic fibrosis (although unlikely). Over time, you were able to tolerate a regular diet and use only oral medications for pain.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old patient with history of hypothyroidism, atrial fibrillation, anemia, who has baseline mild confusion and tangential thoughts, presents with worsening lethargy over the past few weeks (possibly contributing to fall), found to have hyponatremia. ACTIVE ISSUES ------------- # Hyponatremia: patient has had episodes of hyponatremia in past down to 125 noted on outpatient labs, thought to be secondary to diuretic use, most recently in ___, and was instructed to drink Gatorade, but never had repeat follow up labs to reassess. On initial exam, patient appeared slightly volume overloaded with some peripheral edema, crackles on lung exam. Chest X-ray had evidence of pleural effusions bilaterally R>L as well as interstitial edema. patient's thiazide diuretic was held on admission for concern that this was contributing to patient's hyponatremia. patient was bolused furosemide 20 mg IV to try to improve volume status and patient was fluid restricted to 1500 mL daily. patient's sodium levels were trended closely. A TTE was performed which showed preserved ejection fraction, normal biventricular cavity sizes, preserved regional and global biventricular function. With fluid restriction and the furosemide bolus, patient's sodium improved from 117 to 131. patient will follow up with patient's primary care doctor, and have patient's sodium rechecked at that time. patient will continue to observe a 1.5 liter fluid restriction at home. patient's triamterene/HCTZ was discontinued at the time of discharge, as it likely contributed to patient's hyponatremia. A decision should be made with the patient's PCP whether patient requires this medication going forward. Patient's blood pressure was well controlled off this medication over the course of patient's stay. patient may need another medication for patient's lower extremity edema, to be determined by patient's PCP. # Urinary tract infection: Patient with urinalysis in the ED showing large leuks, 46 WBC, few bacteria, concerning for UTI. patient was asymptomatic but started on ceftriaxone in the ED. This was continued for a three day course of ceftriaxone for uncomplicated UTI. Urine culture grew mixed bacterial flora. # Falls: patient's fall was attributed to lethargy, likely from patient's hyponatremia. patient's mental status improved over the course of patient's hospitalization. Physical therapy evaluated the patient and cleared patient's for home discharge with physical therapy. CHRONIC ISSUES -------------- # Anemia: patient has known history of anemia, and has deferred work-up as an outpatient, but has gotten outpatient blood transfusions intermittently. Baseline hemoglobin is ___. patient's last colonoscopy was in ___ (1 polyp, diverticulosis, hemorrhoids). Admission hemoglobin was slightly below baseline ~7, and patient was transfused 1 unit pRBCs and patient's hematocrit responded appropriately. As an outpatient, patient had deferred iron supplementation as it resulted in constipation. patient tries to supplement diet with iron rich foods. Outpatient labs were consistent with iron deficiency anemia. Congenital abnormalities are also possible given ___ ancestry and low MCV. # Atrial fibrillation: known history, previously on warfarin and digoxin, but both discontinued secondary to GI bleeding and bradycardia. patient was continued on aspirin 81 mg for anticoagulation. patient was monitored on telemetry and rate was well controlled throughout admission. Patient remained asymptomatic. # Hypothyroidism: patient has known history and recently had levothyroxine uptitrated to 100 mcg daily which patient continued this admission. Repeat TSH was within normal limits. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES ------------------- # Follow-up: patient will follow up with patient's PCP after discharge, upon which patient's sodium should be rechecked. patient's triamterene/HCTZ was discontinued. patient has pending blood cultures at the time of discharge which will need to be followed up. The patient was intermittently hypoxic while sleeping while admitted. When asked, the patient felt that patient would not want nighttime oxygen or formal sleep study. This should be readdressed as an outpatient. # Code status: full code # Contact: daughter ___ ___ ___ on Admission: The Preadmission Medication list is accurate and complete. 1. Levothyroxine Sodium 100 mcg PO DAILY 2. Triamterene-Hydrochlorothiazide (37.5/25) 1 CAP PO DAILY 3. Aspirin 81 mg PO DAILY 4. Feosol Bifera (iron polysac-iron heme polypep) 28 mg oral daily
summary: You came for further evaluation of falls, as well as a low sodium level. While here, your sodium level was treated with restriction of fluid, and promptly improved. It is possible that this low sodium level is from one of your medications, triamterene/HCTZ, and this should be stopped until further notice. Physical therapy evaluated you and recommends continued physical therapy at home.

text: Brief Hospital Course: PATIENT ___ year old patient hx of COPD, dCHF, OSA, obesity hypoventilation syndrome coming in with hypoxia, AMS, ___, and UTI. patient was admitted to the ICU secondary to patient's hypotension (systolic 90's), hypoxia (sat 70's on RA) and AMS. ACUTE ISSUES # HYPOXIA: Patient was noted to not be on home 2 L NC on admission to hospital, and subseuqently when placed on 2 L NC in ICU quickly hit goal saturation > 88 %. # AMS: On initial presentation, it was noted patient's AMS was likely multifactorial (hypoxia with concomitant UTI, with delerium superimposed on baseline dementia). patient was given haldol sparingly for episodes of acute agitation, was treated for UTI as below and was frequetnly reoriented to self and place. Benzodiazpeines were avoided. Narcotics were not restarted until patient transferred to floor and was fully oriented and returned to baseline mental status. # UTI: For patient's UTI, patient has history of multiple ESBL urinary tract infections and presented with positive UA on admission. patient was started on empiric meropenem, and blood and urine cultures were pending at time of transition to floor. Urine cultures grew ESBL E. coli, so continued on meropenam while in house. PICC line placed at discharge and patient sent out to complete a total of two week antibiotic therapy with ertapenam. # ___: For patient ___, patient had a Cr of 3.9 on admission with baseline 0.9-1.1. patient's FeUrea 5.3% in house was suggestive of pre-renal etiology. Patient's UOP was monitored in the ICU. Renal U/S sound was completed when patient transferred to the floor - demonstrated no signs of hydronephrosis or sludging as a causal factor. Serum creatinine 1.0 at time of discharge. # dCHF: For patient's Acute exacerbation of dCHF, Pt had pulmonary edema on CXR on admission, with BNP at 981 ( was 84 3 months prior), elevated JVP and bilateral ___ edema. EKG was without obvious ischemic changes. Cardiac enzymes were trended in house and patient was set for a goal of -1 L per day with IV lasix boluses, which patient achieved. patient's symptoms and mental status improved with diuresis. patient was discharged to the floor on ___ with plan to continue gentle diuresis, follow-up on urine and blood cultures and narrow antibiotics appropriately, and to continue monitoring of patient's respiratory function which had much improved. On the floor was converted to home torsemide and patient continued to have approprite diuresis. Discharged home without alteration in home dose of diuretics. Discharge Weight: 133.4 kg CHRONIC ISSUES: # Bradycardia: Patient had intermittent episodes of bradycardia while sleeping, likely due to OSA. HD stable and assymptomatic. No intervention # COPD: Initially treated as COPD flare in ED, but treatment discontinued once admitted. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ y/o F with severe dementia, chronic constipation, anal stricture ___ hemorrhoidectomy who p/w leukocytosis, colonic distension, constipation, and new atrial fibrillation with RVR. . # Colonic distension, constipation: Pt presented from nursing home with constipation and colonic distention. CT abdomen demonstrated "diffusely dilated large bowel with a focally narrowed segment in the sigmoid colon, which could either be a stricture or normal peristalsis; Large amount of stool in the rectal vault." Clinically pt appeared distended but had bowel sounds. Pt was found to have a leukocytosis, and given concern for infection of possibly C. diff vs. diverticulitis, pt was started on Ciprofloxacin and Flagyl empirically. A lactate level was normal, which was reassuring for not having ischemic bowel. The patient was evaluated by surgery, who recommended disimpaction. However, patient's HCP did not want disimpaction due to patient's agitation and concern that patient may not tolerate it. patient was managed conservatively with decompression with NGT. However, pt pulled the tube out twice, and after the second time it was pulled out we were unable to replace given pt's confusion. Replacing NGT was not done, given that patient's dilation seemed to be mostly large bowel rather than small bowel. patient was made NPO and IVF were started. Serial abdominal examinations were performed and patient was started on enemas. A rectal exam on hospital day 1 revealed no stool in the vault or masses and guaiac was negative. On hospital day 2, patient had increased distention and there was concern for developing obstruction. Surgery was again consulted in addition to GI for evaluation of possible colonic decompression. However, pt had a large BM later that morning, and colonic decompression was not needed. We spoke with the HCP, whose main concern was pt's agitation and whether patient could tolerate procedures. patient was willing for pt to be disimpacted as long as pt could tolerate and nursing could manage any agitation. Pt was seen by surgery who disimpacted the pt. Pt was then passing gas. On hospital day 3, pt had less distention and passed another large bowel movement after a tap water enema. patient was advanced to full liquids, which patient tolerated well. On hospital day 3, Cipro and Flagyl were discontinued given resolution of leukocytosis and pt remaining afebrile. C. diff and stool Cx had not been sent. . GI recommended colonoscopy vs. gastrograff enema for further evaluation of colonic distention. However, per discussion with HCP and the primary team, it was decided that pt would not tolerate either procedure well and given that patient was now having BM's, conservative tx with enemas and starting GoLytely was chosen. However, given concern for sigmoid stricture on initial CT scan, a repeat CT abd/pelvis was done, which showed again narrowing of the sigmoid segment suggestive of incidental peristalsis versus stricture. It was decided amongst the team, and per the HCP wishes, that pt would not have a colonoscopy at this time as should would likely not tolerate it well. This could be done in the future if patient acutely worsened or it was indicated. . On the day of discharge, pt's distention had decreased, patient was passing gas, having large BM's, and tolerating a regular soft diet. A TSH level was sent, which was normal at 2.8. . patient was discharged with the plan to continue Dulcolax, Milk of Magnesia, and fleet enemas as needed for constipation. . # Leukocytosis: As discussed above, pt had leukocytosis on original presentation. patient was empirically started on Cipro and Flagyl given concern for C. diff vs. diverticulitis, though not suggested by CT scan. Both abx were discontinued on hospital day 3 given clinical improvement, pt being afebrile and resolved leukocytosis. A urine Cx was negative. . # Atrial fibrillation with RVR: Pt was agitated on admission and dehydrated, and found to have a. fib with RVR on the morning of admission. The etiology was unclear, and given new leukocytosis and new early systolic murmur there was concern for endocarditis, vs. mitral regurgitation though no evidence of pulmonary edema, vs. flow murmur secondary to anemia. patient's hemodynamic stability was reassuring. patient was placed on telemetry. Pt had another episode later that morning of HD1 of Afib with RVR that was treated with Lopressor and Diltiazem. Pt was found to paroxysmal atrial fibrillation of unclear etiology. A TTE was attempted on ___ however, the pt was combative and unable to tolerate the procedure. Given patient's paroxysmal atrial fibrillation patient was started on Metoprolol XL 12.5mg daily. patient was also started on ASA 325mg po daily given CHADS score of 2. . On the day of discharge pt was in sinus rhythm with no evidence of hemodynamic compromise. patient's heart rate ranged from 70-80, and was to continue metoprolol on discharge. A TTE could be done as an outpatient if clinically indicated and pt able to tolerate the procedure. . # Dementia: Pt was agitated on the day of admission. patient has chronic problems with agitation and behavior issues that are better controlled with olanzipine and ativan per patient's HCP. However, given patient's lethargy on original presentation, patient's psychiatry medications were held. patient was placed on delirium precautions. Pt had intermittent agitation during this admission, but it improved on hospital day 2. Per patient's HCP who was present each day, pt was at patient's baseline. patient was discharged on patient's prior psychiatric medications per management of the nursing home. . # Iron deficiency Anemia: Pt was found to have a decreased hematocrit of 33 down from 41 on admission. patient was dehydrated on original presentation and thought to be hemoconcentrated. patient's hematocrit remained stable during the admission, with no signs or symptoms of bleeding. A guaiac was negative. patient was on telemetry. patient was given IVF. Iron studies demonstrated iron deficiency anemia; however, iron replacement was not started given patient's recent constipation. Per patient's HCP, further workup for likely chronic iron deficiency anemia such as colonoscopy was not pursued at this time given pt was not likely to tolerate it.

The tube was later removed. You were given enemas, which helped produce bowel movements. You were then able to take food by mouth and having bowel movements. You were also found to have an abnormal heart rhythm, which we treated with a medication to slow the heart rate. This improved after the medication. You were restarted on Lisinopril prior to discharge given improved blood pressures. You were started on a new blood pressure medication, Metoprolol, and Aspirin, for your heart arrhythmia. You psychiatric medications were held during this admission because you were sleepy and lethargic.

Biliary labs vascillated during the hospitalization and it was unclear what the precipitant of the elevation was, apart for progression of known metastatic cancer. G-J tube leakage - Initially there was concern that leakage around the patient's jtube was related to ascites fluid, but per ___ the pt's tube site represents a mature tract, so less likely that this fluid was ascitic fluid, and more likely it was fluid from the G/J connection. ___ was consulted from ED and planned to tack down entry site with additional suture, but overnight the patient's tube was somehow removed/fell out/was pulled out. This did not improve the leakage from the tube site. ___ felt that this leakage was probably a result of poor wound healing and nutritional status. Octreotide was trialed to see if this improved the leakage, but there was no improvement with this either. Gastric Ca - off therapy since ___ due to poor performance status and multiple complications as above. patient is being sent home with hospice services. ___ edema - Likely due to hypoalbuminemia. Lower extremity dopplers were negative for DVT. PAIN: On patient ___ 30mg PO BID + PO dil 8mg q 4. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ patient with history notable for HTN, hypothyroidism, DMII, HLD, and depression transferred from ___ after presenting with unresponsiveness and right gaze preference initially concerning for acute stroke. Mental status improved following admission, with CT and MR brain imaging revealing no evidence of underlying acute ischemia or hemorrhage. CT perfusion imaging notable for relative decrease in right-sided perfusion, which, along with right gaze preference and resolution of symptoms, suggest left-sided seizure. EEG monitoring did not demonstrate further concerning epileptiform discharges or seizures during the admission. Initial laboratory evaluation notable for hypoglycemia, likely precipitating the initial seizure event. Laboratory testing consistent with SIADH, with CT chest not demonstrating evidence of underlying malignancy. Review of medications notable for recent initiation of sertraline; per Nephrology evaluation, SSRIs have been associated with SIADH. Sertraline discontinued, and sodium corrected initially with hypertonic saline and subsequently with free water restriction. Sodium levels normalized and mental status improved prior to discharge. Of incidental note, TTE obtained for evaluation of new dyspnea and exercise intolerance prior to admission demonstrated normal systolic and likely normal age-adjusted diastolic function. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES 1. Ambulatory sodium check following discharge to ensure resolution of hyponatremia. 2. Avoidance of further trials of SSRIs. 3. If continued somnolence after discharge, please contact Dr. ___ for recommendations regarding potential weaning of levetiracetam.
summary: You were transferred to ___ from ___ after being found unresponsive. Instead, you were found to have very low sodium levels at the time of your transfer, which may have been caused by one of your recent medications (sertraline); these low sodium levels likely led to a seizure that caused your symptoms. During your stay, you were also seen by the Nephrology service, who also felt that your low sodium was likely related to your medications; you were treated with concentrated saline solution and restriction of your free water intake, after which your sodium levels improved. You did not have further seizures during your stay. You should avoid taking sertraline as a result of your reaction to this medication.

After patient was extubated, patient had another endoscopic exam and was noted to have some vocal cord dysfunction, improved with relaxation techniques and no obvious epiglottitis. Patient was transferred to the floor on ___ and continued to do well. Still had a sore throat, but no wheezing or shortness of breath, no dysphagia. ENT also recommended increasing omprazole to 40 mg daily. Have scheduled outpt ENT follow-up . # PEA cardiac arrest- this occured while in ICU, patients pulse returned after 1 minute or so of chest compressions. Etiology was felt to be possibly secondary to biting the tube versus related to propofol. summary: You were admitted to the hospital because your bile duct became obstructed by colon cancer. We initially performed an ERCP, which was unsuccessful, so you then underwent placement of three percutaneous biliary drains. This relieved the obstruction in your bile ducts. You will go home with the drains capped and need to return for further procedures by our interventional radiology team in two weeks. Our GI specialist had place a pancreatic stent and later removed it. You were also treated with antibiotics for a possible bile duct infection.

summary: You were admitted for a bleed from the colon in the setting of a low blood pressure. You were admitted to the ICU because of an inability to maintain your blood pressure due to an infection, which caused damage to several organs including your kidneys. Because of this injury, you were started on dialysis. You were intubated because you were not breathing adequately. You were treated with a complete course of antibiotics for possible infection. However, your low blood pressure might have also been related to blood loss from the colon. Once stable and coming out of the ICU, the cause of your bleed in the colon was investigated. You had a colonoscopy, which showed inflammation in the colon, which is likely where the bleeding occurred. However, through your hospital course, the blood in your stools decreased and you began to have formed stools without blood as the inflammation likely resolved. During your course, you were also seen by psychiatry who made recommendations regarding your care. Unfortunately, your hospital stay was also complicated by injury to the brain that included bleeding in brain. This bleeding led to significant agitation as well as seizures. You were transferred back to the ICU for careful monitoring and an anti-seizure medicine was started. After your condition stabalized, you were tranferred to the Neurology-Stroke Service. By the time of discharge your neurologic status had improved significnatly. In addition, your liver appeared to have recovered and your kidneys began making urine so you no longer require dialysis.

The patient was continued on his IV Vanc and Cipro which were started overnight and because of his deteriorating status, Flagyl was also added for anaerobic coverage. In the MICU, his antibiotics were changed to vancomycin and meropenem for broader coverage. Noncontrast CT scan negative for necrotizing fasciitis and the source of his infection was felt to be due to the left leg cellulitis; later MRI once the patient was transferred back to the medicine service showed evidence of underlying osteomyelitis. He did not have other localizing symptoms of an infection and urinalysis was negative. He initially required norepinephrine for about 20 hours to maintain his systolic blood pressure greater than 80, but was able to be weaned off this in the context of aggressive fluid rescucitation. On transfer back to the Medicine floor, the patient's wound swab was found to be MSSA and antibiotics were switched to Nafcillin. MRI showed evidence of osteomyelitis in the ___ toe of left foot. # osteomyelitis with cellulitis: The patient was found to have cellulitis with plain films concerning for osteo. The patient was seen by podiatry who did bedside incisional drain while in the ED. Cultures grew out MSSA and the patient was started on IV Nafcillin. MRI was done which showed osteomyelitis. He ultimately needed to have PICC placed and continue a prolonged course of IV antibiotic treatment of nafcillin (at minimum 6 weeks). He will be seen by ID in as an outpatient to determine the length of his IV treatment and transition to oral antibiotics. # chronic venous stasis: patient has chronic venous stasis. Dermatology was consult and they felt that his foot exam was consitent with elephantiasis verrucosa nostra. They took a skin biopsy of his right shin, results pending. Started on Bactroban for oozing PRN. # seborrheic dermatitis: Started on ketoconazole BID. # superficial thrombophlebitis: Pt had acute swelling and erythema of left upper extremity, ultrasound showed clot in basilar vein. Pt treated with warm compress and elevation, erythema and swelling resolved on discharge. # acute renal failure: On admission labs, the patient was found to have creat of 1.1 which on repeat bumped to 2.5. Because this was happening in the setting of hypotension, likely that patient is in a prerenal state with decreased forward flow. His creatinine improved and ultimately is kidney injury resolved. # LLE Edema: The patient noted 3 months of progressively worsening swelling and drainage. LENIs 3 weeks ago negative for DVTs. # Penile fungus: Fungus and erythema noted on penis. Started on miconazole powder BID. # Demand ischemia: Pt was found to have troponin leak while in the unit, trops .12 ___K-MBs. He was asymptomatic, denying chest pain. Trops downtrended to .08 on ___ and continued to deny chest pain. # HIV: The patient was diagnosed with HIV this past ___, has CD4 130 on ___. Currently on HAART, which he reports he is compliant with and Bactrim ppx. His home medications were continued while in house. As per ID recs, this azithromycin ppx was held at discharge. # patient: Maintained on weekly interferon. Due for it on ___. # Syphilis - Reactive RPR ___ with positive tests in past. Transitional Issues: - Pt is being discharged on IV Nafcillin to complete at least a 6 week course of IV abx. Ultimate final course will be decided by outpatient ID doctors. - The patient will need the following weekly labs: CBC with differential BUN/Cr AST/ALT Alk Phos Total bili ESR/CRP All laboratory results should be faxed to the ___ R.N.s at ___. All questions regarding outpatient parenteral antibiotics should be directed to the ___ R.N.s at ___ or to the on-call ID fellow when the clinic is closed. - The patient takes Bactrim DS daily for PCP ppx, as per his Atrius records. - As per ID recs, his azithromycin prophylaxis was held upon discharge. - The patient has follow up with both his PCP and ID. - The patient was noted to have possible fungal infection on penis; was started on miconazole powder for this. This will need to be followed up as an outpatient.
summary: You were admitted to the hospital because you had an infection of the skin on your legs (cellulitis) and we also found that you had an infection in your bone (osteomyelitis). During this hospitalization, you were also briefly in the intensive care unit because of low blood pressures. We treated you infection with antibiotics. To properly treat the bone infection, you will need IV antibiotics for ___ weeks, so we put in a PICC line which will allow you to get IV antibiotics while at home.

text: Brief Hospital Course: Assessment and Plan (modified from nightfloat note): ___ YO F with advanced ___ Body Dementia, h/o DVT and PE treated with IVC filter now presenting after 1 week of yelling/agitation with UTI and constipation. . # UTI. Urine culture grew >100,000 colonies of yeast. It was impossible to tell if symptomatic given mental status. - Patient with a h/o severe c diff colitis. No treatment indicated as risk of adverse rxn outweigh the benefits to this - treated with a diaper as per home regimen . # Constipation. Patient with markedly distended colon on CT due to large amounts of stool. Patient with a fecal impaction attempt in the ED without success. Significant progress with second fecal impaction attempt on the floor in addition to repeat enemas. As a result, pt had multiple large BMs over a period of 2 days. They were given counseling on how to best manage constipation . # RLE edema. Negative for DVT on ___ U/S. Likely seconary to venous insufficiency given bilaterality.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ y/o patient with past medical history of NASH cirrhosis complicated by hepatic encephalopathy and grade II esophageal varices, seizure disorder (primary generalized vs. frontal lobe epilepsy), post-polio syndrome affecting left leg and anemia, who presented with abdominal distention, lethargy and acute hematocrit drop, presumed to have hemorrhoidal bleed. ACTIVE ISSUES: # Anemia / Acute Gastrointestinal bleed: Primary concern for variceal bleeding given known grade II varices and decompensated liver disease. ___ score >13. Started on octreotide drip, proton pump inhibitor (PPI) drip, 1g IV ceftriaxone daily (for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis prophylaxis). Briefly intubated for airway protection in setting of urgent EGD. Received 4u pRBCs and 1u FFP with good hematocrit response. GI was following and found no source of bleed on EGD. Patient was extubated without complications and was transferred to the floor on IV PPI. patient then underwent flexible sigmoidoscopy which revealed grade II internal hemorrhoids without evidence of bleeding. Recommendation was made to do a pillcam study if hematocrit continued to drop. Hematocrit remained stable so this study was not done. The patient should have a repeat hematocrit checked in 1 week. Hct on discharge was 28.3. The patient received a total of 5 days of prophylactic antibiotics. Typical course is 7 days, but the increased seizure risk on Bactrim or flouroquinolones was felt to be too high, so antibiotics were stopped on discharge. The patient usually receives ferric gluconate infusion every other week. patient was given an infusion on ___. # Altered Mental Status: The patient was quite sedated on admission to the ICU. Most likely this was a combination of hepatic encephalopathy and medication effect from the patient's antiepileptics. Lactulose was uptitrated and rifaximin continued at home dose with improvement in mental status. An infectious workup was negative (urine culture contaminated with lactobacillus, blood cultures with no growth to date on discharge, CXR without focal opacity, diagnostic paracentesis negative for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis). Neurology was consulted and recommended decreasing morning Keppra dose to 1500mg, however the patient and patient's husband were hesitant to make this change, so 2000mg was continued. On discharge, the patient was back to patient's baseline mental status, which includes dysarthria, slow speech, daytime sleepiness. # Blood Pressure Control: Blood pressure in the emergency room was 108/40 with heart rate in the ___. patient briefly required pressors in setting of intubation and sedation but was quickly weaned. Given patient's stable blood pressure on arrival, and hypotension correlating with intubation, most likely etiology is medication side effect. The patient's blood pressure actually rose while patient was on the floor. patient was restarted on nadolol as well as home dose Lasix but BP remained elevated around 140-160s systolic. patient was started on spironolactone 25mg BID to help with hypokalemia, edema, as well has HTN control. This was uptitrated to 50mg BID on ___. BP on discharge was 134/58. # Edema: Likely secondary to resuscitation with fluids and blood products while in the ED and ICU. The patient was restarted on home dose Lasix when patient was hemodynamically stable. Spironolactone was added to help with edema, HTN, and hypokalemia, and was uptitrated to 50mg BID. The patient will need repeat electrolytes checked in ___ days after discharge. CHRONIC, STABLE DIAGNOSES: # NASH Cirrhosis: Complicated by ascites and grade I varices. No decompensation this hospitalization. Diagnostic paracentesis was negative for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. patient was continued on lactulose, rifaximin. Nadolol was restarted before discharge. # Thombocytopenia: Chronic, and likely related to underlying liver disease. Platelets on discharge were 68,000. # Epilepsy: Longstanding history of generalized tonic clonic and complex partial seizures with recent admission for non-convulsive status. The patient was continued on Keppra 2000mg every morning and 1000mg every night, as well as Pregabalin 300mg twice daily. The patient's neurologist had recently recommended decreasing the morning Keppra dose to 1500mg due to oversedation. The consulting neurologists recommended this change, but the patient and patient's husband were hesitant to change the dose due to concern for seizure on top of recent GI bleed. They both prefer to delay this change until patient fully recovers from this bleed. # Chronic Pain: Patient was restarted on home dose oxycodone and tizanidine prior to discharge. # Asthma: Stable while hospitalized. Patient was restarted on home dose fluticasone and albuterol prior to discharged. # Glaucoma: Stable. Latanoprost eye drops were restarted prior to discharge. # Hyperlipidemia: Continued on simvastatin nightly. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: -Consider decreasing AM Keppra dose to 1500mg once patient recovers from this hospitalization -Needs repeat HCT checked in 1 week and forward to ___ MD. ___ HCT dropping, consider pillcam. -Redraw chem7 ___ and ___ and ___ and forward to ___ MD for review. If potassium and creatinine stable, can move to once weekly checks while in rehab.
summary: You were admitted with a gastrointestinal bleed. You were given blood transfusions in the ICU and the GI doctors did ___ (a camera that looks into your esophagus and stomach) to make sure you didn't have a bleed from your esophagus or stomach, which you did not. They also put a camera in your rectum which showed hemorrhoids, likely the source of your blood loss.
