text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ w/underlying neurodegenerative disorder ___ Disease SCA3 p/w worsening RLE erythema and R knee subpatellar soft tissue swelling after 3d keflex, showing improvement after 1gm IV vanc in ED, with baseline neurological status and MJD-associated dyspnea/tachycardia. . #RLE Cellulitis. Patient's exam consistent with RLE cellulitis, as diagnosed by his PCP 3d prior to admission. Unclear why he developed a cellulitis at this site, but he does spend time crawling around on his knees with his 15mo-old daughter. No history of trauma. On exam, he also had some sub-patellar swelling of his R knee without joint effusion. Subpattelar soft-tissue swelling was seen on R knee films, which were performed for question of foreign body (none seen). Subpatellar bursitis also within the differential, but patient had full active ROM of R hip and knee without pain. Joint function unimpaired. At time of admission he had received 3 days of keflex, plus 1g IV vanc in the ED. He showed clinical improvement, with markedly diminished erythema and warmth, by the following morning. He was continued on MRSA coverage: discharged on Clindamycin 450 mg TID. . #Tachycardia. HR in ___ overnight, with an episode of sinus tachycardia to 130. Patient asymptomatic, not aware of increased heartrate. Unclear baseline HR. BUN/Cr normal x 2 so dehydration unlikely. We suspected that autonomic dysfunction in MJD could contribute to decreased vagal tone, and this was confirmed by the neurology consult service who followed the patient in-hospital. TSH was checked for question of hyperthyroidism but it was elevated rather than depressed. . #Tachypnea/dyspnea Neurology consult evaluated patient since he has underlying neurodegenerative disease. They felt it was possible that his symptoms were due to an underlying central sleep apnea/sleep dysfuncton. Recommended urgent sleep clinic follow-up for CPAP fitting; he has seen Dr ___. He has also worn CPAP before but not recently. . ___ Disease SC3. Patient has this chronic diagnosis, followed by Dr. ___ ___ in ___ neurology. Neurology consult evaluated him in the ED and found him to be at baseline. We continued his home meds: baclofen 20 mg QID, chantix 0.25 QD (less than in OMR, but confirmed w/patient), and trazodone 50 qHS. Chart review and conversation with Dr. ___ demonstrated that patient instructed him to stop chantix due to possible side effects, that his valium was discontinued within the past month, and that clonidine & vicodin scripts were not recorded. Unclear indication for these meds (patient reports using them for insomnia); recommend medicine reconciliation by PCP and neurologist at next visit. . #REM sleep disorder. Patient was continued on trazodone 50 mg qHS. . #SENSATION OF URINARY RETENTION Patient developed a sense of urinary retention during this hospitalization. A post-void bladder scan showed residuals of only 5 ccs. Suspect this may also be related to autonomic dysfunction. ___ need urinalysis if symptoms persist. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES 1. FOLLOW-UP COMPLAINT OF URINARY RETENTION

Given patient's recent admissions, patient was treated empirically for HCAP with risk factors for MDR organisms with IV Vancomycin, Cefepime, and Levaquin until cultures returned as E. Coli, most likely urinary source. It was also considered that patient's symptoms were patient's Wegener's Syndrome or mucous plugging but this was felt less likely. patient was treated with iptratropium and albuterol nebulizers and continued on patient's home 2L O2. Except for persistence of patient's dry cough, patient remained clinically stable and comfortable from a pulmonary standpoint. 2) Urinary tract infection with E Coli bacteremia - patient's empiric infection coverage also took into account urinary tract infection (IV Cefepime and Levaquin). patient grew E Coli from both patient's blood and urine (2 different species with similar sensitivity patterns). Once the urine speciated with E. Coli, patient was switched to oral ciprofloxacin for a 2 week course. patient remained afebrile and stable during patient's inpatient stay, CHRONIC PROBLEMS: 1) Wegener's Granulomatosis - The patient received a stress dose of steroids in the ER. patient remained clinically stable on patient's home prednisone. 2) PCP ___. The patient remained stable on patient's home At___. 3) Hypothyroidism - The patient was stable on patient's home Synthroid 4) s/p Breast cancer treated with mastectomy and chemotherapy in 1980s. - Currently stable with no signs of remission. 5) Depression - The patient was continued on patient's home citalopram and remained clinically stable. 6) Lower extremity edema - The patient was stable despite holding patient's home dose of furosemide, which was restarted at discharge. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: 1) ___ surveillance blood cultures were pending at time of discharge, but had no growth to date. 2) The patient reports trouble swallowing the large omeprazole pill at home, and was given oral dissolving Lansoprazole as an inpatient. As an outpatient, however, patient's insurance will require a Prior Authorization letter from patient's PCP in order for patient's to receive this version of the PPI.
summary: You were admitted because you had a fever and a cough. You also had some worse-than-usual haziness on your chest x-ray. These findings were concerning for either a pneumonia, progression of your Wegener's syndrome, or another problem with the lung. In evaluating your fever, we also found that you had an infection in your urinary tract that was perhaps sending bacteria into your blood stream. We treated you for your infection with antibiotics. We gave you a larger dose of steroid medication then continued you on your prednisone for your Wegener's. Finally, we treated you with inhaled nebulizers to try and help you breath better. You responded to the treatments very well, and we feel you can finish the rest of your antibiotics at home.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ with history of severe asthma and recurrent URI over the past few months presenting with dyspnea and wheezing in the setting of pharyngitis and hoarseness. # Asthma exacerbation: Patient with decreased peak flow, symptomatic dyspnea and requiring frequent nebulizer treatments. Required stacked nebs and IV magnesium in the ED. patient was started on frequent albuterol nebulizers, prednisone burst and given augmentin to treat URI (see below, likely trigger). On the day of discharge patient was able to ambulate without dyspnea and was requiring nebulizers no more frequently than every 4 hours. patient was discharged with instructions to taper patient's prednisone and given an albuterol rescue inhaler. patient was also set up to see new Asthma Specialist as outpatient. # Pharyngitis: patient with recurrent pharyngitis and URI over the past several months. Reportedly patient's ENT exam was normal earlier this month, and patient was diagnosed with glosspharyngeal neuralgia. patient met ___ CENTOR criteria, and has been treated with multiple antibiotics, so patient is unlikely to have GAS. Also with negative monospot as outpatient. Recent throat culture with beta strep, not GAS. patient has been on steroids off and on, and uses ICS, so patient could be considered somewhat immunocompromised in that area, but there was no obvious infection. patient does cite issues with tonsilloliths over the past months, which can be evaluated further as outpatient with ENT. patient was continued on augmentin with instructions to finish augmentin course started by outpatient ENT, and to stop valacylcovir as there was no obvious viral component. patient was given prednisone burst as above, and connected to outpatient ENT where patient can obtain second opinion on utility of tonsillectomy. # Leukocytosis: Presented with leukocytosis to 11.3. Likely secondary to steroid use vs. acute infection. Resolved during hospitalization. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: ====================== - continue prednisone with taper (40mg ___, 30mg ___, 20mg ___, 10mg ___ - continue augmentin for total of 7 days - follow-up with outpatient ENT as scheduled

We stopped the valacyclovir because we did not think there was a viral infection. We are providing you with a rescue inhaler to use if you do not have your nebulizer with you. Also, we recommend that you complete the course of augmentin prescribed to you by your ENT physician. We have recommended that you taper the prednisone over the course of a few days: On ___, take 40mg. On ___, take 30mg. On ___, take 20mg. On ___, take 10mg. We have set you up with a new Asthma Specialist at ___ and ENT physician as well.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ yo F with Burkitt's-like (double-hit) lymphoma with large maxillary tumor extension and known T12 spinal lesion admitted for left leg pain and facial swelling. . # Facial/eye swelling: Very rapidly enlarging mass and swelling initially concerning for rapid tumor growth vs. infection. patient was given vanco in unasyn in the ED, and was started on broadened coverage with vancomycin, cefepime, voriconazole, and clinda on arrival to the floor. CT scan showed extension of the tumor into the maxillary and paranasal sinuses, with no involvement of the orbit. patient was seen by ophthomology, who also did not believe that patient's eye was affected. The swelling rapidly decreased with EPOCH therapy and had returned to normal by the day of discharge. . # Leg pain: Symptoms consistent with sciatica, however in this patient with aggressive lymphoma and known spine lesion, suspicion was high for possible lymphoma lesion as the cause of patient's symptoms. patient underwent MRI lumbar spine, which showed epidural disease causing compression of L5 and S1. patient was given morphine, PO and IV dilaudid and tylenol for pain. patient's pain went away following EPOCH and patient's left leg strength and left foot drop improved with treatment. . # Burkitt's-like (double-hit) lymphoma: Facial swelling and leg pain both due to rapid growth of patient's tumors. patient and patient's family understand at this point that chemo is palliative rather than curative. patient underwent patient's second cycle of EPOCH starting on ___ (had originally planned to start ___, complicated by development of atrial fibrillation with RVR (see below). Otherwise patient tolerated the regimen well and had resolution of the facial swelling and leg pain. patient was discharged on neupogen with a plan to undergo another cycle of EPOCH in 21 days. . # Atrial fibrillation: No known h/o a fib, however on day 4 of EPOCH developed A fib with RVR. patient was put on telemetry, given 5 mg lopressor IV x2, converted back to sinus after ~3 hours. Echo showed very mild decrease in systolic function (EF 50-55%), new mitral regurg. Started metoprolol 12.5 TID in place of atenolol with good control. INACTIVE ISSUES: . # H/o hypercalcemia: has had significant hypercalcemia in the past, however levels were only slightly elevated this admission. . # Lower extremity edema: had been put on lasix PRN for leg swelling, has fluid retention and known ___ DVT. patient was continued on the lasix throughout patient's hospitalization to combat volume overload from patient's chemo regimen.

It therefore became unclear if patient's current symptoms were secondary to osteoporotic-related compression fractures or pathologic fractures secondary to a potential metastatic malignancy. text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ with recently diagnosed bilateral deep venous thromboses who initially presented to ___ with word finding difficulty, transferred to ___ for further evaluation and management of hemorrhagic brain lesions found to be likely secondary to primary lung cancer. Active Issues: # Hemorrhagic brain lesions/word finding difficulty: Consistent with noncontrast head CT at ___, brain MRI on admission revealed multiple hemorrhagic brain lesions, seemingly metastatic, with associated vasogenic edema, mass effect, and minimal midline shift, accounting for subacute word finding difficulty. On admission to the neurosurgery service, patient received dexamethasone 10mg IV x1, followed by continuation of dexamethasone 4mg IV q6h thereafter for reduction in vasogenic edema, as well as levatiracetam 500mg bid for seizure prophylaxis. By the time of transfer to the medicine service, word finding difficulty had improved with initiation of pulse dose steroid therapy. As below, brain metastases were presumed secondary to a primary pulmonary malignancy. patient was evaluated by the neurooncology service, with further treatment plan deferred pending cytologic characterization of lung primary. Under the auspices of the radiation oncology service, patient underwent brain mapping, with plain for 10 sessions of whole brain radiation therapy with hippocampal sparing, for a total of 3000 cGgy. patient was discharged on continued dexamethasone 4mg IV q6h, with plan for taper by the neurooncology service following initiation of targeted neurologic therapy, as well as levatiracetam 500mg bid, to be continued indefinitely; gastrointestinal prophylaxis with pantoprazole also was initiated. Close neurooncology and radiation oncology follow ups are being arranged. # Right lower lobe lung mass: CT torso on admission revealed a right lower lobe perihilar conglomerate of mass and atelectasis, likely representing primary malignancy, with associated right hilar and subcarinal lymphadenopathy and moderate to severe compression of the right lower lobe pulmonary artery and bronchus and minimal attenuation of the right inferior pulmonary vein. 2 additional lesions visualized in the left kidney were presumed metastatic. patient underwent uncomplicated transbronchial biopsy of the right lower lobe mass by the interventional pulmonology service, with cytology ultimately returning consistent with metastatic adenocarcinoma postdischarge. The oncology service was contacted prior to discharge to facilitate close outpatient follow up pending tissue diagnosis. Of note, patient reported high anxiety surrounding diagnosis of pulmonary malignancy, given multiple parallels with patient's father's diagnosis with metastatic lung cancer in middle age, with subsequent rapid demise. patient was followed by social work throughout admission, with good effect, and likely would benefit from continued social supports at discharge; patient was pleased with the pace of work up in the hospital and expressed a desire to sustain such momentum henceforward. # Right upper lobe segmental pulmonary embolus/bilateral lower extremity deep venous thromboses: Presence of bilateral lower extremity deep venous thromboses was confirmed on admission, and CT torso revealed previously unrecognized right upper lobe segmental pulmonary embolus. On admission to the neurosurgery service, systemic anticoagulation was held in the setting of hemorrhagic brain lesions as above, and aspirin 81mg daily and prophylactic subcutaneous heparin were initiated. On transfer to the medicine service, aspirin was discontinued due to unclear incremental benefit, as was prophylactic heparin in discussion with the neurooncology service. Given ongoing contraindication to systemic anticoagulation, temporary inferior vena cava filter was placed without complications by the interventional radiology service. patient remained hemodynamically stable with appropriate oxygen saturation on room air throughout admission. Inactive Issues: # GERD: Pantoprazole was initiated for gastrointestinal prophylaxis in the setting of pulse dose steroid therapy as above. Transitional Issues: * Dexamethasone is to be tapered in the outpatient setting by the neurooncology service pending initiation of targeted neurologic therapy. * Close follow ups with neurooncology, radiation oncology, and oncology are being arranged. * Pending studies: None. * Code status: Full.
summary: As you know, you were admitted for evaluation of brain masses and were diagnosed with likely primary lung cancer with brain metastases. In addition, you were found to have a blood clot in your lungs (pulmonary embolism). You underwent placement of a filter to prevent the blood clots in your legs (deep venous thromboses) from moving into your lungs. You also underwent studies (brain mapping) by the radiation oncologists to prepare for radiation therapy to your brain and met with the neurooncologist, who will guide any additional therapy specific to your brain. Finally, a sample of your lung mass was taken by the interventional pulmonologists to help guide future treatment, and the results are pending at discharge. In order to help with your word finding difficulties, you were started on levetiracetam (Keppra) to prevent seizures and dexamethasone (Decadron) (steroids) to reduce swelling associated with your brain masses. You also received lorazepam (Ativan) to help manage your anxiety. Please **do not** take rivaroxaban, which may be harmful in the setting of your brain masses.

Found to have bilateral DVTs in common femoral and right iliac vein, and right femoral neck fracture. After a goals of care discussion with the patient and patient's family, patient's code status was transitioned to DNR/DNI and patient was discharged home with home hospice. CT scan was performed, consistent with increased tumor burden. The etiology of pain was most likely constipation given patient's history. Additionally, the pancreatic lesion on CT appears to compress the common bile duct. However LFTs were normal on admission. Abdominal US was performed showing gallbladder wall edema, and cholecystitis cannot be ruled out given patient having RUQ pain on initial exam. Doppler showed patent portal veins. The patient was clinically stable and afebrile during patient's entire admission, so no antibiotics were initiated. patient was given an aggressive bowel regimen, moved patient's bowels during patient's hospitalization, and was tolerating food at discharge. # Deep vein thromboses - The patient received a CT scan on admission showing proximal deep vein thromboses in common femoral veins bilaterally as well as in the right common iliac. In light of these findings, the patient's family, in discussion with patient's outpatient oncologist, and palliative care, have decided to transition the patient to home hospice. # Right femoral neck fracture - Patient had CT abd/pelvis in ___ showing new incomplete pathologic fracture of right femoral head. The patient's sodium improved throughout patient's admission with fluids and improved PO intake. On discharge, the patient's sodium was 133. # Delirium - The patient presented with worsening confusion. However, the patient had many reasons during patient's admission to be delirious, including organic brain disease and pain. text: Brief Hospital Course: Mr. ___ is a ___ with history of alcohol abuse, BCC, fungal pericarditis, hypopharyngeal cancer currently undergoing XRT who presents with fevers, respiratory distress and transferred to the ICU for close monitoring, ultimately found to have aspiration pneumonia from difficult to manage secretions and was intubated for airway protection and is now s/p tracheostomy placement. # Respiratory distress, airway compromise: Likely secondary to difficult to manage secretions, hypopharyngeal mass and likely aspiration PNA. On evaluation, he was not stridulous and his airways were patent on laryngoscopic evaluation. However, pt's mental status deteriorated. ABG showed slight hypercarbia but sufficient oxygenation. Given his clinical picture and difficult to manage secretions with evidence of possible aspiration pneumonia on CXR, he was intubated on HD#1 for airway protection with the fiberoptic scope. CT chest showed heavy bronchial secretions occluding the left lower lobe bronchus and severely narrow the left upper. There was also evidence of multifocal pneumonia. He was treated with vancomycin, cefepime, and flagyl for an 8 day total course ___ - ___ and continued on fluconazole which was started for fungal pericarditis (below) which should be continued through ___. ENT saw evidence of possible fungal laryngitis on laryngoscopic exam, and he will be sufficiently covered by his current fluconazole course. Given the likely need for prolonged intubation for airway protection in the setting of his progressive pharyngeal mass, the decision was made to proceed with tracheostomy which was performed by ENT on ___. He was weaned from the ventilator on ___ and has been breathing comfortably with sats in the high ___ on 40% trach mask. # Aspiration pneumonia: Patient presented with fevers to 101 at ___ likely related to aspiration PNA vs HCAP. Most likely aspiration PNA given fevers, copious secretions, and difficulty protecting airway in the context of his pharyngeal mass and radiation treatment. CXR suggested possible infiltrate on admission and CT chest confirmed multifocal consolidations. Pt was started on IV Vanc/Zosyn at rehab on ___ and was transitioned to Vanc/Cefepime/Flagyl to cover for aspiration PNA and completed an 8 day total course ___ - ___. Blood cultures sent from ___ grew MRSA and MRSA later grew in endotrachial sputum cultures. This was felt to be likely due to MRSA colonization. However, if pt has bleeding, would recheck platelets. Inactive issues: # Hypothyroidism: Continued levothyroxine # Hypertension: Hypertensive on admission. ACTIVE ISSUES: . # Shortness of breath: recurrent hepatic hydrothorax. Patient was recently admitted one week earlier for the same issue. patient accumulates fluid in patient's thoracic cavity (more so than in patient's abdomen). patient underwent thoracentesis and was subsequently without dyspnea, breathing on room air. patient was kept for a few nights and did not have any more shortness of breath. CXR showed that the hydrothorax was still present but patient was not symptomatic from it so it was not tapped again. Since patient becomes hyponatremic with Lasix & Spironolactone (see below) these were stopped, but patient was continued on Tolvaptan which was uptitrated. patient will likely need planned thoracenteses to manage patient's hydrothorax. patient may benefit from TIPS in the long run. patient was given an appointment for outpatient thoracentesis 1 week after discharge. In addition, 5 days after that patient will follow up with patient's Hepatologist in clinic. . # Hyponatremia: from diuretic use. patient's recent baseline was ~129, and patient's sodium was 126 on admission. Lasix and Spironolactone were held, and aquaporetics were continued - patient's Tolvaptan was uptitrated from 30mg to 45mg. patient's sodium was 125 upon discharge and did not fluctuate widely during the admission. patient had no neurologic consequences from patient's hyponatremia. patient will f/u with patient's Hepatologist. . # Leukocytosis: resolved, possibly CAP. patient remained afebrile without cough but had a leukocytosis up to 12. Since patient had shortness of breath and a CXR that could not rule out a superimposed infiltrate (because of patient's hydrothorax), patient was started on Levofloxacin for a total course of 5 days as Community Acquired Pneumonia treatment. patient's WBC trended down; patient remained afebrile. patient will follow-up with patient's PCP. . # Alcoholic Cirrhosis: MELD ~23. On last admission, there had been concern that patient's T. Bili was increasing though patient denied EtOH use and patient's serum EtOH was negative. On last admission, RUQ U/S was unremarkable. During this admission, patient's T. Bili did trend down well. patient was continued on Lactulose and Rifaximin without any episodes of encephalopathy. patient's Lasix/Aldactone were held (as described above). patient will follow up with patient's hepatologist on ___. . # Depression: possibly Adjustment disorder related to er liver disease. patient was started on Celexa 10mg for depression. patient had no SI or HI. patient knows that this may take up to 4 weeks to become effective; patient will follow up with patient's PCP and ___ to manage patient's depression. . TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: # VRE colonized # CODE STATUS: Full Code (changed from DNR/DNI on last admission) # Emergency Contact: ___ (daughter) ___

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ y/o patient with a history of FAP, nephrolithiasis, renal cysts, s/p colectomy, iliectomy, and ileostomy that presents with a 1-month history of intermittent nausea and abdominal pain, increased ileostomy output, and dizziness/lightheadedness/dyspnea upon standing or ambulating. ACTIVE ISSUES: # Orthostatic and symptomatic hypotension secondary to acute volume loss and decreased PO intake: The patient was resuscitated aggressively with IV fluids as patient's increased ostomy outputs (see below) were treated. patient's blood pressure was stable and patient was ambulating without symptoms by day of discharge. # Increased ileostomy output - The patient regular has loose stools but reported a significant increase in the output volume, and increased frequency of bag changes. Given patient's nausea and abdominal pain, the patient may have been suffering from a gastroenteritis, with this being patient's equivalent of loose stools or diarrhea. Infectious studies of the stools were negative (as above). The patient was treated with anti-diarrheal agents (loperamide and diphenoxylate-atropine) as wells as stool bulking agents and probiotics. Over the course of patient's stay, patient's stool consistency and output had returned to their usual baseline. # Acute kidney injury, prerenal in the setting of volume depletion- resolved with IVF resuscitation as above. # Nausea and mild intermittent abdominal pain -Possibly secondary to acute gastroenteritis. The nausea was preventing adequate PO intake and contributing to patient's volume depletion. patient was treated with antiemetic medications and IV fluid resuscitation. patient was discharged with antiemetics for lingering nausea, but was tolerating PO intake by day of discharge. GI evaluated the patient and did not feel further imaging was necessary during admission. EGD was planned for the outpatient setting. # Mildly Elevated Lipaase - As per GI, the elevated lipase may have been related to duodenal adenoma resection scarring near ampulla of Vater, causing intermittent obstruction, and low likelihood of pancreatitis. # Elevated lactate - Mildly elevated and stable ~2.2-2.3. Likely secondary to hypoperfusion in setting of significant dehydration vs. infection. Low clinical suspicion for bowel or other ischemia. CHRONIC ISSUES: # Gastritis/GERD: The patient was continued on patient's home pantoprazole. # Familial Adenomatous Polyposis s/p colectomy: The patient was continued on patient's home vitamins and supplements once patient was tolerating PO intake. These were most likely due to severe dehydration from increased ostomy output/diarrhea. We treated you with large amounts of IV fluids, anti-diarrheal agents, and anti-nausea medications. Your blood pressure eventually stablized and your kidney lab values returned to normal by the time of your discharge. We also did not find any severe infections in your stools.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ with a history of rheumatic heart disease s/p AVR/MVR in ___, Afib on Coumadin, and CKD previously on HD (baseline Cr 1.2-1.6) who presents from nursing home with 5 days BRBPR, melena, and dyspnea. ACUTE ISSUES: ============= # GIB: patient initially presented to ___, where H/H were ___. patient received 2U PRBCs and was transferred to ___, where patient was admitted to the MICU. On admission, INR was 4.1, and patient's coumadin was stopped. Home metoprolol and dilt were also held. patient was started on IV pantoprazole. A rectal exam showed scant maroon blood. Flex sig showed old blood to 15 cm, and EGD was normal. patient became transiently hypotensive on day 1, but responded to IVF and 2U blood, and was been otherwise hemodynamically stable. On hospital day 2, after INR had dropped to <2.4, heparin drip was initiated. Home metoprolol was restarted. patient was transferred to the floor on hospital day 3. patient underwent colonoscopy and capsule endoscopy, which were unable to locate source of bleed. Considering patient's normal EGD and the appearance of dark stool on sigmoidoscopy, it was thought that patient likely bled from the right colon or from the small bowel (hx of jejunal AVM in ___. Per GI, it is possible patient bled from an AVM which had resolved prior to capsule endoscopy. patient remained hemodynamically stable with stable hemoglobin, and resolution of melena or hematochezia. # UTI: UA positive for nitrites on admission, and culture grew out e.coli. patient was treated with 3 days of IV ceftriaxone. # dCHF: patient did not appear to be volume overloaded on admission, and patient's diuretics were held given hypotension and active GI bleed. On hospital day 6, patient complained of orthopnea, and exam showed wet crackles. patient had no chest pain. patient was diuresed with lasix 40 mg BID and spironolactone 25 mg daily. patient's weight dropped 4 kg and patient's breathing improved. patient did not require supplemental oxygen. CHRONIC ISSUES: =============== # Afib: The patient is chronically in Afib. patient received Metoprolol Tartrate 12.5 mg TID for rate control. patient's home diltiazem was not restarted, as patient was adequately rate controlled on metoprolol alone. As discussed above, pt's coumadin was held in the setting of GI bleed and restarted once the bleed had resolved. Pt was bridged to coumadin with heparin IV. Pt's coumadin dose was increased from 6mg daily to 7.5mg daily for goal INR 2.5-3.5. At discharge, pt's INR was 2.6. # MVR/AVR: The patient has a history of rheumatic fever, s/p AVR/MVR in ___. Follow-up of valve function has been unclear. patient appeared to be hemolyzing here, with haptoglobin of 5. Given high risk of thromboembolic events in setting of mechanical valve, patient was maintained on a heparin drip until therapeutic on coumadin. # CKD: Patient has a history of dialysis for CKD. patient's kidney function appeared normal while inpatient. patient did have an increase in creatinine to 1.5 when diuretics were restarted, but this appears to be patient's baseline while on diuretics. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: =================== # Anticoagulation: Please continue to adjust warfarin as needed for goal INR 2.5-3.5. Warfarin dose on discharge was 7.5 mg daily. INR 2.6 on discharge. # Pt's home metoprolol 12.5mg BID was changed to TID for better rate control. In addition, given adequate rate control with metoprolol, pt's diltiazem was not restarted at discharge # Mechanical valves and Ascending Aortic Aneurysm: It appears patient has not seen a cardiologist in quite some time for evaluation of patient's valve, ascending aortic aneurysm, and overall cardiac function. patient should follow up with a cardiologist in the next two weeks. # Diuresis: The patient is being discharged on 40 mg BID PO Lasix, up from patient's prior home dose of 20 mg BID. Please monitor electrolytes and replete as needed while on lasix. Please monitor volume status and renal function, as patient may not require this higher dose when back at baseline weight. # Lupus anticoagulant: The patient has a positive lupus anticoagulant that was discovered in ___ in the setting of elevated PTTs. patient saw Dr. ___ at ___ ___ in ___ for an initial visit, but did not return for further evaluation. He would like to see patient's again, as some lupus anticoagulants can cause bleeding. # Adenomatous polyp: The patient had a polypectomy during patient's colonoscopy. Pathology revealed an adenomatous polyp. GI recommended repeat colonoscopy in ___ years, or sooner if patient should develop a change in bowel habits or rectal bleeding.
summary: You presented with a gastrointestinal bleed and resulting severe anemia. You received blood transfusions, and in an attempt to find the source of bleeding, you underwent EGD (endoscopy via mouth), sigmoidoscopy, colonoscopy, and capsule endoscopy. No source of bleeding was found, however it is believed that you most likely had an AVM (arteriovenous malformation) that has resolved. Your bleeding resolved, and your blood levels stabilized. You remained hospitalized until your coumadin became therapeutic after it had held while you were bleeding. In addition, you were restarted on your Lasix (water pill) which was adjusted to 40mg twice a day. At discharge your weight was 54 kg. Finally, you were found to have a UTI during your hospital course, and you were treated with antibiotics for three days.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ Year old patient with PMH significant for type I DM resulting in ESRD on HD presents with pneumonia complicated by difficult to control blood sugars and hypertension. Chest CT showed interstitial edema, which was consistent with chronic renal failure and chronic volume overload, but inconsistent with acute presentation. patient underwent dialysis the next day, but developed a low grade fever and worsening cough and was treated with one dose of vancomycin for concern for bacteremia. Presentation was again suggestive of bacterial pneumonia, thus patient was restarted on antibiotics, this time on renal-dosed levofloxacin. There was gradual improvement in cough and subjective malaise and patient was discharged on 4 more doses of oral levofloxacin to take every 48 hours. #2 Diabetes: Pt treated for hypoglycemia with resolution (glucagon) in the ED and pt's course was complicated by difficult to control blood glucose. RUQ US with patent portal vein but with concerns for worsening portal hypertension, but no focal liver lesions. The patient underwent diagnostic paracentesis in the ED without evidence of infection. patient received 20 mg IV lasix and 20 mg PO lasix. Due to patient's tense ascites the patient underwent large volume paracentesis at the bedside ___ with 4L of fluid removed followed by albumin replacement. Given slight rise in creatinine with diuresis and paracentesis the patient was given albumin replacement. Thoracentesis was held given no respiratory symptoms, and the patient was in no respiratory distress satting well on room air. Additionally given the etiology of the hydrothorax thought to be from the patient's ascites, the pleural fluid was thought to likely rapidly accumulate without addressing the patients ascites primarily. The patient was restarted on home furosemide and spironolactone at reduced doses (20 mg and 50 mg respectively) with good effect. In the future the patient may need consideration of more frequent paracenteses or even an indwelling catheter pending the rate of fluid re accumulation. patient remained asmptomatic and on room air throughout. patient was evaluated by interventional pulmonology for thoracentesis. Given no hypoxia, dyspnea, and incerased aeration of the left hemithorax, and after discussion with the patient and patient's son, it was determined that thoracentesis was not indicated. patient remained asymptomatic satting well on room air on discharge. # Anemia/GIB: The patient reported an episode of BRBPR on the morning prior to arrival. Exam in ED with red blood in rectum (guaiac positive), as well as worsening Hgb to 6.5 on arrival with prior baselines ___ and multiple transfusions in the past. Patient was transfused 2uPRBC with appropriate bump on repeat check of H/H. Likely due to hemorrhoids vs rectal varices vs. AVMs seen on last colonoscopy. More likely lower GIB given bright red blood and slow bleed and hemodynamic stability. The patient also has a history of MDS complicated by anemia, which could have been contributing. The patient was started on cefriaxone due to concern for variceal bleeding, and placed on an ocreotide gtt as well as Pantoprazole IV BID initially. Acute EGD/colonoscopy was not indicated by hepatology. The patient had an episode of melena towards the beginning of the admission and patient's H/H was trended closesly. The ocreotide gtt was discontinued, as was ceftriaxone, and the patient was transitioned to PO pantoprazole BID.patient received 1 unit of PRBCs on ___ with appropriate bump. patient's blood counts stabilized, and patient's Hgb was stable in the 7s on discharge. # NASH cirrhosis: Complicated by grade I varices, hepatic encephalopathy, and fluid retention. Childs class B, MELD score 11. As above, signs for worsening portal hypertension and splenomegaly on imaging on admission, but no focal liver lesions. The patient was initially encephalopathic, but was continued on lactulose TID and rifaximin with improvement. Lasix and spironolactone were initially held given the rise in creatinine, but were subsequently started as above. patient's encephalopathy had greatly improved by discharge, and the patient was alert and oriented x 3 on discharge. # CKD: Cr 1.3 on admission, with recent baseline creatinine 1.5-1.7. During the admission the patients creatinine uptrended in setting of diuresis/paracentesis and lower GI bleed. patient required intermittent albumin towards the beginning of the admission, however patient's creatinine stabilized. patient's creatinine was trended closely, and remained stable in the setting of restarting home diuretics at a reduced dose. patient's creatinine was 1.7 on discharge. # Goals of Care: The patient was noted to have a prior MOLST for from ___ that documented the patients wishes to be DNR/DNI. However on discussion with the son, the patient's HCP, he stated that his mother would currently want everything done. As the patient's encephalopathy improved, patient was asked by the attending hepatologist about patient's goals of care. patient expressed patient's desire to be DNR/DNI. patient also noted that patient's daughter (alternate HCP) was the person that patient felt most comfortable discussing these issues with. patient was advised that patient should speak with patient's daughter to consider making patient's the main HCP and document that decision accordingly. The patient's outpatient hepatologist Dr. ___ was made aware of this conversation as well as the future need to address the patient's goals of care and consideration of need for new HCP that fit more closely with the patient's own wishes. # Hypernatremia: The patient had a sodium of 146 on admission. Likely total body water overloaded but intravasuclarly depleted due to cirrhosis. The patient's electrolytes were trended closesly. patient had another episode of hypernatremia that responded well to free water, and patient's sodium remained stable through the rest of the admission. # IDDM: The patients home insulin dose was decreased due to NPO status on admission. patient had an episode of hypoglycemia to the ___ and patient's insulin regimen was further downtitrated. However given significant improvement in PO status patient's insulin regimen was slowly uptitrated. During the hospitalization the patient had hyperglycemia as high as 500, and patient was started on an additional dose of lantus in the morning to help control patient's blood sugars. # Hypothyroidism: The patient continued home levothyroxine ================== TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: ================== - Patient discharged on new diuretic regimen - 20 mg Lasix and 50 mg spironolactone daily - Due to persistent hyperglycemia with blood sugars as high as 500, patient's insulin regimen was increased to 10U glargine QAM and 15U glargine QHS -Lactulose started to help with hepatic encephalopathy - Ensure follow up with PCP ___ ___ - Ensure follow up with hepatology with Dr. ___ on ___ - Ensure follow up in ___ clinic with Dr. ___ ___ - Please draw CBC on ___ at PCP visit given intermittent need for pRBC tranfusions while inpatient - Will need further discussion of goals of care and to address possibility of making the patients daughter patient's primary health care proxy # Contact: ___ (Son - HCP) ___, ___ ___ (daughter - alternate ___ # Full Code
summary: You were admitted to the hospital with signs of increased swelling in your abdomen and legs. Imaging showed increased fluid in your abdomen. You underwent a procedure called a paracentesis to help remove this fluid from your abdomen. You were given fluids to help protect your kidneys. You were restarted on diuretics on discharge at a lower dose. You also had some blood in your stool but this did not require any endoscopic intervention. You were evaluated by the pulmonology team but did not require any fluid removed from your lungs during the admission. You were doing much better by discharge.

text: Brief Hospital Course: SUMMARY =========== ___ is a ___ year old patient with SLE on chronic prednisone and hydroxychloroquine, class IV lupus nephritis on HD, remote abdominal wall calciphylaxis, chronic hypotension on midodrine, R BKA (___) for R heel MRSA osteomyelitis, E. faecium bacteremia w/endocarditis c/b respiratory failure from metapneumovirus ___, s/p ___bx), RIJ thrombus (___), CVA x3, who presented with worsening abdominal pain and fever, likely due to persistent necrotizing pancreatitis with polymicrobial fluid collections, course complicated by episode of hypotension and somnolence requiring ICU transfer, exposed tunneled line, and persistent pancreatic findings. Following prolonged and complicated hospital course, ultimately, patient clearly voiced definitive decision not to continue with active medical treatments, including dialysis, antibiotics, and nutrition feeds through the NJ tube. This decision was made following extensive discussions with patient, health care proxy, patient's mother, ___ Care, ICU nursing and ICU physicians. The health care proxy supported the patients decision to discontinue medical care, and clearly voiced the decision to discontinue medical care was most consistent with the patient's previously expressed values and goals -- also supported by the mother. After discussion with palliative care and patient's health care proxies, patient was transitioned to comfort-focused care, and discharged to hospice care. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES ====================== [] Mother is healthcare proxy. Friend ___ is alternative healthcare proxy. [] Continue Dilaudid 0.5-1mg Q3 for pain/dyspnea [] Continue Ativan0.5-1mg Q4 for anxiety or dyspnea ISSUES ================ # Necrotizing pancreatitis # Peripancreatic fluid collections # Carbapenem resistant citrobacter/pseudomonas Patient presented with fevers, tachycardia, leukocytosis. Peripancreatic fluid collections appear similar to prior. JP drain in pancreatic biliary system, fluid culture polymicrobial including carbapenem resistant citrobacter (from ___ and pseudomonas. ___ consulted, felt that adjacent fluid collections too small to drain. Patient declining NJ tube to reduce pancreatic exertion. Despite carbapenem resistance, ID did not feel patient had clearly failed meropenem. Meropenem continued at 500 mg Q24H. End date to be determined by ID/OPAT. Repeat CT abd/pel on ___ showed new anterior gastric collection/inflammation. Discussed with GI-pancreas and felt to be unclear etiology. D/w ___ surgery and no role for surgery. Emailed outpatient rheumatologist ___ at ___ re possibility of serositis; seems unlikely. Interventional team holding off on EGD +/- EUS for further evaluation of new collections in anterior stomach wall until nutritional improvement. Repeat CT obtained on ___ demonstrated resolution of anterior gastric wall collection, and ongoing acute on chronic pancreatitis, with fluid collections similar to prior. JP drain was removed on ___. Repeat CT abd/pelvis ___ showing improved size of fluid collections. patient's meropenem was discontinued upon decision to transition to hospice care. # Goals of care patient briefly required ICU stay for hypotension and tachycardia, likely from patient's refusing patient's midodrine and increased anxiety. Within a few days in the ICU, patient began to express clear wishes to refuse dialysis. patient's NJ tube was clogged and patient wanted it out and not replaced. A meeting at the patient bedside was held with patient and patient's mother (health care proxy) and friend ___ (alternate health care proxy), palliative care, ICU nursing ICU physicians, and all were accepting of patient decision to transition to hospice care. Pain is being managed with PO oxycodone, and IV dilaudid and tylenol, anxiety and dyspnea is being managed with IV lorazepam. Patient preferred to continue IV pantoprazole to avoid GI discomfort. # Malnutrition patient received tube feeds through patient's NJ tube placed ___. NG tube was clogged. As patient expressed desire to have it removed and not replaced, this was found to be according to patient's goals of care. NJ tube was removed prior to discharge. # ESRD # Acute pulmonary edema / pleural effusions / hypoxic respiratory failure ESRD secondary to Lupus nephritis. CT with volume overload and bilateral pleural effusions. patient continued to receive dialysis but upon transition to comfort care, dialysis was discontinued per the patient's request. patient's last session was ___. # Episode of somnolence, hypotension, hypercarbia patient triggered on the floor ___ for hypotension to 68/54, and somnolence with depressed respiratory rate (RR 8). VBG showed 7.25/65/217, lactate normal at 1.3. patient was given 500 mL LR and Narcan 0.04 mg IV x1, with improvement in somnolence and increase of patient's BP to ___ (at/above patient's baseline). Repeat VBG was 7.29/58/177. The most likely trigger for patient's somnolence is opioid overdose (given that patient had received oxycodone 10 mg PO x3 on ___, with improvement in patient's somnolence and development of tachycardia, clamminess, and shaking after Narcan administration), on the backdrop of likely obesity hypoventilation and potential ?OSA. started oxycodone 5 mg PO Q6H. Attempted Trilogy/AVAPS while in the ICU but patient refused due to claustrophobia. # Exposed tunnel catheter HD tunnel catheter exposed. Risk for infection, but BCx negative. Had planned for replacement with ___ but after extensive discussion, patient declined the procedure due to the high likelihood of requiring intubation for the procedure. After multidisciplinary discussion decided to pursue awake temp line placement to reduce risk of infection and provide dialysis access. Ultimately when patient went for the temp line placement patient was actually felt to be safe for tunneled line placement, and so this was performed ___. Unfortunately, this line again became exposed, and patient was taken for replacement on LIJ tunneled line placed ___. # RIJ thrombus On apixaban, but was on prolonged heparin gtt for procedures. # Hx of CVA Prolonged holding of home plavix while awaiting tunneled line. # Severe malnutrition No longer on tube feeds. Patient declining NJ tube at this time. # C Diff s/p treatment Continued vancomycin prophylaxis while on antibiotics (___) # Chronic hypotension Continue home midodrine 20mg TID # Constipation: Treated with bowel meds
summary: You were admitted to the hospital because of ongoing abdominal pain and fevers, which were related to the fluid collections around your pancreas, which initially required placement of a drain (which we were later able to remove) as well as broad spectrum antibiotics. You also had an episode of sleepiness and low blood pressure, which was most likely related to your pain medications. You also had contamination of your tunneled dialysis catheter due to a wound over the catheter, and so this had to be changed. After a series of discussions with your family and friend ___, it was decided that you would transition from the hospital to hospice care facility. The focus of your medical care was transitioned to comfort, and several of your medications were stopped.

text: Brief Hospital Course: # Aseptic Meningitis: Patient with lymphocyte-predominant CSF at OSH. Pt also initially presented with bradycardia, so some concern that it could be lyme, but also could be enterovirus, HSV, HIV, CMV, EBV. Given recent groin lymphadenopathy and sexual exposures concern for HIV/HSV. he was started empirically on vancomycin, CTX, acyclovir, and doxycycline. On PE, the patient showed meningeal signs with nuchal rigidity, and has severe HA and photophobia. We tried multiple narcotics, compazine, and IV caffeine for what was presumed to be post-LP HA (LP done at ___ with little relief. His Head CT showed some cerebral edema at the time of admission. When we attempted to get an MRI, he was found to have AMS and unable to hold still. We decided to do an LP, and his opening pressure was 54 cm H2O though pt not in left lateral decub position. His repeat CSF was Poly predominant (376 WBCs with 73% of Polys, 23% lymphs, 2% monos). He was also acutely altered after the LP, and a code purple was called (combative, disoriented). Given the opening pressure, he was intubated and sent to MRI and NSG was called to c/s for the high opening pressure. The MRI was reassuring to the ___ team and further intervention was deferred. We kept him on Q1H serial neuro checks with a low threshold to repeat head CT with any change (did not occur) After this episode o/n, he stabilized and was extubated on HD 3, and his patient began to return to baseline. He was transferred to the floor and continued to have baseline mentation. He had recurring severe headaches, nuchal rigidity, and nausea/vomiting the following day. Given negative cultures (bacterial and HSV), antibiotics and acyclovir were stopped. All viral cultures eventually came back negative and first Lyme serum Ab negative (second one pending at time of discharge). Because of the pt's persistent headaches and febrile episodes, and with inconsistent findings of second CSF with viral meningitis, we decided to do a third LP. Tap was dry and were unable to measure opening pressure or collect fluid. However, pt improved the following day with around-the-clock tylenol, ibuprofen, and PRN fioricet and zofran. He did not spike fevers any more but continued to have episodic headaches and chills with few episodes of vomiting. Pt declined another attempt at LP and after discussion with neuorology, it was decided that viral meningitis was still the most likely etiology and pt was improving overall. Pt was discharged home with tylenol, ibuprofen, fioricet and zofran (PRN) and instructed to follow up with PCP immediately upon returning to ___. Second Lyme serology pending at time of discharge and we will contact PCP with results if positive. If pt is not improving after discharge and Lyme serology is negative, it should be considered to recheck given that it has been about 2 weeks since onset of illness and it can take this long for serum Lyme to convert. Pt was given copy of ALL lab results to give to PCP upon return. . . (contact at ___ lab is ___ ___, pager ___. ___ will send specimen to ___ lab on ___. Follow up with ___ re results later in week. . Most likely causal organism for pt's viral meningitis is enterovirus given season and geographic prevalence, ___ assays were negative but did not test for echovirus or other enteroviruses. As mentioned early, Lyme should still be considered as less likely possibility, pending results of second serum test and pt's clinical improvement. . # Bradycardia: Pt developed bradycardia since admission, as low as high ___ though mostly in ___ throughout admission. ECG done in MICU showed junctional rhythm with no block. (There was initial concern for AV block at outside hospital and thus Lyme was high on differential, though there was no evidence of AV block on ECG/telemetry here). Electrophysiology team was consulted several times and concluded that bradycardia was likely due to high vagal tone in an athletic young patient and that pain/infection may be concomitant on already low resting HR. Pt was asymptomatic with bradycardia and monitored on tele throughout admission. He should have ECG repeated by PCP or army medic and HR should be followed up. An echo was done here which was normal (except small ASD) and revealed no structural abnormalities or valvular problems. .
summary: You were admitted to ___ with headache, fever, and groin pain. You were found to have meningitis and we did a spinal tap to determine that it was not bacterial. We sent many tests from your blood and cerebrospinal fluid which were all negative. The most likely cause of your meningitis is viral and given this time of year, the most likely pahtogen is enterovirus. This is not contagious and other people in your barrack will not need to take prophylaxis. We gave you IV fluids and anti-inflammatory medications to help control your pain and fevers. You began to improve after about 3 days. You should continue to take tylenol and motrin as needed for pain and fever. You should only take fioricet if tylenol and motrin do not control your pain because continually taking fioricet can cause you to get rebound headaches. While at the hospital, you were also found to have bradycardia (slow heart rate). The cardiologists saw you and felt that this was most likely due to you being young and healthy and having a low resting heart rate with pain and infection causing a vagal response that further lowered your rate. You were monitored on telemetry and your bradycardia improved throughout the admission.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ with HTN, anxiety, tobacco abuse, originally admitted to OSH ICU ___ for influenza A and PNA causing hypoxic respiratory failure, found to have neurological deficit concerning for anoxic brain injury, now presents with improving neurologic status as a transfer for second opinion. ACUTE ISSUES: ============= # Hypoxemia: The patient was received by the ___ MICU intubated and completing a 7 day course of vancomycin/Levaquin and a 10 day course of Tamiflu. patient's respiratory status gradually improved and patient was extubated on hospital day 2, but had a continued oxygen requirement up to 5 L NC with 50% face mask. Exam revealed wet crackles bilaterally, multiple chest xrays showed pulmonary edema, and patient was reportedly up 30 lbs from patient's baseline, making volume overload the most likely etiology of patient's continued O2 requirement. Volume overload was thought to be most likely due to fluid resuscitation at OSH. In addition, as discussed below, pt developed hypertension to SBP 180's, and an ECHO demonstrated moderate aortic regurgitation, both of which likely contributed to pt's pulmonary edema. Finally, reactive airway disease was another contributing factor, as pt is a longtime smoker. CT chest was done to rule out PE. Given patient's lasix allergy, patient was diuresed with ethacrynic acid and afterload reduced to lisinopril for blood pressure control. Ultimately, pt's oxygen requirement was decreased to 2L nasal cannula. # Encephalopathy: Per OSH Neurology, the patient showed signs of hypoxic brain injury with only brainstem function remaining. However, on arrival exam the patient had evidence of spontaneous movement and some ability to respond to commands. patient had brisk upper motor neuron reflexes in patient's upper and lower extremities. patient began responding to commands and patient's encephalopathy cleared as patient's sedation was weaned. patient was extubated and patient's mental status cleared. patient had an MRI that showed only chronic small vessel disease. patient had an EEG that did not show any epileptiform activity. patient's Keppra was then discontinued. Upon transfer to the floor, patient was mentating normally, with some residual increased tone in patient's extremities and with upgoing toes bilaterally. On discharge, pt's mental status had improved dramatically, and patient's neurological findings of spasticity improved as well. # Hypertension: The patient became transiently hypertensive to the 180s after transfer to the floor. patient's home metoprolol was discontinued in favor of captopril 6.25 mg TID, which has better anti-hypertensive efficacy. patient was normotensive on this regimen. patient's captopril was changed to lisinopril 10 mg daily prior to discharge. Home Aspirin was continued. # Bacteremia: patient briefly was restarted on broad spectrum antibiotics for sputum that was gram stain positive for GPCs. patient also had GPCs in patient's blood. This eventually grew out staph epidermidis, thought to be a contaminant, with follow up cultures being negative. patient's vital signs and white count remained stable and patient's antibiotics were discontinued prior to finishing a full course. # Rash: patient developed a blanching maculopapular rash that was thought to be related to a drug rash. patient's antibiotics were discontinued secondary to thought that patient's bacteremia was a contaminant. patient's rash improved prior to leaving the MICU. # Abdominal distention: patient developed abdominal distention while on fentanyl for sedation. KUB was concerning for ileus vs obstruction. Follow up CT abdomen showed subcutaneous air and edema in the abdomen, with radiology reading this as possibly concerning for nec fascitiis. Surgery was consulted and did not think this was an infection. patient remained stable with no further treatment. With discontinuation of patient's fentanyl patient's abdominal distention improved. # Guaiac positive stool: The patient's stool was reportedly guiaic positive stool in OSH ED. There was no sign of active bleeding and patient's hemoglobin was stable during both patient's OSH and patient's stay at ___. CHRONIC ISSUES: ============== # EtOH use: The patient was reported to have a history of alcohol abuse. Once communicative, the patient denied alcohol abuse, and patient reported having <1 alcoholic beverage per day. patient was supplemented with folic acid and thiamine for this questionable history of alcohol abuse. # Anxiety: The patient's home escitalopram was continued. Xanax was re-started as needed after sedation weaned. patient received patient's home seroquel nightly. Albuterol nebulizers were noted to increase patient's anxiety, so patient was switched to xopenex. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: =================== # Possible hypothyroid: TFTs revealed high TSH (TSH=13), low t4, normal T3 while inpatient. It can be difficult to interpret TFTs in the context of acute sickness, but sick euthyroid is unlikely as typically presents with low T3 and normal-low TSH. Patient denies any known hx of thyroid issues and was not on thyroid medication prior to this admission. Recommend repeat TFTs as outpatient once acute illness resolves. # Pt was started on lisinopril 10mg PO daily for blood pressure control # Pt was discharged on Ethacrynic acid 50mg PO BID for diuresis of iatrogenic volume overload secondary to IVF resuscitation. patient's diuretics will need to be reassessed based on volume and respiratory status. # Pt will need Chem10 ___ given patient's ongoing diuresis # Pt will need DAILY weights to assess patient's ongoing diuresis # Pt will need a yearly seasonal influenza vaccination # Pt has a history of B12 deficiency and was continued on PO vit B12. Would also consider further evaluation by heptalogy as liver disease may also be causing patient's macrocytosis (Last B12 checked was high). # Pt is on a regular diet with thin liquids, but will require aspiration precautions. #Aortic regurgitation - seen on ECHO, difficult to quantify. Would consider repeat ECHO once euvolemic and cardiology followup. #Hypoxia - currently requiring 2L NC, attempt to wean O2 as volume status improves and lungs recover. In addition patient is receiving q6h xopenex nebs (had tachycardia with albuterol) which can be weaned to prn.
summary: You initially presented from an outside hospital where you had been intubated for respiratory failure. While at ___, you were extubated and were able to wake up. After extubation, you continued to require nasal cannula oxygen, and you were noted to have fluid on your lungs likely the result of IV fluids received. You were diuresed with ethacrynic acid, and your nasal cannula oxygen was able to be reduced to 2 liters. You continued to improve from a neurological and respiratory standpoint, and it was determined that you would require rehabilitation after discharge.

text: Brief Hospital Course: Patient Summary for Admission: ============================== patient. ___ is a ___ w/ dementia, AFib on warfarin, multifocal primary cutaneous marginal zone lymphoma on rituximab, recent ___ surgery for ___ admitted from nursing home with dyspnea. Patient Summary for Admission: Acute Medical Issues Addressed: =============================== # Dyspnea: # Pleural effusions: # Goals of care: Initial CXR was notable for b/l pleural effusions, R-sided atelectasis, & possible superimposed infection. CT showed large right and small left pleural effusions with near complete collapse of right middle and lower lobes and extensive lymphadenopathy. Given concerns initially for CAP & aspiration PNA, the patient was started on azithromycin, ceftriaxone, and metronidazole. Antibiotics were discontinued due to low suspicion for infectious etiology. Etiology of effusions is presumed to be malignant as one-sided and history of lymphoma. The patient has baseline dementia but was able to follow conversations about risks and benefits of thoracentesis and on serveral occasions refused the procedure since patient was not overly symptomatic. The medical team agreed that this was appropriate. PCP ___ was contacted and agreed with this assessment. patient currently has no health care proxy, as patient's daughter was HCP but recently passed away, and patient's son (alternate) was unable to be reached on multiple attempts, with previous documentation stating that at other admissions he was also unable to be reached. The medical team including attending felt that the patient had capacity to refuse the thoracentesis. The patient's HCP (patient's daughter) recently passed away and as such patient has no current HCP. See above for discussion re capacity to decline thoracentesis. Felt patient had capacity as well to change code status, and patient's code status was changed to DNR/DNI. Medical team felt that since patient did not want to pursue thoracentesis and work-up or treatment of the pleural effusion, and etiology of effusion was likely malignant, hospice would be most appropriate for this patient. Patient clearly stated patient did not want any invasive procedures and did not want resuscitation, but the concept of hospice was too complex for patient to follow and felt that patient could not consent at this time to hospice. Medical team still feels that comfort focused care is most in line with this patient's wishes at this time. # Atrial Fibrillation w/ RVR: Rates were initially elevated 150s in ED likely ___ to patient not receiving home metoprolol given BP parameter. patient was re-started on metoprolol tartrate initially at 37.5mg q6h and uptitrated to 50mg q6h due to increased rates. patient was discharged on 200mg metoprolol succinate. Continued rivaroxaban. Chronic Issues Pertinent to Admission: ====================================== #Dementia, unable to achieve ADLs: Stable. See above for capacity discussion. We continued mirtazapine for sleep promotion. Transitional Issues: []Monitor blood pressures, if consistently SBP <100, consider decreasing metoprolol to 125mg daily []Medical team recommends comfort focused care at nursing home is most in line with patient's stated goals, though felt did not have capacity at this time to completely understand meaning of hospice []continue to monitor for dyspnea, if becomes more dyspneic thoracentesis may be within stated goals of care for this patient []discharged with trazadone discontinued, started olanzapine PRN -- recommend no further trazadone

We also treated you with antibiotics in case you had a lung infection. When you leave, you will go back to your facility. We will communicate with your caretakers there and let them know how to take care of you.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ Y F w/ atypical Burkitt's lymphoma D s/p IVAC admitted ___ with febrile neutrapenia found to have ___ GNR Bacteremia (ENTEROBACTER ASBURIAE, KLEBSIELLA OXYTOCA) re-admitted ___ with asymptomatic fever to 101.3 on cipro. . # Fever: source unknown but given ___ GNR Bacteremia (ENTEROBACTER ASBURIAE, KLEBSIELLA OXYTOCA) during recent admission a gram negative is a likely pathogen Differential was very broad including transient cholangitis ___ transiently passing gallstones into the CBD (given cholelithiasis and CB dilatation), UTI, liver or diverticular abscess (although none seen on recent CT abd with contrast), endocarditis (although murmur is old and no valvular abnormalities on a ECHO from ___, illiopsoas abcess, occasional seeding from hemorrhoids when stooling and use of "gum massager". Thorough workup however, including MRI of hip, CT Torso and multiple cultures, did not reveal any source of infection, and patient was empirically treated with Zosyn in order to cover previously cultured organisms. . While on zosyn patient defervesed and patient completed a 14 day course of zosy in house without further culture growth, fever, or other complication related to patient's bacteremia. patient was started on levaquin prior to discharge for prophylaxis while neutropenic. . #. Peripheral neuropathy: During this admission, patient reported the relatively new development of weakness/ numbness of patient's fingers. Although patient had received Vincristine in the past, patient's symptoms were felt to be out of proportion to patient's exposure. Neurology was consulted and performed EMG which revealed polyradiculo-neuropathy. Because of ongoing lymphoma, concern for leptomeningeal involvement prompted LP and MRI of entire spine. Lumbar puncture was not consistant with neoplastic involvement and broad infectious workup revealed no infection. Neurology felt patient's symptoms were likely due to vincristine toxicity. . During patient's hospital stay (following chemotherapy) patient developed 48 hours of fecal incontinence that resolved spontaneously. Given patient's new symptoms and the difficulty with detecting CNS disease patient was re-tapped and reimaged including repeat MRI of the ___ (given motion artifact on previous images) and imaging of brachial plexus. No evidence of CNS disease was detected, and brachial plexus was normal. Repeat MRI of the brain was not undertaken due to possibility of abnormal signal enhancement s/p LP. If desired, this test could be undertaken as an outpatient along with repeat LP for a ___ time to increase the sensitivity for detection of lepto-meningeal disease. Prior to discharge patient's incontinence had resolved, and patient's weakness had improved somewhat. Residual weakness was attributed to vincristine toxicity. . # Burkitt's lymphoma: Patient was hospitalized at due time for next IVAC cycle(rituximab, ifosfamide, etoposide, cytarabine, MTX w/ mesna, dexamethasone, Ara C [held ara-c on ___ due to periorbital edema and rash]). During the second cycle, Ara C re-introduced and although patient developed a mild facial rash, this was felt to be secondary to steroids (steroid rosacea). Patient completed a further cycle of IVAC with only complication of neuropathy as described above. Patient was started on neupogen prior to d/c at 300ucg daily. We continued prophylaxis with pentamidine, acyclovir, and levaquin as above and patient received patient's monthly pentamidine dose in-house on ___. . # Illeopsoas Bursitis s/p right hip replacement: As above, suspected to be source of infection, but no radiographic evidence to suggest this was found. Pain controlled with long and short acting opiates with good response. . # Hypothyroidism: We continued on levothyroxine 50mcg daily . # Depression: Patient developed new symtoms of labile mood and depression. Psychiatry was consulted and recommened re-starting celexa. Because of prior history of sedation with this medication, dosing was performed at bedtime with good toleration. Patient will need to follow up with psychiatry as an outpatient. . #. FEN - regular neutropenic diet, avoid vitamin c, no carbonated beverages, citric acid, NSAIDS, etc . # PPX: bowel regimen, ambulation . # ACCESS: PIV x2 . # CODE: FULL . # CONTACT: husband . # DISPO: pending resolution in fevers/neutropenia.
summary: You were admitted to the hospital for evaluation of fever. This fever was thought to be due to bacteria in your blood stream and you were treated with 14 days of IV antibiotics to clear the infection. While in the hospital you completed your previously planned course of chemotherapy. The neurological weakness you experienced was thought to be due to toxicity from one of your medications - vincristine. You had two lumbar punctures and MRI evaluation of your spine to determine whether there might be any evidence of lymphoma in your spinal fluid. All of this work-up showed no evidence of lymphoma in your spinal fluid.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ y/o F w/ PMH Schatzki ring s/p EGD w/ dilation in ___, Celiac disease presented to the ED w/ 1.5 month history of worsening dysphagia and poor PO intake. Following the procedure, patient had good PO intake and was tolerating mechanical soft diet at discharge. EGD performed given history of Schatzki Ring, which revealed recurrent Schatzki Ring with 15 mm lumen; balloon dilation was performed, with improvement in clinical status. Notably, GI does not believe the Ring can account for all of patient's symptoms. Other contributing etiologies include GERD, given history of untreated reflux symptoms, and functional motility disorder of the esophagus. At discharge, patient was able to tolerate PO intake. You were started on a medication called omeprazole to improve pain you may be having from these ulcers. Please continue to take omeprazole 20mg twice daily.

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ patient with BRAF/V600E+ metastatic melanoma on ___ and trametinib, pembrolizumab C1D22 presenting with worsening abdominal distension, lower extremity edema, acute renal failure, and hyponatremia. Pt presented with ___ (Cr 3.0 on admission) in setting of recently starting pembroluzimab, suggestive of autoimmune response or medication toxicity. Pt received IV contrast for CT torso as outpatient prior to labs resulting, resulting in likely superimposed contrast nephropathy. Pt's creatinine continued to rise beyond the expected contrast nephropathy timeframe, which was concerning for pembrolizumab-induced autoimmune nephritis, although spun urine sediment bland without evidence of significant ATN or glomerulonephritis. Started trial of empiric steroids for autoimmune nephritis on ___ given worsening ___ (Cr 4.8), and Cr now downtrending to 4.0 on discharge. Pt should continue prednisone 1mg/kg/day (30mg BID) for now. Pt will follow up with outpatient oncologist, Dr. ___, to determine prednisone treatment duration (at least one month) and length of slow taper. Pt presented with hyponatremia to 125. Initially attributed to fluid overload, was given Lasix IV x1, and Na worsened to 124. Urine osms/lytes c/w SIADH compounded by intrinsic renal failure (Na 40, Osm 299, FeNa 2.7%). Pt was restricted to 1.5L free water daily, which was d/c'ed prior to discharge when Na had returned to normal (136) after starting steroids for autoimmune nephritis. Pt presented with normocytic anemia with inappropriately low retic count concerning for poor RBC production possibly from chronic chemotherapy medications compounded by acute renal failure. EPO WNL (10.8). No evidence of hemolysis or DIC, no evidence of active bleeding. CBC monitored daily and active type and screen maintained, although blood transfusion was not required. H&H on discharge were 8.0/25.4. Pt developed new onset narrow complex tachycardia on ___ concerning for Afib vs SVT with PVCs. On ECG, it was difficult to visualize p waves and rhythm appeared irregular, making Afib more likely. Suspect Afib related to pembro side effect and acute renal failure given no previous episodes. CHADS2 score 0, therefore no indication for anticoagulation at this time. Thyroid function within normal limits on admission. Converted to NSR, rate ___, after diltiazem 60mg q6h, which was converted to diltiazem ER 240mg daily prior to discharge. Pt was febrile to 100.8 on ___, suggestive of infection or autoimmune reaction. No localizing symptoms or indications to start broad spectrum antibiotics. CXR with new small pleural effusion but no evidence of PNA. Urine culture with mixed bacterial flora, c/w contamination given no urinary symptoms. Afebrile after starting steroids. Pt's metastatic melanoma has had an excellent response to ___ and trametinib. Pembrolizumab was added on ___ and is the likely etiology of current renal failure. Per outpatient oncologist, Dr. ___ and trametinib were held during admission and on discharge given acute renal failure. Pt has outpatient appointment with Dr. ___ on ___, and he will consider restarting chemotherapy medications at that time. [] Outpatient oncologist will decide when to restart home ___ and trametinib. [] Pt will have repeat Chem10 on ___. summary: You came into the hospital because of lower extremity swelling and abdominal swelling. We found that you had low salt levels and kidney failure. You were evaluated by the kidney specialists (nephrologists) and we determined this was most likely related to your medication (pembrolizumab) as well as contrast received with your CT scans. You were started on steroids which helped to improve your salt level and kidney function.

text: Brief Hospital Course: The patient was admitted to the Otolaryngology service on ___ and underwent a radical neck dissection on the right side for a known squamous cell carcinoma with unknown primary. The patient tolerated the procedure well and patient's post-operative course was uneventful. patient was discharged home on POD4 and will have assistance there with patient's daughter. ___: Post-operatively, the patient received morphine and Dilaudid IV with good effect. patient was transistioned to oral pain medications but continued to require some IV morphine on POD 2 and 3. On POD3 patient attempted liquid morphine alone for pain relief but did not have adequate control overnight. patient was transitioned back to vicodin on POD4 with good effect and adequate pain control. CV: The patient was stable from a cardiovascular standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored. The patient has baseline tachycardia during this and last inpatient stay. patient did have sinus tach into the 110s on several occasions this admission, but this was not associated with any chest pain or shortness of breath. patient's hct was checked and was within normal limits, patient had minimal blood loss during patient's procedure. patient's urine output was consistently adequate. Pulmonary: The patient was at patient's baseline from a pulmonary standpoint, patient required ___ N/C of O2, which is patient's baseline requirement at home, patient has a history of COPD. patient does become SOB on ambulation, but was not significatly more so during this hospital stay. GI/GU: Post-operatively, the patient was given IV fluids until tolerating oral intake. patient's diet was advanced from clears to regular on POD ___, and this was tolerated well. patient was also started on a bowel regimen to encourage bowel movement. During patient's prior admission there was concern for a GI bleed - patient had not hematemesis on this stay and did not have any bloody stools or abdominal pain. patient was continued on patient's home protonix. summary: You were admitted to the hospital and underwent a right sided neck dissection for squamous cell carcinoma. You procedure was uneventful and you have recovered without significant events during your stay. You will go home with the staples in place and have them removed during your follow up visit. You can take a regular diet and can continue pain medications as needed. You may shower but should NOT submerge your incision in water - you can use plastic wrap to keep the area covered. You can resume normal activity but should avoid heavy lifting until after your follow up visit.

Your diuretics medication dose was adjusted to help with the swelling in your belly and legs. You received teaching in managing the PleurX catheter and Lovenox injections.

Echo was performed which was normal, and did not show any structural cause for prolonged QTc. Patient was monitored on telemetry without any further events or arrhythmias. ACTIVE ISSUES . #**FALL RISK** During hospital admission, patient was assessed twice by physical therapy, which determined patient's to be a fall risk and stated that it was UNSAFE for patient to be at home alone. Physical therapy recommended a discharge to a rehab facility for this patient. However, after a discussion with physical therapy, the daughter of the patient still wanted to take patient's directly home, and this was the patient's preference as well. Physical therapy then offered family training for the family, but no family member could come to the hospital during daytime hours to receive this training. The family understood that their decision was against our recommendations. . # UTI Patient has no urinary symptoms but ___ the ED had +UA with many bacteria, +nitrite, and +Lg leuk esterase, highly typical of urinary tract infection. Urine culture revealed Amp-resistent E. coli. Given fever, cough, and question of pneumonia, we covered both CAP and UTI with abx treatment, starting renally dosed Levoquin 750 mg Q48 hour PO on ___ for a low creatinine clearance. This should be continued for a total of 5 doses, ending on ___. . # Productive cough Patient presented with productive cough and recent history of fever. During admission, patient had some shortness of breath while lying flat. Patient has no confusion, uremia, tachypnea or hypotension. patient was started on renally dosed levofloxacin 750mg Q48hr PO, with guaifenesin for cough management, initially for suspected CAP. CXR showed no acute processes nor consolidation consistent with PNA. Sputum culture showed growth of only commensal respiratory flora. Legionella urine antigen was negative. . # Hypertension: Nifedipine was initially held due to vasodilation properties while patient was hospitalized with an infection, but restarted on ___ when SBP increased to 170. . INACTIVE ISSUES # Raynaud's phenomenon Per daughter PCP is uncertain about the dx but is treating with nifedipine ___ conjunction with hypertension management. Nifedipine was held during this hospitalization while patient showed signs of active infection. . # Chronic Pain Inactive issue. Patient has chronic pain secondary to osteoarthritis and spinal stenosis. Takes high dose vicodin for breakthrough pain at home. High dose home morphine which is unavailable ___. patient was put on patient ___ instead. patient's home regimen of hydrocodone-acetaminophen was continued. . # Hydrocephalus S/p VP shunt. Neurologically intact and appropriate on exam. patient showed no signs of mental status change. . # GERD patient was continued on home dose of omeprazole. You were also noted to have a urinary tract infection. You were started on oral antibiotics (levofloxacin), which is an appropriate treatment for both infections, and improved. Please continue this medication on discharge.

summary: You were cared for in our hospital for shortness of breath from your COPD. Reportedly you were sent to your primary care doctor's urgent care clinic after your home ___ was finished with patient's course of care. You reportedly had some trouble breathing at the clinic and some concerning EKG findings. In our ED, you were found to be without a fever.
