You also reportedly had a dobutamine stress test several months ago that did not show any concerning abnormalities. We gave you some antibiotics, prednisone, and some nebulizer treatments, and your symptoms improved.

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ with history of hypertension who presented with newly diagnosed cirrhosis and ascites. # Goals of care: On ___, had family meeting with patient, husband, and son's caretakers regarding prognosis and goals of care. Informed them that case had been reviewed by transplant committee and that patient was ineligible for transplant based on advanced age and frailty. Knowing this, patient made decision to transition care to comfort based care. Lactulose was discontinued as patient would prefer not to have frequent bowel movements. In place of the lactulose, will start rifaximin. Antibiotics were discontinued. Patient continued on albuerol/ipratropium nebulizers for comfort with breathing. Lasix and spirnolactone started to reduce discomfort from worsening ascities and pulmonary edema. PRN ativan and dialudid started. Patient discharged to ___ ___ close to home. # ETOH HEPATITIS: Admission MELD was 25, DF was 79.8. Pt with a hx of 2 drinks/day for ___ years. Reports patient has not been drinking for a month. Given infection as below, not on steroids. Concerning prognosis given worsening Tbili, INR. Patient not a transplant candidate given age and fraility. Husband quiet upset that pt is not a transplant candidate. On regular diet with Ensure Plus TID. Unable to use tube feeds given recent variceal bleeding. SW talked to PCP yesterday, but has not talked to husband. #Variceal Bleed s/p TIPS: EGD showed 4 cords of grade III varices in the lower third of the esophagus, esophagitis, bleeding from a varix at the GEJ. patient was started on octreotide and pantoprazole drips and given 1g CTX. A ___ was placed and the patient went to the ___ suite for TIPS with successful decrease in portal pressure from 19 to 6. patient was transferred to the ICU s/p TIPS for further monitoring. patient did well with stable Hcts and was extubated on ___. No further bleeding. # Leuckocytosis: concern for infection given also sinus tachycardia. on vanc/cefeppime for HCAP, so would be organisms not covered such as VRE, anearobs or resistant ones. Given worsening ___, tachypnea, CXR on ___ with worsening upper lobe opacities, CTA obtained on ___. CTA notable for heterogeneous ground-glass opacities most pronounced in the upper lobes c/f infection vs hemorrhage vs edema. Expanded coverage(added falgyl for anearos and azithro for atypicals). UA looked contaminated with multiple epis, UCx only notable for yeast. No further workup per goals of care discussion. # HCAP/Tachypnea: Pt with nonproductive cough this admission, febrile overnight ___ intiated on empiric HCAP rx with vanc/cefepime (had been on empiric CTX prior). On ___, with worsening tachypnea, concern for worsening PNA, PE, worsening asicites, or worsening pleural effusion. CXR on ___ with worsening upper lobe opacities, CTA obtained on ___. CTA notable for heterogeneous ground-glass opacities most pronounced in the upper lobes c/f infection vs hemorrhage vs edema. No PE. Expanded coverage(added falgyl for anearos and azithro for atypicals). Antibiotics d/c'ed on ___ per goals of care discussion. =================== TRANSITIONAL ISSUES =================== [ ] Per family discussion on ___, comfort based care only [ ] After goals of care discussion, lactulose discontinued given patient did no want multiple bowel movements, rifaximin started to prevent/alleviate confusion/hepatic encephalopathy. Antibiotics discontinued. Patient continued on albuerol/ipratropium nebulizers for comfort with breathing. Lasix and spirnolactone started to reduce discomfort from worsening ascities and pulmonary edema. PRN ativan and dialudid started. # CODE: DNR/DNI # CONTACT: ___ (Husband) ___ (home) ___ (cell)
summary: You were admitted with yellowing of your skin, confusion, and fluid in your abdomen. You were found to have cirrhosis(scarring of the liver). You had a screening EGD(a procedure to look in your bowel with a camera). You were found to be bleeding and underwent a procedure to stop the bleeding. During your hospitalization, you developed a pneumonia and were started on treatment. Your liver disease worsening during hospitalizaion. Given your age and overall fraility, you were not eligible for a liver transplantation. Given this and poor prognosis related to no liver transplantation, we had a meeting with you, your husband, your child's care taker and it was decided that we would transition your care to comfort-focused.

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient ___ is a ___ year-old patient with history of multiple sclerosis who presented to the ED with L flank pain and suffered severe anaphylactoid reaction to IV contrast with acute hypoxia and hypotension while undergoing CT scan; in this setting patient received 1 mg 1:1000 IV epinephrine and developed acute lung injury/pulmonary edema and acute myocardial injury for which patient was transferred to the Medical Intensive Care Unit as described above. patient was subsequently transferred to the medical floor on ___. Once transferred to the medical floor, patient's supplemental oxygen was progressively weaned off. Despite persistent symptoms of central chest discomfort following patient's anaphylactoid event, EKG/enzymes failed to demonstrate ongoing/residual cardiac injury. patient ___ noted post-prandial nausea/vomiting for several days s/p patient's ICU stay. patient was treated with compazine and zofran with minimal relief. With ongoing symptoms, patient received a second dose of compazine on ___ approximately four hours later, the patient developed facial contortion and left hand spasm felt likely to represent an acute dystonic reaction to the compazine. patient was treated with benadryl, cogentin, and valium. After approximately ___ hours, patient's left hand spasm resolved, however patient ___ remained unable to open patient's jaw from a closed position despite repeated dosing of benadryl, cogentin, and valium. patient was seen by the Neurology Consult Service and also by Dr ___ Oral-Maxillofacial ___. Although initially unable to speak because of concurrent inability to move patient's tongue, after two days patient's tongue "loosened" and patient was able to communicate verbally despite persistent jaw closure. It was uncertain whether patient's inability to open the jaw represented trismus vs alternate complication of patient's dystonic reaction. patient ___ was observed during sleep with persistent closed jaw, arguing against conversion disorder. patient was maintained on IV fluid hydration and liquid diet by straw. Consideration was given to administration of nerve block to facilitate mechanical manipulation to open the jaw, however on ___ patient's jaw was released from the closed position after 10 mg IV valium and mechanical manipulation by patient's mother - once released, patient ___ was able to independently open/close patient's jaw, eat, and speak without need for further mechanical intervention. In terms of patient ___ original complaint of left flank pain, Neurology Consult service felt that this most likely represented a thoracic radiculopathy related to a herniated disc. patient's symptoms persisted, in waxing/waning intensity, throughout patient's hospital course. On ___, patient ___ notice that patient's right foot was "turning in" (ankle inversion) when patient walked; patient notes that this is a finding patient relates to prior flares of patient's multiple sclerosis. patient also noted "clumsiness" of patient's right hand, most noticeable in patient's hand-writing which has become less legible, as well as right eye "blurry vision". A head MRI was obtained which demonstrated new multiple sclerosis disease activity. Upon consultation with patient ___ primary neurologist, Dr ___ scheduled ___ dose was postponed and patient was treated with a 3-day course of intravenous methylprednisolone at a dose of 250mg every 6 hours. patient's next scheduled ___ dose was arranged for ___. Repeat echocardiogram ___ demonstrated essentially normal cardiac function, without evidence of pericardial effusion or focal wall motion abnormality.
summary: You were evaluated in the Emergency Department for left-sided flank pain. You had an abdominal CT scan to evaluate this pain, and had a severe allergic "anaphylactoid" reaction to the intravenous contrast used for the CT. You were given a high dose of epinephrine, as well as steroids, famotadine, benadryl, and intravenous fluids for treatment of this reaction. The severe allergic reaction and high dose of epinephrine resulted in injury to your heart and lungs. You were admitted and treated for this reaction in the Intensive Care Unit for 2 days, and once stable, transferred to the medicine floor. You also developed a facial contortion and locked jaw (a dystonic reaction) in response to a medication you took for nausea, called Compazine. This resolved initially with medications, except your jaw remained locked for 4 days. You recieved benadryl, benztropine (Cogentin), and Valium. Higher doses of valium in addition to manual manipulation of your jaw was required to finally open the jaw. You developed symptoms of right foot inversion, right hand clumsiness, and right eye "blurring". An MRI of your head was consistent with an active multiple sclerosis flare. You were treated with high-dose steroids for three days, with mild improvement.

In the hospital, you were monitored for abnormal rhythms. You had a pacemaker placed to avoid long pauses in your heartbeat as well as inappropriately low heart rates. Your heart medications were adjusted.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ with a PMHx s/f Crohn's disease s/p colectomy in ___ w/ chronic abdominal pain, h/o GI bleeds, RA, asthma, and previous PE in ___ (on coumadin) who presents with supratherapeutic INR to 7.8, and report of recent large bloody BMs x 3. #LARGE BLOODY BOWEL MOVEMENTS OCCURING EVERY 3 WEEKS. Likely secondary to supratheapeutic INR which is tending to bleed (consider AVM versus small polyp, much less likely diverticular or ischemic colitis) versus hemorrhoid. Also possible is a Crohn's exacerbation given increased stress, although the patient is not having more diarrhea than baseline. Other possiblity entertained in the past is a filling fistula/ aneurysm which releases blood every 3 weeks. It is also possible that the elevated INR is an incidental finding in the context of taking 10mg warfarin daily (although patient is stabilized on this regimen) and a possible factitious disorder as workup has been mostly unrevealing and patient has never had a witnessed episode of hematochezia. Hct is 37.2 (at/ above previous baseline) and MCV is 79. Five mucosal biopsies (EGD and sigmoidoscopy) from ___ were unremarkable. During hospitalization, patient initially was treated with 80mg protonix in the ED, for concern of upper GI bleed, but home omeprazole was resumed when it was clear that this was not an ongoing upper GI bleed. Patient had guiac negative stools, and was able to tolerate PO. patient did endorse some evolving abdominal pain, shifting from patient's right to left lower quadrant, although patient was able to ambulate without difficulty and was witnessed to be outside smoking cigarettes. Infectious work-up was unremarkable with : FECAL CULTURE: No Salmonella, No shigella CAMPYLOBACTER CULTURE: negative FECAL CULTURE - R/O E.COLI 0157:H7 (Final ___: NO E.COLI 0157:H7 FOUND. CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILE TOXIN A & B TEST (Final ___: Feces negative for C.difficile toxin A & B by EIA. MRA was done, showing no vascular cause for patient's pain/bleeding and also showing pancreatic divisum. #SUPRATHERAPEUTIC INR: Unclear etiology, possibly due to decreased PO intake prior to admission. Patient unfortunately was not present for lab draws occasionally during patient's hospitalization, however, patient's INR decreased after 2.5 mg vitamin K. #MICROCYTIC ANEMIA: Likely due to anemia of chronic disease versus gastrointestinal losses as above. Reticulocyte count was appropriate. Patient with ferritin at 9.5. Patient was loaded with 125mg ferric gluconate x2 on ___. ___: Up from baseline of 1.0, but has been to this level in the past. Likely ___ decreased volume given to poor PO intake and report of hematochezia. (HR was 127 at presentation) and will improve with fluid. #Hyponatremia: Again, likely ___ poor forward flow. Resolved to 135 at discharge #Chelitis: Patient was seen to be touching patient's lips during the interview, likely exacerbating some drooling. Also possible is Fe deficiency versus other deficiency as Zinc. Also, ___ Crohn's disease, but less likely. Patient was given Vitamin A and D combined emolient with improvement. Treated with ferric gluconate simultaneously with improvement. #CHRONIC ABDOMINAL PAIN: Pain is ___. Has needed PCA during previous admissions but seems to at baseline at admission. We continued home regimen throughout hospitalization with no changes made. We continued fentanyl 62 mcg/hr Patch Transdermal Q72H (every 72 hours), Gabapentin 300mg q12 hours adjusted for decreased renal function. (was taking 800 mg Tablet PO three times a day) and hydromorphone 2 mg Tablet ___ Tablets PO Q6H as needed for pain. Patient was in contact with patient's outpatient pain team and will follow up with them in the future. #HISTORY OF PULMONARY EMBOLI: Concerning for history of chest pressure and dyspnea on exertion, althoug less concerning given supratherapeutic INR. Goal INR is ___. Patient was discharged with INR of 1.6 with instruction to take 15mg warfarin day of discharge followed by patient's regular 10 with home check on INR on ___ prior to patient's clinic appointment. No heparin bridging was done as concern for GI bleed was greater than concern for PE (both small concerns) #ASTHMA: Not currently active, patient comfortable on RA without wheezing on exam. Will continue home medications. We continued albuterol sulfate 90 mcg 2 Puff Inhalation Q6H prn wheezing, SOB. We held fluticasone 110 mcg/Actuation Aerosol Inhalation BID PRN for now (patient does not take often.) #DEPRESSION: Patinet stable mood, denied SI. We encouraged patient to consider therapy and continued citalopram 60 mg Tablet PO once a day. #ANXIETY: We continued clonazepam 1 mg Tablet PO QID and Temazepam 15mg qHs insomnia. #NAUSEA: home regimen, at baseline throughout hospitalization. We continued dronabinol 10 mg Capsule PO QID as needed for nausea. #VITAMIN D DEFICIENCY: We continued Calcium 600 + D(3) 400units Two (2) Tablet PO twice a day and held cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) 50,000 unit Capsule PO once a week. #Pain control: Patient was kept on home pain regemin. This proved to be a source of conflict as the patient stated subjectively that patient's pain had increased above patient's baseline of ___. However, patient was often seen walking around in patient's room and around the hospital, only endorsing pain when patient was interviewed. #Follow up: -******Patient is to have a rapid CT angio in ED if patient returns for a GI bleed.**** -Pain control per pain clinic. -INR per ___ clinic -Follow up of MRI. -IV Ferric Gluconate x6 (for a total of 1g following ferritin measured at 9.1). Patient was not given scripts to receive these infusions prior to discharge and they will need to be done as an outpatient.
summary: You were admitted for passing bright red blood per your rectum and an INR above your goal of ___. Your INR and blood levels both stabilized during admission and continued to be stable prior to discharge. In addition to ensuring that you had no further blood in your stool and repleting your iron with ferric gluconate, we performed a MRI of your abdominal blood vessels.

text: Brief Hospital Course: Patient is a ___ year old patient with past medical history of ESRD on HD, HTN presenting with 2 days of dyspnea and found to be in hypertensive emergency with flash pulmonary edema and initial concern by CXR for HCAP. ====================== ACUTE/ACTIVE PROBLEMS: ====================== #Hypertensive emergency #Flash pulmonary edema #Respiratory distress / hypoxia Based on physical exam and imaging, the patient's respiratory distress was thought to be due to flash pulmonary edema in setting of hypertension with BP up to 220/166. This responded well to BiPAP in the ED, IV diuresis (though output was reportedly not impressive) and a nitro drip. CXR showed a possible consolidation obscured by pulmonary edema concerning for HCAP, but given a lack of infectious symptoms antibiotics were not initiated. See below for discussion of consolidation. Hemodialysis was performed on day of admission and blood pressure decreased to SBP 180's. The patient's respiratory status improved with this. patient's Carvedilol dose was increased from 12.5 to 25mg BID, while other home medications were kept at the original dosing. Lastly, the patient also under went ultrafiltration on day of discharge to further reduce fluid overload. With these interventions SBP decreased to ~140 at time of discharge. Patient's breathing likewise was back to baseline on room air. #Leukocytosis #Questionable HCAP Due to a lack of symptoms, no fever and a non-definitive CXR, suspicion for HCAP was low. Ultimately the team did not think the patient had an HCAP because patient's leukocytosis returned to baseline without any intervention and a repeat CXR after resolution of pulmonary edema did not show a consolidation. #ESRD Hemodialysis was completed as above while the patient was inpatient without complication. ======================== CHRONIC/STABLE PROBLEMS: ======================== #Gout The patient was continued on home allopurinol. ==================== TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: ==================== [ ] Please keep appointment for hemodialysis on ___. [ ] Follow up with outpatient PCP for blood pressure management. [ ] Recommend outpatient TTE in light of sudden pulmonary edema, heart murmur on exam.
summary: You were admitted to the hospital because you had extra fluid on your lungs making it hard for you to breathe. This fluid was there because your blood pressure had become very high. You received a breathing treatment to open up your lungs and a medication to help your body urinate more. You had hemodialysis and a procedure called "ultrafiltration" to help remove extra fluid. One of your blood pressure medications was increased to reduce your blood pressure.

text: Brief Hospital Course: Summary: patient. ___ is a ___ patient with a history of IBS-C, NIDDM, myotonic dystrophy type II, Takutsubo cardiomyopathy, and rececent admission for campylobacter, who presented with diarrhea, weakness, and leukocytosis. Diarrhea resolved however leukocytosis persisted. Despite extensive work-up it remains elevated at discharge. Further work-up to be pursued as an outpatient. Acute Issues: # Leukocytosis with left shift and thrombocytosis: On admission the patient presented with a leukocytosis as well as a thrombocytosis. patient's initial WBC count was 32 with a monocytosis. The differential of patient's leukocytosis could be a leukemoid response to severe infection, versus a clonal process such as CML or CMML. A Quantiferon test returned as indeterminate, but TB was thought less likely given no known risk factors or imaging findings that would support this. The patient's leukocytosis persisted despite completing a five day course of azithromycin for empiric treatment of campylobacter. Additionally patient underwent a diagnostic thoracentesis to evaluate persistent pleural effusion, which revealed a transudative process. An abdominal ultrasound was performed which incidentally showed an enlarged spleen (14 cm), this together with leukocytosis and thrombocytosis and a persistently elevated WBC count despite improvement in diarrhea was concerning for a myeloproliferative disorder and so hematology/oncology was consulted. On ___ Atrius hematology/oncology obtained a bone marrow aspirate, which demonstrated a reactive process. The bone marrow aspirate was sent for JAK2 MUTATION (V617F), QUALITATIVE WITH REFLEX TO EXONS 12, 13 AND MPL, FISH, CML/ALL, BCR/ABL T(9,22), FISH, MDS/MYELOID PANEL, -___, +8,20Q-, and chromosomal analysis. The results were all pending at the time of discharge. In order to work up a potential infectious etiology, a CT of the torso was obtained on ___, which showed no acute abdominal pathology, and non-specific ground glass opacities in the lungs likely representing pulmonary edema, marrow was heterogenous which could be consistent with a myeloproliferative disorder. SPEP showed no abnormality. Pulmonary also saw the patient and had no specific recommendations but did not believe patient's lung findings were infectious. Outpatient rheumatology and ID followup were arranged as well to exclude auto-immune or infectious etiologies. Despite persistent leukocytosis, patient appeared well. Extensive discussions with family and outpatient providers were held and it was decided that further work-up would be pursued as an outpatient. Further considerations may include evaluation of occult infection (although less likely) versus idiopathic inflammatory process (i.e. rheumatologic). # Diarrhea: The patient had recent admissions for campylobacter diarrhea and presumed c. dif and was treated with azithromycin, levofloxacin and metronidazole on previous admissions. patient completed a 7 day course of levofloxacin (___), which coincided with recurrence of diarrhea on ___. Upon admission, patient was started on PO vancomycin for presumed C. diff colitis, which was stopped on ___ when the C diff assay returned negative. The patient had three stool cultures which were negative for campylobacter or any other infectious process. patient was also retreated with an empiric course of azithromycin while admitted, which was completed on ___. During patient's hospitalization, patient's symptoms improved. # Hypoxia/Pleural Effusions: Patient was hypervolemic on admission with notable pleural effusions on CXR and hypoxia to 92% on RA. Echo revealed normal cardiac function. patient was diuresed with lasix 20mg which improved symptoms. Given persistent leukocytosis, patient also underwent a diagnostic and therapeutic thoracentesis which revealed a transudative process. The underlying cause for patient's ongoing effusions was likely ___ low albumin possible the result of malnutrition and an element of protein loss from patient's GI tract in the setting of recent colitis. A CT chest was completed as part of patient's leukocytosis work-up which showed a "pavement pattern." Pulmonary was consulted who felt this was more likely to be related to pulmonary edema and recommended diuresis. At discharge the patient will require further diuresis with 20mg likely every other day. patient will also follow up with patient's pulmonologist as an outpatient. # Elevated alkaline phosphatase and GGT: The patient presented with an elevated alkaline phosphatase, which slightly worsened during hospitalization, as well as elevated GTT. text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ y/o F w/ peripheral vascular disease c/b L medial malleolus ulcer, recent hospitalization for cellulitis, hypertension, and carpel tunnel syndrome, who presented with worsening left leg redness, swelling, and pain. Several possible causes - this could represent true cellulitis, in which case the bacteria was not adequately covered or possibly needed a longer IV course given venous insufficiency. Equally or more possible based on serial exams is that this does not represent an infection but rather lipodermatosclerosis from chronic venous insufficiency. Supported by this was development of mild RLE erythema and discomfort after 2 days on IV antibiotics with vancomycin and ceftriaxone, and patterns/size of erythematous areas on each leg correlating well in size to the more distal areas of chronic discoloration. Patient had leukocytosis, but per review of Atrius records, no normal WBC count has been documented. It is possible patient's symptoms and exam worsened after hospital discharge because patient was not elevating patient's legs. Has a history of wearing compression stockings but they became too small. Trialed new stockings in house with good effect. Given some uncertainty over the etiology, and relatively safe profile of cellulitis treatment, opted to extend PO treatment for strep coverage to 14 days total, and completed a 7 day course of doxycycline for MRSA coverage which patient completed in the hospital. text: Brief Hospital Course: Primary Reason for Hospitalization: Patient is a ___ F who presented with progressive fatigue, decreased exercise tolerance and easy bruising and was found to have AML. patient completed a course of induction chemortherapy which was complicated by aspergillus pneumonia, ___, and fluid overload. patient's respiratory status improved on antifungal medication and transiently required supplemental oxygen. patient was discharged with blood counts recovered, stable respiratory status, and on oral voriconazole for aspergillus. Physical exam showed ecchymoses on the bilateral thighs, thrush seen in posterior oropharnyx, and temperature to 101.9. CBC showed a WBC count of 123.1 with 96% blasts, and initial bone marrow biopsy showed marrow cellularity of nearly 100% and mostly replaced by blasts. Flow cytometry/cytogenetics showed intermediate risk. FLT3 internal repeat, positive NPM mutation, no metaphase cells available to do karyotype analysis. Patient underwent leukopheresis, and induction chemotherapy with 7 + 3 high dose daunorubicin/cytarabine. patient's chemotherapy course was complicated by mucositis, febrile neutropenia, and pulmonary aspergillosis (see below). Repeat bone marrow biopsy on day 14 of therapy showed markedly hypocellular bone marrow consistent with chemotherapeutic ablation. Patient's WBC count dropped to 0.1, and gradually recovered to 5.8 on day of discharge, day 35, with no blasts detected. On day 32, patient had a repeat bone marrow biopsy, the results of which were pending on discharge. 2. Aspergillosis: Patient presented initially with fever and was given micafungin for empiric fungal coverage. Fevers persisted and a chest CT scan was done showing multifocal nodules c/w mycotic infection. Initial serum galactomannan and beta glucan were negative, but galactomannan antigen on BAL was positive. Patient was switched from micafungin to ambisome for treatment of aspergillosis. Ophthalmologic exam revealed no lesions. Because of acute kidney injury related to ambisome therapy, patient was switched to voriconazole therapy, which patient did not tolerate due to hallucinations. patient was switched back to ambisome and eventually back again to voriconazole, starting with lower doses and tolerated it well. During the course of therapy, patient had one episode of scant hemoptysis, and repeat CT scan showed new cavitations, but stable nodule opacities. Patient continued to improve on antifungals with no further episodes of hemoptysis and remained afebrile with therapy, and was discharged continuing on voriconazole. While patient transiently required supportive care with inhaled bronchodilators and inhaled corticosteroids with supplemental oxygen, by discharge patient had ambulatory oxygen saturations in the high 90's without supplemental oxygen. 3. Drug rash to Cefepime: While being treated for neutropenic fever, patient developed a drug rash on the abdomen with pruritis. This was presumed a drug rash to cefepime and resolved with cefepime being discontinued. 4. Superficial PICC line infection: Patient had pustulence noted at the site of a PICC line placed 30 days prior. It was removed and the tip was cultured, growing no organisms. patient was switched from vancomycin to a 10-day course of daptomycin for empiric coverage for VRE. The site was not erythemetous or tender and patient was afebrile off antibiotics on discharge. 5. Blood product transfusions: Patient was given transfusions of pRBC to maintain Hct goal above 25 and platelets to maintain count above 10. Patient developed anti-platelet antibody and had to receive HLA-matched platelets. 6. Volume overload: In the course of patient's therapy, patient developed pitting edema in patient's lower extremities bilaterally. This was managed expectantly as patient auto-diuresed large fluid volumes. patient felt leg pruritis as the swelling in patient's legs decreased. Chronic Care: Patient presented with no significant PMH Transitions in Care: Patient was instructed to follow-up in the outpatient clinic within a week of discharge. patient has outstanding bone marrow biopsy results to be reviewed and should have blood counts measured. Patient was scheduled for a follow-up CT scan to monitor the progress of patient's resolving aspergillosis. The transplant ___ clinic was contacted and will contact the patient for a follow-up appointment 1.5 weeks after discharge.

Because of your injuries and your neck instability, you had a trach performed and a feeding tube placed for nutrition. You were monitored in the intensive care unit for 2 weeks. Once your vital signs stabilized, you were transferred Your vital signs have stabilized and you are now preparing for discharge to an extended care facility where you can further regain your strength.
original_text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old female who was involved in a car/car MVC. She was brought to ___ ED as trauma activation ___. Following trauma evaluation patient was admitted to ___ trauma service for further care in ___ intubated/sedated. Systems based hospital course as follows: INJURIES: - bilateral comminuted mandibular fx (OMFS non-operative) - basilar skull fx (non-operative) - L squamous temporal bone fx (non-operative) - Post C2 body fx w/ C2-3 flex-distraction (s/p ant fusion ortho-spine) - bilat preseptal hemorrhage (s/p neuro ___ coiling/optho following/stable IOP) - tiny bilateral PTX (stable) - splenic injury (s/p splenectomy) - bilat anterior acetabular fx (stable, WB as tol) - R inferior pubic ramus fx (stable, WB as tol) - laceration x2 R anterior shin/knee (stable, WB as tol) - Shallow impaction fx ant tibial cortex (stable, WB as tol) - RLL contusion (stable, WB as tol) Neuro: Patient was intubated in trauma bay for altered mental status. CT head showed no TBI. Sedation was administered as needed for patient comfort. Followed commands when sedation lightened throughout. Sedation weaned as appropriate. Given hx opiate abuse chronic pain service was contacted ___ to assist w pain control issues. Methadone was started ___ in combination w dilaudid combination long/short acting analgesia. Mental status noted to be markedly improved ___. CT of the head and c-spine were completed as part of trauma evaluation revealing likely carotid-cavernous sinus fistula as well as C2 hangman's fracture. ___ patient went to neuro ___ for embolization of carotid-cavernous fistula. Type I CC fistula w enlarged superior ophtalmic vein was seen and embolized. Unable to embolize cavernal sinus. ___ b/l femoral sheaths were removed. Neurosurgery cleared patient for c-spine repair ___. Repair was initially deferred secondary to presumed pulmonary infection and hesitance to insert ortho spine hardware in setting of active infection. ___ patient went to OR with ortho spine for C2-3 anterior fusion w/ iliac BG and halo application. Per ortho/Nsurg, CT head/c-spine performed ___ revealed interval placement of multiple embolization coils within the right superior ophthalmic vein. No coils are demonstrated in the region of the right cavernous sinus. There is persistent right-sided proptosis and preseptal soft tissue swelling. No evidence of intracranial hemorrhage. On ___ she underwent a repeat cartoid angiogram and had placment of 3 coils to the right carotid sinus fistula. Right ophthalmologic injury noted with ophtho consult obtained on ___. Bedside evaluation ___ was notable for bedside periorbital blood evacuation by opthalmology. Drops/ointments were applied per ophtho recs. ___ optho exam was notable for pressures as follows: R eye pressure 18,23,21. L eye pressure 18,22,19. Opthalmologic evaluation continued on ongoing basis. ___ pressures were approaching normal limits. CV: Patient was resuscitated per trauma protocol with adequate/appropriate response. The patient was stable from a cardiovascular standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored. Pulmonary: Patient was intubated in trauma bay for altered mental status/agitation. Noted to have small B/L PTX though chest tubes not required. Remained intubated for procedures as well as likely VAP (see ID). ___ patient made progress weaning ventilatory support. ___ bronch with BAL was repeated but was not terribly impressive. Respiratory status improved ___. Trajectory of pulmonary progress improved such that patient met criteria for extubation ___. Patient proceeded to decompensate from respiratory standpoint ___ requiring urgent nasotracheal intubation (given halo). With difficult airway and tenuous respiratory status patient was taken to OR for trach/PEG ___. Speculated that poor gag at this time may be related to superior laryngeal nerve stress in setting of recent neck instrumentation. Bronch repeated ___ with clearing secretions. ___ patient weaned off of ventilatory support. ___ tolerated trach mask throughout day. Patient also noted to cough well with good clearance of respiratory secretions. S&S tried PMV eval ___ which patient did not tolerate due to coughing and increase secretions. Concern for laryngeal edema. Vital signs were routinely monitored. GI/GU: Trauma scan revealed splenic laceration for which patient was brought to ___ for attempted embolization. Adequate hemostasis required coil/gel foam embolization multiple splenic branches. Given likelihood of subsequent splenic infarct patient was taken to OR for splenectomy ___. Patient tolerated this well and was brought to ___ for further management intubated/sedated. Patient was given IV fluids on arrival per trauma resuscitation protocol. Dobhoff was placed ___ and TFs initiated which were tolerated well. PEG was placed ___ without incident and TFs resumed ___. She was also started on a bowel regimen ___ to encourage bowel movement. Patient had bowel function per normal with flatus and BMs. Foley was placed as part of trauma evaluation. Urine output was adequate and patient resuscitated accordingly. Intake and output were closely monitored. ID: Patient noted to be febrile ___. Tylenol and cooling measures were initiated. 4+GNR on sputum were found on gram stain and cipro/zosyn started for antipseudomonal coverage. ___ abx were changed to Vanc/Cefepime/Cipro for broad coverage on PNA. Bronch performed for desat to 89 with large amount of thick secretions demonstrated. BAL specimen was sent showing 3+PMNs, no orgs on gram stain. Bronchs were repeated as needed with specimens sent accordingly. Nystatin was started ___. Abx d/c'd ___ as all cultures remained negative. Prophylaxis: The patient received subcutaneous heparin during this stay, and was encouraged to get up and ambulate as early as possible. MSK: See neuro for mgmt of C2 fx. OMFS consult requested for mandibular fx. Noted that evaluation should take place when patient awake/cooperative so formal evaluation deferred through ___. On eval for mandibular fx OMFS stated no indication for operative intervention. Rec chlorhexidine rinse x 1month. Pelvic fractures as above injury list. Eval by ortho notable for non-op management. HEME: Patient required massive transfusion protocol initiation at time of arrival for hypotension. ___ patient received 7 pRBC, ___ FFP, 1 pack platelets. Hct throughout remainder of admit remained stable. No further transfusions required as of ___. DISPO: Remained in ICU from ___ for recovery. ___ consult was placed ___. ___ central line and a-line d/c'd with expectation that patient would go to floor ___. Transferred to the surgical floor on ___. She was evaluated for placement of a speaking valve in hopes of allowing her to speak and to assess her ability to manage her secretions. She was reported to have severe coughing with the cuff deflated and recommendations made to down-size trach tube before attempts made to allow oral intake. Her trach tube was down-sized to a #7 non-cuffed fenestrated trach tube on ___. Tube feedings continued as per order. She was evaluated by Opthamology for further assessement of visual acuity, but exam deferred related to patient's mental status, but recommendations made for lacrilube to right eye every 2 hours. She was re-evaluated by speech and swallow on ___ to assess her ability to tolerate a speaking valve. A Sheily speaking valve was placed and patient was able to vocalize. She did experience coughing after swallowing thick nectar and pain with chewing. In order to better assess her swallowing, she underwent a video swallow and was found to continue to aspirate with liquids, but did tolerate pureed foods. She will need to be evaluated again by Speech/Swallow prior to increasing her diet (see note Speech/Swallow) The patient was found to be making good progress with ambulation, and balance, but continues to have require trach care and tube feedings and for this reason was evaluated for a rehabilitation facility where she can further regain her strength and mobility. She did receive her post-splenectomy vaccines on ___ Of note: she will need follow-up for repeat angio on ___. Neuro. is aware and will call facility regarding time and place.

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ patient with a history of COPD, hypothyroidism, and hemochromatosis who presented as a transfer from an outside hospitalwith a new left femoral fracture, as well as fatigue, nausea, anemia, and new liver lesions on outside hospital abdominal CT, now biopsy-proven diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. patient also had new PEs (now on Lovenox). patient started treatment for DLBCL with mini R-CHOP. patient's course was complicated by persistently elevated bilirubin (likely due to liver disease and hemolysis), warm hemolytic anemia (on Rituxan), steroid psychosis/delirium, and hypoxia that ultimately required a stay in the FICU. patient's mental status ultimately improved and patient was weaned off oxygen. On the floor patient continued to improve, worked with ___ and was deemed stable to continue chemo. patient is now being discharged on C3D10 of R-mini-CHOP. ACUTE ISSUES = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = ================================================================ # Diffuse Large B- Cell Lymphoma: During an outpatient workup for anemia, a CT scan that showed numerous liver lesions. Biopsies show high-grade diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with high nuclear proliferation index (>90%). patient was initially started on treatment with only cyclophosphamide on ___ and Solu-Medrol on ___ and ___ due to an elevated bilirubin. The patient then developed severe delirium and hypoxia from volume overload and was transferred to the FICU on ___. While in the ICU the patient briefly required BIPAP support and improved with diuresis. patient's delirium improved with the discontinuation of dilaudid and olanzapine 10 mg twice per day. Following discharge from the ICU patient subsequently received dose-reduced vincristine and Adriamycin on ___ and Rituxan on ___. Over the course of the next week the patient was weaned to room air, patient's mental status returned to baseline, and patient began to work with ___. Per the recommendations of patient's primary oncologist, it was decided to start patient's next cycle of chemo inpatient. On ___ patient received R-CHOP w/ a dose-reduced prednisone regimen. patient started a cycle of R-mini-chop on ___, which patient tolerated well. patient started G-CSF on ___ and is being continued on it upon discharge. # Pulmonary embolism # COPD # Hypoxia (resolved) On admission, CTA was notable for new segmental and subsegmental PEs. patient was started on therapeutic Lovenox. The patient was stable on ___ NC/facemask and intermittently off of additional oxygen. After receiving 4L of IVF during prep for patient's chemo, patient developed new onset increasing tachypnea, hypoxia and tachycardia to the 140s. patient's hypoxia and tachycardia significantly improved in the ICU with diuresis. The patient progressively was able to be weaned off of O2 on the ___ service, and returned to patient's baseline respiratory status. patient has been maintained on therapeutic Lovenox and will be discharged on Lovenox. # Femoral fracture: The patient initially presented to an OSH w/ a left femoral fracture in the setting of a mechanical fall. X-rays showed an acute periprosthetic fracture at the midportion of the femoral stem of the left hip arthroplasty. Orthopedic surgery determined patient could have surgery if desired but non-operative management is fine as well. The pt did not wish to have surgery. The patient received pain control initially with Tylenol, oxycodone, and morphine with good effect. patient worked with physical therapy when patient returned from the ICU and was reevaluated by ortho who recommended no interventions and ___ until discharge to an acute rehabilitation facility. patient will continue getting ___ at patient's rehab facility. # Urinary retention: Pt was not requiring a foley prior to this admission. Foley has been present for almost entire admission; several voiding trials during the week prior to discharge were unsuccessful. Discontinued olanzapine, which was felt to be the only drug contributing to urinary retention. patient is being discharged with a foley catheter to rehab. This will be a transitional issue for the rehab facility to work on, and if the pt is unable to void, patient should follow up with outpatient urology. # Hemolytic anemia: The patient was noted to have an elevated indirect bilirubin. Labs showed a warm hemolytic anemia with Coombs (+), anti-C3 (+), and haptoglobin <10. patient's LFTs and LDH remained stable. An eluate test was negative. Given that patient was receiving Rituxan as part of patient's DLBCL regimen, there was no need for additional treatment. It was suspected that this was secondary to the patient's hematologic malignancy. # Psychosis (resolved: The patient became psychotic/delirious after receiving high dose steroids on ___, ultimately requiring ICU transfer due to a lack of response to Haldol and increased nursing requirements. patient was started on standing Olanzapine and Dilaudid in the ICU, which ultimately led to better control of agitation and pain. However, patient became non-responsive to questions and commands. On transfer back to the ___ service, patient's mental status progressively improved once Dilaudid was discontinued. Of note, the patient underwent an EEG that showed epileptiform discharges, but no organized seizure activity. When patient underwent patient's second cycle of chemotherapy w/ R-CHOP patient's prednisone dose was modified to 4mg PO QD x3 days and patient was started on Olanzapine 10mg PO QD for 3 days for prophylaxis of steroid induced delirium. This regimen worked and patient underwent patient's second round of chemo without issue. patient was then continued on Olanzapine 2.5mg thereafter. Olanzapine was eventually discontinued several days prior to discharge(due to concern for urinary retention), and the pt did not have any further sx of psychosis or AMS once off the olanzapine. # ?GPC bacteremia (determined to be contaminant). Labs in the ICU showed a lactic acidosis and new leukocytosis. patient was started on Cefepime and Vancomycin. 1 culture bottle grew coag negative staph and corynebacterium, which was deemed to likely be a contaminant. patient received a course of linezolid for growth of GPC in the setting of vancomycin. Ultimately, patient was transitioned off of antibiotics on the ___ service without incident. CHRONIC ISSUES = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = ================================================================ # Tachycardia Baseline is 100-120s, was diagnosed w/sinus tachycardia as outpatient and put on metoprolol XL 50mg PO. Also had new PEs on admission w/ assoc tachycardia. EKGs showed NSR. Cardiology was consulted and felt this is consistent with atrial tachycardia; they agreed on continuing metoprolol. patient's dose was increased to 100mg daily. #Hypothyroidism: The patient was maintained on patient's home levothyroxine. Please check them on ___ and ___ and fax them to ___ to Dr. ___ for monitoring. []Will need Oncology follow up w/ Dr. ___ to discuss further treatment -- this is scheduled for ___ []Please monitor platelets while the pt is on lovenox. patient is on this for patient's pulmonary emboli. Should patient's plts drop to between ___, please reduce the dose in half (from 60bid to 30bid). If plts drop below 30K, please stop lovenox. summary: You fell at home and were found to have a broken hip. We found out that you had blood clots in your lungs. You were recently diagnosed with lymphoma and needed to begin treatment You were seen by the orthopedic surgeons who determined that you did not need surgery for your broken hip. You were started on blood thinners for the blood clots in your lungs. You received chemotherapy to treat your lymphoma. During the chemotherapy, you became very confused; this was likely because of the steroids and pain medications you were being given. You were moved to the ICU for several days because of your confusion and difficulty breathing. In the ICU you received medication to help you urinate, which helped to improve your breathing. Your confusion and breathing improved enough for you to be moved back to the general lymphoma floor. While on the general floor, your cell counts came back up. We gave you a second cycle of chemotherapy which you tolerated well. You worked with physical therapy and became strong enough to go to an acute rehab facility. You should work with physical therapy at the rehabilitation facility. You should have your blood counts checked about every three days at the rehabilitation facility.

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ patient with ER+ Metastatic Breast Ca with involvement of the liver, bone, brain, as well as malignant effusion who presented with fever, pleuritic chest discomfort, and SOB following recent thoracentesis attempt. He was diagnosed with a right hydropneumothorax and admitted to the hospital. # malignant hydropneumothorax patient. ___ presented with fever, pleuritic chest discomfort and SOB s/p unsuccessful therapeutic thoracentesis with ___ on ___. A CTA of the chest revealed a right hydropneumothorax with a small pneumothorax component and moderate to large pleural effusion. It did not show evidence of pulmonary embolism. On ___ patient. ___ underwent right-sided thoracentesis with removal of 770 of straw-colored pleural fluid. This led to significant improvement of the clinical symptoms. The pleural fluid was sent for culture. A repeat CXR post drainage showed a minimal residual right apical pneumothorax. # Fever: In setting of recent thoracentesis with multiple puncture attempts. patient experienced pleuritic discomfort and shortness of breath in setting of known effusion but denied productive cough. patient's WBC was normal. Furthermore, there was no evidence of consolidation on CTA of the chest. patient didn't have any fevers while being hospitalized. Final blood and urine cultures were pending at the time of discharge but with no growth. # ER Positive Metastatic Breast Ca: Followed by Dr. ___. Patient has been hesitant to undergo additional chemotherapies and is currently on PO tamoxifen and everoliums. Previously considering eribulin and pembrolizumab trial but not currently a candidate given suspected cerebellar lesion. Under the guidance of patient's outpatient oncologist, patient received one dose of taxol on ___ with further plans per Dr. ___. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: ================= [] monitor for evidence of recurrent malignant effusion and arrange thoracentesis as clinically indicated. [] further treatment for metastatic breast Ca per outpatient oncologist, Dr. ___ #HCP/CONTACT: ___ (husband) ___ #CODE STATUS: full with limited trial
summary: You presented to the hospital with fever, chest pain and shortness of breath. A CT scan of the chest did show the buildup of a large amount of fluid around your right lung. You underwent ultrasound-guided drainage of the fluid around your right lung and your symptoms improved. You didn't have any more fevers while you were in the hospital and thus we are not concerned about infection at this time. Prior to leaving, you were given one dose of chemotherapy, which you tolerated well. You will discuss further treatments with Dr. ___.

If the steroid dose is too high patient becomes impulsive and agitated requiring Haldol/Ativan. At the moment patient's steroid regimen of 3mg BID is controlling patient's symptoms. [ ] titrate medication regimen for agitation versus somnolence as needed. If patient is somnolent can trial increasing steroids to total daily dose of 7.5mg. Agitation regimen involves Ativan as first line with Haldol as second line. [ ] we discontinued bupropion and Ritalin per discussion with palliative care providers. ACUTE INPATIENT ISSUES: ======================== #Agitation Patient was encephalopathic and obtunded on admission, was initiated on steroids. patient became much more alert however then became impulsive and agitated. Family meeting ___ where the decision was made to pursue home with hospice services for support. summary: You were admitted for weakness and difficulty urinating. We treated you for a urinary tract infection with antibiotics through your IV. We also performed imaging of your chest and brain, which showed that you cancer is overall stable/not dramatically changed from prior scans. Due to your difficulty urinating, we obtained a MRI of your spine. Our radiation-oncology team felt that you may benefit from radiation treatment, so you received 5 radiation treatments to your spine. Due to difficulty urinating, we had to leave the foley catheter in place. You also had difficulty moving your left leg, which we think is due to some swelling from the radiation treatment. We have put you on increased doses of steroids, which you will decrease gradually. You and your family decided that it would be best for you to transfer to a rehabilitation facility with the eventual plan to transfer to hospice where the main goal would be to keep you comfortable.

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ y/o patient with a history of large cell breast lymphoma who presents for autologous stem cell transplant. # Autologous Stem Cell Transplant: At the time of patient's admission patient was started on BEAM protocol for an autologous stem cell transplant. patient tolerated the first days of chemo well. IV fluid rates were decreased and patient diuresed without diuretics. Stem cell infusion was without complications. Post-transplant, patient. ___ developed mucositis that was alleviated with a Fentanyl PCA. patient was placed on TPN while pain limited ability to tolerate PO intake. As cell counts returned and mucositis resolved, PCA was weaned off. patient suffered intermittant diarrhea, testing for c. diff was negative. patient. ___ experienced intermittant dry heaves towards the end of patient's hospitalization, however was able to tolerate 2L of fluid and eat solid food prior to discharge. Labs were monitored daily, electrolytes repleted as needed. patient was discharged home on acyclovir prophylaxis. Follow-up was arranged in outpatient clinic. # Neutropenic Fever: patient. ___ developed neutropenic fever post-transfusion after patient's stem cell transplant. patient was started on Vancomycin and Cefepime with Coriconazole added on after 72 hours. Serial cultures and chest x-ray were negative for infectious process. Urine culture negative. patient's central venous line had erythema and pain around the insertion site and it was decided to remove the line and use patient's port and peripheral IV for access. patient defervesced over the next ___ hours and remained afebrile for the rest of patient's admission. patient was discharged home on no antibiotics. # Right Tooth Pain: Patient had a tooth on the bottom right of patient's mouth that acutely caused patient's pain and patient's cheek became swollen. patient had a panorex done, and was seen by dental who recommended extraction of patient's tooth. summary: You were admitted to the hospital for an elective procedure to fix one of the valves in your heart, the aortic valve. We hope that this procedure will improve the shortness of breath and activity intolerance you've been experiencing. The procedure went well but because of the new valve placement, you developed a change in your heart's electricity that required insertion of a permanent pacemaker. This device will help coordinate the contractions between the top and bottom of your heart. You should take antibiotics for two more days to prevent infection at the site. Lastly, you had episodes of high fever after your valve replacement. Our xrays, blood tests, and urine studies did NOT show an infection. These fevers are likely related to your body's immune system adjusting to the new heart valve.

An MRI was done showing FLAIR signal hyperintensity and patchy enhancement involving the right thalamus, mid brain, splenium of the corpus callosum, inferomedial temporal lobe and right cerebellum with associated leptomeningeal enhancement in the right cerebellum. Broad spectrum antibiotics were begun at that time and the patient was sent to the ICU. ICU: # Neuro: Patient was admitted with headache, fever and altered mental status. There was initially a broad differential that included brain abscess and meningoencephalitis. Head CT and MRI showed multiple FLAIR and enhancing hyperintensities throughout the brain (R thalamus, corpus callosum, midbrain). LP was extremely significant for WBC 1150. ID was consulted. Patient was started on vancomycin, CTX, ampicillin, and acyclovir. Numerous bacterial, viral, parasitic and fungal studies were sent from blood and CSF. PPD was placed and was negative. HIV was negative. Patient continued to wax and wane, and remained somnolent on exam. patient was started on mannitol, which did not improve patient's exam very much, it was stopped ___ for increasing sodium levels. ID recommended treating empirically for TB and mycoplasma. All other empiric antibiotics and antivirals were discontinued once cultures were negative for 48 hours and HSV PCR was negative. Patient was started on RIPE and moxifloxacin. They also recommended dexamethasone to treat the inflammation that could be associated with TB meningoencephalitis. Consecutive CT scans showed improvement of cerebral edema. Step Down: Neuro: Patient's mental status began to improve significantly after decadron was started on ___. Since that time the patient is more awake and alert. A repeat LP showed stable pleocytosis but no improvement. An extremely extensive workup was pursued for infectious and inflammatory causes in the serum and CSF. All of these studies were negative. CT of the torso was done to look for underlying malignancy, and was negative. There was no sign of intrapulmonary TB. Opthomology performed an eye exam to look for tubercles which would suggest TB and/or malignant cells in the vitreous representing lymphoma. The eye exam was normal. We continued to treat the patient empirically with dexamethasone, RIPE and moxifloxicin. patient continued to improve in terms of neurologic exam. patient's left sided weakness improved significantly, however patient continued to have neglect of that side making activity difficult for patient. At discharge, patient's gaze preference and skew deviation was improved, and nystagmus was minimal. patient's left facial droop was mild compared to initial exam. Motor strength was 5- in left deltoid, tricep, wrist and finger extensors and IP, otherwise full strength. Repeat LP showed significant improvement in pleocytosis at this point. MRI on day of discharge showed decreased inflammation and decreased size and intensity of the prior lesions, although radiology read is still pending. Brain biopsy was considered at several points, however it was felt that the patient was improving clinically and the biopsy would not be without risks. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ F with h/o end stage renal disease ___ cadaveric renal transplant admitted for evaluation of generalized weakness and nausea/vomiting after recent change in immunosuppressive medications. . # Nausea/vomiting: The patient's nausea and vomiting were much improved at the time of admission. A non-gap metabolic acidosis was noted and was thought to be to due to the patient's recent vomiting. This was monitored and resolved with IV fluids. Regarding the etiology of patient's nausea, the time course of patient's symptoms correlated with a change in transplant medications; specifically, the addition of Rapamune. The patient's family was adamant that patient's symptoms were due to the medication change. In conjunction with the renal transplant team, the patient was restarted on patient's original combination of transplant medications which included prednisone, CellCept, and Neoral. The patient had no abdominal pain nor diarrhea to suggest other intraabdominal process. The patient remained without symptoms of nausea or vomiting throughout patient's admission. . # Fever: The patient was had documented low grade temperatures in ED at ___ and temp to 100.9. WBC was 9 with a left shift. Urine analysis was suggestive of a UTI and cultures were positive for Klebsiella. patient was started on a 7 day course of ciprofloxacin with a resultant decrease in patient's WBC. The patient remained afebrile throughout the remainder of patient's admission. patient was discharged with a prescription to complete a 7 day antibiotic course. patient was scheduled for a repeat urine culture and follow-up with patient's Nephrologist one week post discharge. . # End Stage Renal Disease ___ CRT: Initial eval in ED was significant for a creatinine of 2.3 and on physical exam in the ED, the patient reported tenderness over patient's renal graft. However throughout patient's admission, the patient's abdominal exam was benign. U/S was obtained to evaluate the graft and this showed no evidence of transplant abnormalities or hydronephrosis. Home Lasix dose was held in light of patient's previous nausea and vomiting and the patient was given gentle hydration which did little to improve patient's kidney function. However, the patient remained stable and at the time of discharge, creatinine was 2.2. . # EKG changes: The patient had ST-depressions in the inferior and lateral leads on EKG from the outside hospital. However, this was considered to be related to demand ischemia given that patient's pulse at this time was 116. EKG here was obtained and showed little change from the patient's baseline. Physical exam was significant for a harsh, systolic murmur at the right upper sternal boarder. CK was negative and troponins were mildly elevated to 0.03 which is within this patient's baseline. It was suspected that this elevated troponin was due to renal insufficiency. Repeat cardiac enzymes demonstrated flat CK with mildly elevated troponins. The patient was restated on home medications without difficulty. . # Edema: Per family report, the patient was markedly edematous including face and Lower extremities. CXR showed no pulmonary edema or effusions. BNP at OSH 293. Lasix was originally held given the that the patient was likely intravascularly dry on presentation in setting of nausea and vomiting. Lasix was restarted during admission and at the time of discharge, the patient was without facial edema and had only trace pedal edema. It is unclear what the cause of patient's initial symptoms were, but given the correlation with patient's recent medication changes, drug effect remains a high possibility. . # Lower Extremity Weakness: Patient and family reported weakness when walking due to back pain. Physical exam was notable for marked hyperreflexia and upper extremity tremor but no focal tenderness. It was unclear how long these symptoms had been present, but pt underwent neurologic evaluation as an outpatient and further work up was referred due to the apparent chronic nature of the symptoms and the patient's plan for further follow-up. Physical therapy was consulted to assess the patient's mobility and initial assessment recommended home physical therapy for deconditioning. .

text: Brief Hospital Course: 1. Bilateral lower extremity edema - The cause of the patient's bilateral lower extremity edema was most likely due to patient's hypoalbuminemia from nephrotic range proteinuria from patient's SLE nephritis. Patient's urine electrolyetes on admission were notable for a urine protein/creatinine ratio of 6.9. patient's creatinine was 2.4 on admission, which was unchanged from discharge from ___ on ___. Nephrology was consulted and recommended starting the patient on lasix. Patient received 40 mg IV lasix on hospital day 1 and responded with a urine output of 700 cc. Lasix was uptitrated to 80 mg IV twice a day, with good response. Patient was maintained on a low-sodium diet. On hospital day 3, patient reported decreased ankle swelling and improved ability to ambulate. Nephrology recommended transitioning to PO lasix in anticipation of discharge, and patient was thus switched to Lasix 80 mg PO BID. Patient's renal function improved during patient's hospital stay, with patient's creatinine decreasing from 2.4 on admission to 2.0 on day of discharge. Patient was able to walk 75 feet with pain controlled and minimal shortness of breath. Neprology recommended stopping sodium bicarbonate, and continuing Lasix at 80 mg BID with daily weights at home. On day of discharge, patient's ankle edema had improved from 4+ to 3+, with no change more proximally in patient's legs bilaterally. - Patient will weight herself daily. - Patient will call patient's nephrologist should patient note increasing weight. - Patient has close follow-up with patient's nephrologist. 2. Lupus: On admission, patient reported pain in patient's ankles, knees and hips, in addition to Cushingoid appearance from patient's prednisone treatment. Rheumatology was consulted and felt there was possible synovitis, and recommended continuing prednisone at the current dose given the standard treatment is 4 wks and patient only had 2.5 wks of treatment. Rheumatology also recommended starting Plaquenil as a baseline medication, and agreed with the plan for cytoxan every month (first dose ___ per OSH records. Calcium and Vitamin D supplementation was initiated for protection from osteoporosis due to chronic steroids. Bactrim was started for PCP ___. On hospital day 3, patient developed few petechiae around the ankles and dorsum of feet bilaterally. The etiology of the rash was most likely secondary to trauma, and was not consistent with a drug rash. - Rheumatology arranged for follow-up with Dr. ___ in two weeks. - Anti-cardiolopin antibody and lupus anticoagulant levels were pending at the time of discharge that will be followed up by Dr. ___. 3. Anemia: Patient's hematocrit was 26.7 in the emergency department. Review of the outside hospital records showed a baseline hematocrit in the low ___. Patient had iron studies done at ___, which were consistent with anemia of chronic disease (serum iron 79, iron saturation 44%) with negative hemolysis labs (although haptoglobin was trending downward on labs). On arrival to the medicine floor, patient's hematocrit was 20.8, with recheck at 23.5. patient's hematocrit remained stable in the low ___ throughout patient's hospital stay. The etiology of patient's anemia was most likely multifactorial, with etiologies including anemia of chronic disease, with possible further insult from the cytoxan patient had received on ___. In addition, hemolysis labs were sent that were notable for a low haptoglobin (<20), elevated LDH (331) and an elevated reticulocyte count (4.8). A blood smear was obtained and showed 1/ schistocyte per hpf by housestaff review. - Patient will have HCT check at nephrologist's on ___. 4. Pleural Effusion: Patient was noted to have a left pleural effusion and small right pleural effusion on patient's admission CXR. Patient had a thoracentesis performed a week earlier at ___ ___, and the results were consistent with a transudate, most likely secondary to the hypoalbuminemia from patient's nephrotic range proteinura. Patient was asymptomatic, and given the recent diagnostic thoracentesis, it was decided to not perform a thoracentesis unless the patient became symptomatic. The effusion on the left was mostly mobile on lateral decubitus. The effusions were thus conservatively managed with diuretics. Patient did not develop any orthopnea, PND or significant shortness of breath during patient's hospital stay. 5. Hypertension - On admission, patient was on Amlodipine for blood pressure control. patient's amlodipine was stopped and patient was started on lisinopril 10 mg PO Qdaily, given the additional benefit of renal protection. Patient tolerated the new medication well. patient's lisinopril was uptitrated to 20 mg PO Qdaily on hospital day 4 to meet patient's target range < 130/85 blood pressure. 6. Hyperlipidemia: Patient's lipid profile was notable for an elevated LDL (261) and elevated triglycerides (207), most likely secondary from patient's nephrotic syndrome. Patient does not have any family history of hypercholesterolemia. The abnormal lipid values should improve with better control of patient's underlying renal disease, and thus anti-cholesterol medications were not started during this hospital stay. - Patient was informed to follow-up as an outpatient with patient's primary care physician regarding patient's lipid profile and the decision to initiate therapy if there was no change after improved control of patient's renal disease or inability to control patient's renal disease. 7. Active urine sediment: Patient received one dose of ciprofloxacin in the emergency department given patient's active urine sediment, which was most likely due to patient's underlying SLE nephritis rather than infection. PND: Patient reported having symptoms consistent with PND two days prior to admission, but denied any orthopnea. During patient's hospital stay, patient had no further episodes of PND. Patient had an echocardiogram that showed normal systolic function with borderline pulmonary hypertension. 9. "Cold" Sensation - On admission, patient reported feeling "cold" despite warm weather. Patient's TSH was low (0.15), and total T4 was also low (3.1) consistent with sick euthyroid sydrome. No treatment was initiated. 10. Constipation - Patient did not have a bowel movement during patient's hospital stay, most likely secondary to narcotics. Patient was discharged home on Colace and Senna at a standing dose, and Dulcolax prn. 11. Patient's urine electrolyetes on admission were notable for a urine protein/creatinine ratio of 6.9. Her creatinine was 2.4 on admission, which was unchanged from discharge from ___ on ___. Nephrology was consulted and recommended starting the patient on lasix. Patient received 40 mg IV lasix on hospital day 1 and responded with a urine output of 700 cc. Lasix was uptitrated to 80 mg IV twice a day, with good response. Patient was maintained on a low-sodium diet. On hospital day 3, patient reported decreased ankle swelling and improved ability to ambulate. Nephrology recommended transitioning to PO lasix in anticipation of discharge, and patient was thus switched to Lasix 80 mg PO BID. Patient's renal function improved during her hospital stay, with her creatinine decreasing from 2.4 on admission to 2.0 on day of discharge. Patient was able to walk 75 feet with pain controlled and minimal shortness of breath. Neprology recommended stopping sodium bicarbonate, and continuing Lasix at 80 mg BID with daily weights at home. On day of discharge, patient's ankle edema had improved from 4+ to 3+, with no change more proximally in her legs bilaterally. - Patient will weight herself daily. - Patient will call her nephrologist should she note increasing weight. - Patient has close follow-up with her nephrologist. 2. Lupus: On admission, patient reported pain in her ankles, knees and hips, in addition to Cushingoid appearance from her prednisone treatment. Rheumatology was consulted and felt there was possible synovitis, and recommended continuing prednisone at the current dose given the standard treatment is 4 wks and patient only had 2.5 wks of treatment. Rheumatology also recommended starting Plaquenil as a baseline medication, and agreed with the plan for cytoxan every month (first dose ___ per OSH records. Calcium and Vitamin D supplementation was initiated for protection from osteoporosis due to chronic steroids. Bactrim was started for PCP ___. On hospital day 3, patient developed few petechiae around the ankles and dorsum of feet bilaterally. The etiology of the rash was most likely secondary to trauma, and was not consistent with a drug rash. - Rheumatology arranged for follow-up with Dr. ___ in two weeks. - Anti-cardiolopin antibody and lupus anticoagulant levels were pending at the time of discharge that will be followed up by Dr. ___. 3. Anemia: Patient's hematocrit was 26.7 in the emergency department. Review of the outside hospital records showed a baseline hematocrit in the low ___. Patient had iron studies done at ___, which were consistent with anemia of chronic disease (serum iron 79, iron saturation 44%) with negative hemolysis labs (although haptoglobin was trending downward on labs). On arrival to the medicine floor, patient's hematocrit was 20.8, with recheck at 23.5. Her hematocrit remained stable in the low ___ throughout her hospital stay. The etiology of her anemia was most likely multifactorial, with etiologies including anemia of chronic disease, with possible further insult from the cytoxan she had received on ___. In addition, hemolysis labs were sent that were notable for a low haptoglobin (<20), elevated LDH (331) and an elevated reticulocyte count (4.8). A blood smear was obtained and showed 1/ schistocyte per hpf by housestaff review. - Patient will have HCT check at nephrologist's on ___. 4. Pleural Effusion: Patient was noted to have a left pleural effusion and small right pleural effusion on her admission CXR. Patient had a thoracentesis performed a week earlier at ___ ___, and the results were consistent with a transudate, most likely secondary to the hypoalbuminemia from her nephrotic range proteinura. Patient was asymptomatic, and given the recent diagnostic thoracentesis, it was decided to not perform a thoracentesis unless the patient became symptomatic. The effusion on the left was mostly mobile on lateral decubitus. The effusions were thus conservatively managed with diuretics. Patient did not develop any orthopnea, PND or significant shortness of breath during her hospital stay. 5. Hypertension - On admission, patient was on Amlodipine for blood pressure control. Her amlodipine was stopped and she was started on lisinopril 10 mg PO Qdaily, given the additional benefit of renal protection. Patient tolerated the new medication well. Her lisinopril was uptitrated to 20 mg PO Qdaily on hospital day 4 to meet her target range < 130/85 blood pressure. 6. Hyperlipidemia: Patient's lipid profile was notable for an elevated LDL (261) and elevated triglycerides (207), most likely secondary from her nephrotic syndrome. Patient does not have any family history of hypercholesterolemia. The abnormal lipid values should improve with better control of her underlying renal disease, and thus anti-cholesterol medications were not started during this hospital stay. - Patient was informed to follow-up as an outpatient with her primary care physician regarding her lipid profile and the decision to initiate therapy if there was no change after improved control of her renal disease or inability to control her renal disease. 7. Active urine sediment: Patient received one dose of ciprofloxacin in the emergency department given her active urine sediment, which was most likely due to her underlying SLE nephritis rather than infection. Antibiotics were thus held on transfer to the medicine floor. Patient's urine culture from admission grew bacteria consistent with skin contaminant and with less than 100k organisms. A repeat urine culture showed preliminarily no growth at the time of discharge. Patient was asymptomatic throughout, with no complaints of dysuria. 8. PND: Patient reported having symptoms consistent with PND two days prior to admission, but denied any orthopnea. During her hospital stay, she had no further episodes of PND. Patient had an echocardiogram that showed normal systolic function with borderline pulmonary hypertension. 9. "Cold" Sensation - On admission, patient reported feeling "cold" despite warm weather. Patient's TSH was low (0.15), and total T4 was also low (3.1) consistent with sick euthyroid sydrome. No treatment was initiated. 10. Constipation - Patient did not have a bowel movement during her hospital stay, most likely secondary to narcotics. Patient was discharged home on Colace and Senna at a standing dose, and Dulcolax prn. 11. Mood symptoms - Patient reported feeling depressed mood at times during hospital course, and envisioned the next few weeks to be even more difficult. Patient was offered a trial of Fluoxetine and was interested in starting the medication. She was thus started on Fluoxetine 10 mg PO Daily, with instructions to continue at 10 mg each day for the first week, and increase to 20 mg each day on the second week. - Patient will discuss her depression with her primary care provider who will titrate Fluoxetine. Patient will see her PCP ___. 12. Right Upper Quadrant Abdominal Pain: Patient endorsed pain in the right upper quadrant of her abdomen on ___. An ultrasound of that area revealed indeterminate hyperechoic regions. It was recommended that the patient undergo an outpatient MRI to further characterize these lesions which ___ be consistent with fatty infiltration. - Plan for patient PCP to order ___ MRI w/o contrast to evaluate liver lesions. The patient was provided with access to ___ pharmacy to fill all of her medications given her lack of medical insurance for medications. Patient was provided with social work support including instructions on filing for partial SSDI, resources in her area, how to deal with her work. The patient was provided a note for work. The patient and her parents were informed of the plan upon discharge and all questions were answered. The patient was FULL CODE during this hospitalization.

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ yo patient with hx of cryptogenic cirrhosis (MELD score ___ who was found to be anemic and hyponatremic in outpatient labs and admitted for further management. #) Anemia: Patient presented with Hct of 29 (baseline of 30 for the past year). While in the Emergency Department, patient became transiently hypotensive and labs were notable for a 3 point hematocrit drop without a clear source of bleeding. Etiology of transient hypotension was most likely in the setting of cirrhosis and poor PO intake. #Shortness of breath: While in the MICU, patient developed acute shortness of breath with new oxygen requirement, was found to have bibasilar crackles on exam and CXR consistent with pulmonary edema thought to be secondary to colloid administration. Cardiac etiology was ruled out with normal EKG and normal ECHO. #)Acute kidney injury: Patient with a creatinine of 2.8 (baseline 0.9), FeUrea 40% and FeNa of 0.27%, suggestive of pre-renal etiology. Creatinine improved with diuresis and at discharge, trended down to 1.2. #) Hyponatremia: sodium of 130 during admission, most likely secondary to advanced cirrhosis. Sodium level normalized by HD3 with fluid restriction. #)Cirrhosis: diagnosed in ___. Cryptogenic cirrhosis thought to be most likely NASH in view of patient's diabetes and HTN, decompensated by SBP, ascities, HE, and lower GI bleed ___ hemorrhoids. MELD score was trended daily during current admission and remained between ___, ___ class C. On exam, mild ascites, spider angiomata and scleral icterus without evidence of encephalopathy. EGD and colonoscopy on ___ notable for grade I esophageal varices and grade II internal hemorrhoids. Given MELD of ___, BMI 32, no history of alcohol abuse, no cardiopulmonary disease and no malignancy, liver transplant work-up was started during present admission. Patient's nadolol was discontinued as there were only grade I varices and patient is ___ class C. patient was continued on cipro ppx (SBP ruled out), lactulose, rifaximin. Initially with aggressive diuresis due to sob and by discharge restarted on patient's home dose of lasix and spironolactone. Hemorrhoids were treated with tucks hemorrhoidal ointment. #) vitamin D deficiency: 25-OH vitamin D was slightly low at 27. Patient was started on vitamin D 800 UNIT PO DAILY. #) DM: Diet controlled with last HbA1c of 5.6 on ___. Metformin held. Was maintained on insulin sliding scale during current hospitalization. #) Migranes: stable, continued on sumatriptan PRN TRANSITIONAL ISSUES ======================================= -Bone/density scan, mammogram, panorex, and PFTs needed for pre-transplant workup -nadolol discontinued given grade I varices and ___ class C -9 mm right lower lobe pulmonary nodule seen on CTA abdomen. Please follow up with a chest CT -patient will have weekly outpatient lab draws, please follow up with CBC and ensure hematocrit remains stable -please note patient had flash pulmonary edema with colloid administration, please give fluids/blood cautiously or with diuresis in the future
summary: ___ patient. ___, It was a plessure taking care of you during your stay at ___ ___. You were admitted to the hospital because of blood tests that showed low sodium and low blood counts. You were given fluids and blood in the intensive care unit. You developed some shortness of breath because some of the fluid went up to your lungs. As a result, you were given medications to get rid of the extra fluid. ECHO of your heart did NOT show any signs of heart failure. You also had a colonoscopy and an endoscopy which showed small esophageal varices (enlarged veins in your esophagus) and hemorrhoids. Your low blood counts were a result of bleeding from your hemorrhoids as well as low coagulation factors (factors that help you clot). They are both due to your liver disease. You will need weekly labs to make sure your blood counts stay stable. Please let your physician know if you begin to notice increased bleeding from your stools.
