text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ y/o F with PMHx of Restrictive Lung Disease, Mild PHTN, Schizoaffective D/o, Hx of rhabomyosarcoma of right face/orbit s/p radical surgical resection, obesity and ___ edema who was sent in from ___ with acute on chronic mixed respiratory failure #Acute on chronic hypoxic and hypercarbic resp failure: Per patient's group home staff, has had frequent abnormal O2 sats in the past with recent baseline oxygen saturation in the high ___. patient was admitted with mixed hypoxic and hypercarbic respiratory failure. Based on prior PFTs, has known restrictive lung disease with some baseline CO2 retention. On admission patient was hypoxic with compensated hypercarbic respiratory failure. Work-up notable for TTE with only mild pulmonary hypertension and some mild LVH/RVH, negative LENIs, Chest fluoro without diaphragm paralysis and CXR without opacities. patient did have some mild pulmonary vascular congestion on CXR for which diuresis was trialed with bump in creatinine. Symptoms felt to be in part due to chronic hypoventilation with atelectasis causing shunting. Psych was consulted for assistance managing patient's sedating psych medications and recommended weaning patient's Seroquel, and we were able to stop Seroquel completely. patient's resp failure improved with clearing secretions, but still requires 2L O2 upon discharge which will likely be patient's chronic requirement #Schizoaffective Disorder: Mental status at baseline on admission. patient was continued on home abilify, trazodone, fluvoxamine and gabapentin. Seroquel was weaned as above per recommendations by psychiatry. Mood stable without change after medication stopped. All meds other than Seroquel were continued. Hypothyroid: continued Levothyroxine Chronic constipation: continued bowel regimen Possible Seizure D/o: continued Gabapentin Left Parotid Mass: currently pursuing work up with ENT and plan for surgical excision, will need to be rescheduled after 1 month
summary: You were admitted to the hospital for respiratory problem related to oversedation from psych meds. We discontinued your Seroquel and the respiratory problem improved. Your breathing appears to be chronically weak due to chronic restrictive lung disease, and it was noted that you needed O2 as an outpatient. patient's in the hospital you also required O2 to maintain adequate oxygenation. You will thus be sent to rehab on O2. Your excess nasal and upper airway secretions should be coughed out when able.

It was felt by the hematology team that patient's anemia is multifactorial with chronic GI loss, impaired bone marrow response and extrinsic nonimmune hemolytic anemia in the setting of chronic liver disease. They felt the hemolytic anemia was a small contribution to the overall anemia and recommended nutritional support to the bone marrow and ETOH abstinence. Pt may need ongoing blood transfusions to support patient's chronic losses, this was discussed with Dr. ___ on ___ who agreed to follow up labs at the ___ appointment. Pt received a total of 3units prbcs and hematocrit was 27 prior to discharge. Pt was continued on folate, thiamine and multivitamin with plan for nutrition and social work consult at rehab. . Acute hepatitis panel was negative and infectious work up was unrevealing including Urine Cx and diagnostic Paracentesis which was negative for SBP. Pt had one blood Cx bottle return positive for coag negative staph and pt was treated with IV vancomycin while awaiting further surveillance Cx. Pt was seen by physical therapy who felt that patient would definitely require rehab and pt was eager for transfer to ___ on ___. .
summary: You were admitted with acute on chronic anemia, worsening liver function and mild encephalopathy. You have been evaluated by the liver team and underwent an EGD which did not show any acute bleeding. It did show portal gastropathy and grade II varices. You have been seen by the hematology team who feel that you have multiple factors contributing to the anemia including slow GI bleeding, depressed bone marrow function and a mild degree of hemolysis. You have been transfused with 3units of prbcs with improvement in your hematocrit to 27. You underwent a diagnostic paracentesis which did not any evidence of peritonitis. The infectious work up has been unrevealing and you have been started on rifaximin twice daily for hepatic encephalopathy.

Brief Hospital Course: #) Altered mental status: Felt to be most likely due to metabolic encephalopathy in setting of underlying infection. #) Status-post fall: Patient unable to full recall details. ___ have been mechanical, secondary to seizure, or other etiology. patient was never hypotensive, and EKG and telemetry were unrevealing for etiology. Physical therapy evaluated the patient and felt that either 24 hour care or rehabilitation was appropriate.
#) ___ body dementia: Per family, oriented x2 most recently, has hallucinations especially at night, sees people who aren't there, knows they are hallucinations but still feels scared by it. patient was treated with supportive care and did well aside from occasionally refusing medications unless re-assured by a physician. patient was continued on patient's home aricept.
#) Diarrhea: Loose stools were noted during the ___ and ___ days of hospitalization. During this presentation, patient reported high fevers, malaise and cough productive of blood-tinged sputum. patient had also recently completed an antibiotic course for pneumonia with levaquin. Clinical picture was concerning for atypical pneumonia in an immunocompromised patient (s/p alloSCT; ___ years ago). Differential included atypical infection including bacterial, fungal, and AFB. Given patient's recurrences, we also considered impaired humoral immunity (like hypogammaglobulinemia) or aspiration (in the setting of patient's known esophageal dysmotility). Inflammatory or autoimmune causes of patient's lung opacities are also possible including cryptogenic organizing pneumonia. However, this was felt to be less likely given that patient improved without treatment with steroids. patient's infectious work-up including flu, acid fast smear, blood cultures, sputum cultures and fungal markers were negative. Patient underwent a bronchoscopy with BAL sent for infectious work-up as well. This was also unrevealing with a few studies pending on discharge. We had planned for a lung biopsy but follow-up CT chest showed interval improvement therefore this was aborted. Since patient improved on antibiotics, it was felt that this was a bacterial infection. However, patient is at risk for aspiration with patient's known esophageal dysmotility so patient was encouraged to take PPIs and follow-up with patient's gastroenterologist. patient was also noted to have low IgG subtype 2. We checked baseline pneumococcal serotype, diphtheria/tetanus and strep titers for elucidation of response to polysaccharide and protein antigens. These were pending on discharge. text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ F with a history of bronchiectasis who presents with 2-day history of worsening cough/dyspnea. In the ED, patient was noted to be hypoxic requiring 6L by NC to maintain O2 sats in mid-90s and had elevated lactate to 2.6 and was referred to the ICU given concern for deterioration. In the ICU, patient received initial broad coverage with oseltamavir and antibiotics and respiratory status stabilized. patient was called out to the floor on hospital day #2 and continued to require less oxygen prior to discharge. ACTIVE ISSUES: #. HYPOXIC RESPIRATORY DISTRESS: Patient has a history of bronchiectasis but based on imaging findings may also have an element of COPD/emphysema. patient had wheezing on exam on admission and felt symptomatically improved after nebs in the ED. patient also had dry rales at the bases. patient was swabbed for influenza (DFA negative; oseltamavir stopped) and urinary legionella antigen was also noted to be negative. patient was covered with broad spectrum antibiotics with vancomycin, cefepime and azithromycin to cover HAP given patient's recent admission for kyphoplasty. Despite wet-sounding cough, patient was unable to produce a sputum sample suitable for analysis. At the time of call out from the ICU, patient's O2 sat was 88-90% on RA and mid-90s on 4L NC. During patient's time on the floor, patient only required ___ L O2 for saturations in the mid ___. patient will continue on antibiotics (Cefpodoxime and Cipro) for a 10-day total course, or 5 more days after discharge. #. You received treatment with lactulose and rifaximin, which you will need to continue taking as an outpatient (the rifaximin is waiting for you at the pharmacy!). We decreased the dose of your clonazepam because with cirrhosis, the liver is unable to break down clonazepam as effectively and thus levels can accumulate in your system causing confusion. You were started on a medication called Buspar to help with symptoms of anxiety. Cardiology fully examined the patient and patient's cardiac monitoring strips and determined there was no indication for intervention. The patient then began showing prolonged pauses in between heart beats, and out of an abundance of caution patient was transferred back to the trauma surgery ICU. Cardiology re-evaluated the patient, and electrophysiology was also consulted, and both teams decided since patient was asymptomatic there was nothing to do for this patient and they recommended transferring patient's back to the floor and taking patient's off telemetry. Chest X-ray was unremarkable. patient's respiratory status and oxygen saturation were monitored closely in the ICU, and patient improved. Cardiology was previously on consult was reconsulted and suggested we start amlodipine 5mg. patient's vitals improved after starting the amlodipine. On ___ the NG tube was clamped given low output and removed. A pigtail catheter that was placed to drain pleural effusions in the ICU was also removed at that time. A follow up chest xray did not reveal any new abnormalities. Talked to Dr. ___ (___) at ___ and communicated information about restarting xarelto, stopping the atenolol, restarting the amlodipine in the setting of bradycardia per our formal cardiology recommendation. A surgery was done to reduce it. This was successful but they were not able to repair the hole that the stomach went through because of bleeding. Repeat imaging after your operation showed that your stomach was untwisted but you still had part of it in your lung space. We believe that at this time a second operation would be contraindicated. You would need to gain strength before a second operation. A Gastric tube that connects to your stomach was also placed at the time of operation and you are receiving feeds through there. That should help get you stronger.

text: Brief Hospital Course: Mr. ___ is a ___ year old man with HTN and daily etoh abuse who woke up at 7am with worse HA of life at noon found by wife in a likely complex partial seizure with secondary generalization (loud vocalization left head deviation and then tonic rigidity) that self resolved in about 1 minute. BRIEF ICU COURSE: Patient was initially admitted to the NeuroICU for close monitoring. Neurological exam shows unequal, reactive pupils (L>R) but otherwise, nonfocal exam. Noncontrast head ct showed a 3 cm left temporal bleed with mild surrounding vasogenic edema and localized mass effect, but no midline shift and basal cisterns intact. Etiology for bleed unlikely to be hypertensive given location and only mildly elevated BP at OSH. Underlying structural lesion is possible, especially since there appears to be prominent vasculature on CTA. Venous thrombosis was also considered. . #Left Temporoparietal Intraparenchymal Hemorrhage: The patient underwent and MRI/MRV to further delineate an underlying mass/lession (see full report above). There was no evidence of venous sinus thrombosis or mass, and the previously identified bleed was deemed stable. Our colleagues in Neurosurgery were consulted and a cerebral angiogram was performed but did not identify any pertinent vascular abnormalities. The patient due to initial presentation of seizure (likely secondary to temporoparietal bleed) was placed on Keppra 1000mg BID without any notable seizure events. He will continue this as an outpatient. The patient had his stroke risk factors evaluated, HBA1c WNL, and LDL of 136. He did not require starting of a statin as this has been shown to increase the risk of bleeding. The patient did have noticeable memory deficits on cognitive evaluation with occupational therapy. It has been recommended to the patient to schedule an appointment with Dr. ___ (___) in order to receive a full cognitive evaluation prior to returning to work. As to the etiology of the stroke, it is possible that is HTN related although the location is not necessarily specific for this. Patient will have a follow up MRI in about one month, and follow-up with Neurosurgery and Neurology to help delineate if there is another underlying lesion that was not identified on current studies. #ETOH: Per report from wife patient had been drinking up to 18 beers/day. Patient was placed on CIWA while in the unit and received only minimal doses. He clinically did not go into withdrawl. The CIWA was kept upon transfer to the floor but he did not require any BZD's. LFT's were WNL, with no transminitis, and liver synthetic function was normal. Patient was given thiamine, folic acid, and multivitamin while in the hospital. #HTN: Patient initially had goal SBP<160 with PRN hydralazine. He was on lotrel (5 amlodipine, 40 benezepril) at home. He had this restarted upon arrival to the floor and acheived good control with this. He will continue his home Lotrel as he received #Tobacco Use: Patient has been a lifelong smoker. We discussed that this was a risk factor for stroke. He was given a nicotine patch while in hospital. He will discuss cessation options (including welbutrin or chantix) with his PCP. Patient was given a prescription for nicotine patches. # Social issues: The patient's wife was uncomfortable coping before baseling and more worried after patient's husband's stroke. Social work was consulted and helped provide resources to Mr. ___ regarding alcohol cessation, in addition the patient's wife was given support resources as well. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: 1) Continue Keppra until follow up with Neurology (Dr. ___ 2) Repeat MRI in about 1 month, f/u with Nsurg 3) Continued monitoring of blood pressure control per PCP 4) Discussion of continued tobacco cessation with PCP ___ on ___: Lotrel (almodipine 5, benzepril 40)
summary: You were sent to the hospital after having had a seizure and a terrible headache. You were admitted to the Neurology service, and a scan was performed of your head that showed a bleed in the left side of your brain. While it is still unclear exactly what caused the bleed, the most likely cause is your high blood pressure. You had a study of your blood vessels of the brain which was reassuring, but did not help to reveal a potential cause for the bleed in your brain. Your seizure that you had was most likely due to the bleed in the brain. For this reason we are starting you on an anti-seizure medication known as Keppra.

We performed a thoracentesis to drain the fluid around your lung and a paracentesis to drain the fluid around the abdomen. You were seen by our pulmonologists to determine the cause of your low oxygen, but you wished to go home before the work-up was completed. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ patient with a past medical history of hypertension, hyperkalemia, muscular weakness, thyroid toxicity, recent left hemispheric stroke presenting as transfer due to worsening cerebral edema and left ___ nerve palsy.Original stroke caused by L ICA occlusion was on ___ per son. It is unclear why patient has malignant cerebral edema so long after initial infarction. Initially, it was thought possible that patient's hyponatremia may have prevented early herniation and patient is experiencing rebound edema. But patient had intervening sodium levels which were normal. Most likely explanation is that may be initial infarction was not complete and patient had further subacute infarction in the same vascular territories while at rehab which may not have been clinically apparent as patient already had aphasia and right hemiparesis. Patient had clinical and radiographic e/o uncal and subfalcine herniation and would have required decompressive hemi-crani. text: Brief Hospital Course: This is an ___ year old patient with a history of untreated ITP who sustained a mechanical fall and was found to have right hip and humerus fracture now s/p R TFN. . # R hip and humeral fracture: patient with mechanical fall and resultant hip and humerus fractures. Followed by orthopedics who recommended sling for R proximal humeral fracture and non-weight bearing, and surgery. In order to be safe for surgery, a platelet count >50 and hct >28 was required. Hematology was consulted regarding increasing plt count and anticoagulation in this patient with fracture and DVT risk but complicated by ITP as below, they recommended IVIG x2days (___) and prednisone 1mg/kg (40mg) daily. They endorsed initiation of standard anticoagulation once platelets were >50 and the pt was started on metoprolol 12.5mg BID to decrease ___ mortality. The pt was transfused to goal levels and on ___ underwent R hip TFN. patient subsequently had q8h CBC and was initially transfused to plts >50 and hct >25, with heparin sc TID given as DVT ppx. However, the pt's plts were incredibly unstable and would fluctuate from ___ to <10 over the course of several hours. Therefore, in discussion with heme and the pt it was decided that it is not safe to DVT prophylax patient's at present as the plts are consistently below 50 despite transfusion and adding heparin or lovenox onto this would represent a significant risk of hemorrhage which outweighs the risk of clot. The pt was made aware of these risks and agreed with the plan. Further it was decided to hold off on transfusions unless plts fall below 30 or pt has significant hct drop. After about 10 days post-op the hope is that the risk of bleeding will significantly decline and at that point the blood checks and transfusions will cease assuming the pt remains hemodynamically stable. The hematology team is also looking into the possibility of giving N-plate. The pt will be discharged to ___ where patient's blood counts will continue to be monitored as detailed below. patient will follow-up with hematology as an outpatient. . # ITP: patient has history of ITP previously treated with rare platelet transfusions and patient has declined treatment for ITP in the past. Platelet count was 8 on admission which improved to ___ s/p 1U platelets, then drifted down to 17. Heme/onc was consulted and patient was started on IVIG x2 days and prednisone 40mg daily with goal platelets >50 pre-operatively. After surgery patient's plts were initially transfused to goal of >50 in order to allow DVT ppx however given the instability of the plt levels patient was unable to continue ppx and instead was transfused to goal >30 in order to decrease risk of bleeding. patient will continue with transfusions until patient's hct is stable despite low plts. The pt received a total of 14 units of plts. . # Anemia: HCT of 19 on admission with unclear baseline. There was initially concern for development of hematoma given low platelets in setting of fracture and CT pelvis was done showing R gluteal hematoma. No evidence of hemolysis on labs. patient was transfused to goal hct >25 given cardiac risk factors and received a total of 6u RBCs during admission. At discharge patient's hct was 28. . # Leukocytosis: Likely related to fractures and stress response, possibly exacerbated by steroids. BCx were sent, u/a was clean, with ucx pending, CXR showed no evidence of infiltrate and surgical site looked clean and nonerythematous. No need for antibiotics now. Possibly response to plt and blood transfusions. . # Acute renal failure: Baseline ~1 with Cr 1.2 on admission, resolved after transfusions to 0.7. . # Incidental finding: CT with cystic structure within the pelvis. Can f/u as an outpt. . # HCP: ___ (sister) ___ . # Code: DNR/DNI . # Dispo: Pt will be dispoed to LTAC. . Dispo planning: The pt will be discharged to an LTAC with plt transfusion abilities. patient will have q8h CBCs through ___ ___ with goal plts >30 and goal hct >25. After ___ the patient will continue q8h CBC checks for one day without transfusing plts. If the hct drops greater than 3 points or there is evidence of active bleeding, then platelet transfusions will resume with goal of >30 for another 48h at which point stopping transfusions will again be attempted. If the pt's hct remains stable and the pt remains hemodynamically stable despite low plts then patient can have daily CBC checks instead. If the pt drops patient's hct >3 points or has evidence of bleed then q8h checks and transfusions of plts to >30 will again commense. If at some point the pt's plts stabilize >50 for 48h in absence of transfusion (which currently seems unlikely) DVT ppx should be initiated with heparin sc TID. After ___ patient's prednisone should beb tapered by 10mg every 3 days until it is off. The pt has required occasional doses of Lasix 10mg IV for pulmonary edema with transfusions (every few days). If patient becomes hypoxic or develops crackles, a dose of lasix should be considered. The pt will have follow-up with hematology and orthopedics.
summary: You were admitted for fall resulting in R hip fracture and R arm fracture. You had surgical repair of your R hip. You also have low plts and therefore required multiple transfusions to prevent bleeding. You are being sent to a facility that will continue to transfuse you as needed to prevent bleeding and you will continue to work with physical therapy to improve your mobility.

However, the patient was called after discharge to discontinue calcium/vit D due to hypercalcemia on discharge. patient completed seven days of ceftriaxone and five days of azithromycin for possible CAP. # Seronegative RA: Pt has been without flare of patient's disease since starting methotrexate in ___. patient's methotrexate was discontinued due to high suspicion for methotrexate-induced lung injury as above. patient was discharged on 60mg prednisone daily. A quantiferon gold was sent, given that the patient may need biologics to control patient's disease if methotrexate is no longer an option. Of note, AFB smear on BAL and CT chest were negative for TB. Continued nifedipine for Raynaud's. patient will follow up with rheumatology for further management. # Pseudogout: cont colchicine. # HTN: Normotensive here. Cont nifedipine and chlorthalidone. # CKD: Cr 1.8 which is approximately at baseline since ___. Etiology not known. Pt may not tolerate calcium supplementation due to likely secondary hyperparathyroidism from CKD. patient was called after discharge to discontinue calcium/vit D. summary: You came to the hospital because you had shortness of breath. We treated you with antibiotics for possible pneumonia. text: Brief Hospital Course: Mr. ___ is a ___ with PMH hep C cirrhosis and HCC s/p resection x 2 in ___, TACE x 2, incisional hernia repair, and evidence of disease progression on most recent imaging in ___ with plan for TACE ___ who presents from clinic with increased right lower chest/right upper quadrant pain, here for pain control and evaluation, found to have new t% lesion. . #. T5 lesion: The patient has imaging that shows a 5.3 x 3 x 3.2 cm mass that replaces the right posterior elements at T5 and causes marked canal narrowing with leftward deviation and compression of the spinal cord at this level. Given past imaging this appears to be a new lesion development. He was placed on dexamethasone. Remains neurologically intact at this time. Likely c/w metastatic HCC (esp given increasing AFP), although this is not a tumor that commonly goes to bone, so tissue Dx is important. Neurosurgery was uncomfortable doing large procedure given thrombocytopenia and need for HLA-matched plts. He was set up with radiation oncology appointment and will see them on ___ for palliative radiation to the lesion. #. Pain: Likely multi-factorial given known disease progression, mesh displacement from prior hernia surgery, and new met. Patient was started on patient contin 30mg TID with improvement in his pain regimen. He briefly had issues with AM delirium while on larger doses of narcotic, and this should be titrated by his oncologist. Palliative care was involved with care and helped titrate his medications. he was also uptitrated on gabapentin with good effect. #. Thrombocytopenia: Likely due to underlying liver disease. He had a incomplete bump in his platelet count yesterday from 16 to 23 following 1 unit of platelets. Fibrinogen 101, but pt has advance liver disease and may be under producing. No shictocytes on smear. Following transfusion of 1 unit of platetles only bumped 10. PRA was 15% (below the threashold of 20% but rather stongly reactive in the markers that were availible), based on further testing, Transfusion medicine would recommend HLA-matched plts as noted above, however he only had a small bump even with HLA matched platelets. #. Cogaulopathy: Likely due to underlying liver disease/nutritional status. Patient was given 5mg PO vitamin K x 5 days with good effect. He will likely remain coagulopathic in the future given his liver disease. #. Constipation: Was an issue on admission, but pt enorses he is moving bowels well on current regimen. He was continued on an aggressive bowel regimen and should continue this on discharge. #. Hypothyroidism: stable issue. -continue home levothyroxine #. Depression: stable issue. -continue home Lexapro #. Hep C cirrhosis: Mild varices on most recent EGD. Mild elevation in bili, otherwise LFTs unchanged. No encephalopathy, no edema. Likely his liver disease is the etiology of his cytopenias. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: #. Primary Oncologist should titrate pain medications and adjust for sedation as well as improvement in pain with radiation. #. Code status: Full Code #. Emergency contact: ___ (wife, ___

text: Brief Hospital Course: In summary, patient. ___ is a ___ yo F with longstanding SLE complicated in the past by nephritis, pericarditis and peritonitis, HTN, EtOH and substance abuse that was referred from rheumatologist office with 3 days of left sided neck pain and left sided jaw area swelling, CT imaging suggestive of parotitis. CT scan without evidence of abscess, however there was evidence of likely parotitis given note of nonspecific soft tissue stranding around patient's left parotid gland. No palpable stones on exam, but patient would only allow brief exam secondary to patient's pain, so limited assessment at times. Suppurative parotitis was a major concern as this can often suggest IV Abx management vs. oral therapy while patients stabilize. Parotitis is somewhat more common among collagen vascular disease patients and patient's SLE is a relative risk factor for this presentation unfortunately. We discussed imaging and case with general surgery and with ENT resident. No interventions were recommended as there were no focal collections on CT scan. You were treated with multiple medications to lower your blood pressure, and with peritoneal dialysis. Your shortness of breath resolved with treatment of your hypertension and specifically with a diuretic that caused you to excrete some of the excess fluid that has been retained by your body due to your kidney disease. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old left handed patient with history of squamous cell neck mass s/p XRT x2, HLD, GERD who presents as a transfer from ___ with history of TIA symptoms and MRA head/neck revealing significant bilateral carotid artery stenosis. Ten days ago, pt developed a constellation of neurological symptoms including a visual phenomena of blurred vision/seeing rainbows migrating from left eye to right eye in a horizontal line. Also, had tongue heaviness/slurred speech. Had numbness/tingling in left palm and left lateral aspect of the foot. Also developed a mild headache at symptom onset. patient has had these symptoms on and off for 10 days. Five days ago patient went to see patient's PCP who was concerned about stroke and started patient's on aspirin 81mg qd and referred patient's for MRI/A. MRI did not show an acute stroke, did show small vessel disease. MRA showed significant severe stenosis of the bilateral carotid arteries at the common carotid arteries and bifurcation/proximal internal carotid arteries bilaterally. CTA brain/neck also showed severe stenosis of the bilateral carotid arteries at the common carotid arteries and bifurcation/proximal internal carotid arteries bilaterally patient's neurological exam is normal with no evidence of objective weakness, numbness, or vision changes. Imaging as above. Suspect that the carotid stenosis is due to primarily radiation changes, but there was also a contribution from atherosclerosis. patient's symptoms sounded unlikely to be related to a stroke or TIA given the progression of the visual disturbances (first only affecting the left eye and then moving to the right eye) and the stereotyped nature of the events. It seemed to be more likely due to migraines. patient's description of tingling of the left foot seems more likely due to left sided radiculopathy (patient has a history of herniated disc on the left at L4/L5). The tingling of the left hand may possibly have been due to peripheral neuropathy. MRI showed no stroke. Carotid US was also obtained, which revealed ___ stenosis bilaterally at the common carotids, likely related to radiation changes and atherosclerosis. It is likely that the carotid ultrasound was not able to give an accurate estimation of stenosis at the ICA bifurcation and proximal ICA because flow was likely disturbed by the common carotid severe stenosis. This was felt to represent ASYMPTOMATIC stenosis given no evidence of stroke and low suspicion for TIA. On MRI, there were 2 small R frontal enhancing lesions seen on MRI of uncertain significance, the differential diagnosis is a small mass (but oddly without associated edema), vs a subacute stroke that is too old to show up on DWI or inflammatory lesion. Radiology recommended a repeat MRI brain in 2 months to follow up. Vascular surgery was consulted, and recommended outpatient follow up for consideration of possible stenting procedure in the future (they would not do a CEA given the prior h/o radiation exposure). Also, there will be significant risk associated with intubation for major surgery given stenotic changes in patient's throat after radiation, patient's previous doctor had warned patient's that intubation in the future will be extremely difficult and may be dangerous for patient. Thus, we will not rush into surgery at this time, but will have more discussions outpatient once MRI is obtained in 2 months time. Vascular surgery initially suggested considering ASA + plavix as antithrombotics. However, given that patient's stenosis is likely largely ___ radiation, and since patient just started aspirin 5 days prior, and has NOT had a stroke or TIA, we decided to control patient's stroke risk factors with an aspirin and statin for the time being. Statin was transitioned to a stronger medication (simva--> atorvastatin) to stabilize plaque, PCP should check fasting LDL as an outpatient. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES - F/U Neurology - Repeat MRI with and without contrast in 2 months to evaluate abnormal enhancing lesions - F/U Vascular Surgery - continue aspirin and statin - F/U with PCP - PCP should check fasting LDL, goal LDL is less than 70 (statin was increased to stabilize plaque inpatient)

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ with HTN and osteoporosis presenting with RLE pain concerning for nonresolving cellulitis s/p fall and ___. # Right Lower Extremity Hematoma: The patient presents to the emergency room with RLE pain and erythema with pain described as burning in nature. patient has had emergency room visits before, and imaging on patient's has revealed no acute fracture by x-ray, DVT U/S which have been negative x 2 on the RLE, as well as an MRI whose summary of patient's findings indicate that patient has extensive subcutaneous edema with laminar fluid collections overlying the leg fascia, more so laterally; fluid overlying the fascial hiatus for the superficial peroneal nerve in the distal leg may result in impingement of the cutaneous nerve , in addition to suggesting that there may be possible venous or lymphatic occlusion. Had several episodes of watery diarrhea concerning for steroid-refreactory progression of GVHD to gut involvement, but this remitted without intervention. patient was also treated with extracorporeal photopheresis three times/week and given topical steroids by dermatology. patient's rash markedly improved in distribution and intensity of erythema, but patient continued to complain that patient's skin was "hard" without significant improvement. Had switched from cyclosporin gtt to PO, but headache returned concerning for recucrrent CSA-associated headache which patient has previously experienced. Thus, patient was transitioned back to CSA gtt which patient will continue at home. #) IDDM: Pt BS elevated to 300 at time of admission, and very difficult to control during steroid therapy. ___ consulted and followed daily. Significant osmotic diuresis with resultant increase in Cr combatted by IV and PO fluids with resolution of ___. At time of discharge patient's SSI regimen consisted of 25 U NPH in the AM with patient's PO prednisone, 55 U Lantus QHS, and a comprehensive sliding scale with Humalog. patient is being discharged on a box each of Humalog pens, Lantus pens, and NPH pens. #) RUQ Pain: Admitted with moderate RUQ TTP. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ yo with metastatic small cell lung cancer who presents with change in patient, fever and seizeures who was found to have vasogenic edema. # Seizure: Intubated in ED for airway protection. MRI showed two previously known metastatic lesions. He was evaluated by neurology and started on levetiracetam, dexamethasone, and phenytoin. He was also evaluated by radiation oncology. Dilantin was tapered off as Keppra was increased, and he is being discharged on Keppra and Decadon alone. If his steroids are to be continued long-term, he should be started on Ca/Vit D/Bisphosphonate/Bactrim. PPI continued at discharge but can be discontinued when steroids are stopped. The patient was instructed that he should not drive until he has been seizure-free for 6 months. # Fever: Initial concern for aspiration pneumonia vs. ventilator associated pneumonia. Multiple chest X-rays showed no evidence of infection and antibiotics were stopped. He had no fevers while on the general medicine floor. # Shortness of breath: Patient had an acute episode of shortness of breath on ___ after being laid flat for removal of a central line. He improved with supportive care alone. Chest CTA showed no evidence of emboli or infiltrates, but did show small bilateral pleural effusions, likely related to volume resuscitation in the ICU. Patient improved and had oxygen saturations of 97-99% on room air.

You had a chest CT which showed no evidence of infection or clot.

text: Brief Hospital Course: REASON FOR HOSPITALIZATION: ___ F pmhx jejunal intussuseption s/p ex. laparoscopy p/w recurrent abdominal pain thought to be due to celiac disease with intermittent intussusception. # ? CELIAC DISEASE/ABDOMINAL PAIN: The patient's abdominal pain was felt to be due to Celiac Disease with possible intermittent jejunal intussusception and overlying constipation. patient's prior biopsies showed villous atrophy, which is consistent with Celiac Disease. Surgery & GI evaluated the patient during hospitalization given patient's prior history of intussusception. TTG & anti-DGP were checked on admission, but resulted negative (in the setting of adhering to a gluten-free diet over the past month). During admission, patient had an acute episode of severe R lower quadrant abdominal pain associated with development of a firm, mass-like structure in the same area. patient was taken for a CT scan which did not reveal any abnormal findings. This episode was possibly due to intermittent jejunal intussusception. The acute surgery service did not feel there was an indication for surgical intervention. patient's small bowel enteroscopy from prior admission showed an area of small intestine edema and inflammation. patient was also noted to be significantly constipated during admission due to poor PO intake and opioid pain medication, which was felt to be exacerbating patient's intestinal process. With an aggressive bowel regimen, patient's pain was significantly improved. GI will consider enterocort if patient's abdominal pain reccurs. It is possible that patient will have another recurrence of jejunal intussusception. patient will continue on a gluten-free diet until learning the results of patient's HLA tests during patient's follow up with GI. # CONSTIPATION: The patient has not had normal bowel movements since first developing patient's abdominal pain. This was thought to be due to poor nutrition, dehydration, and opioid pain medication use. An aggressive bowel regimen was successful in relieving patient's constipation. patient was advised to avoid opioid pain medications. patient was discharged on a bowel regimen of Miralax & Bisacodyl. # FOLLOW UP: The patient will follow up with GI and nutrition as an outpatient.
summary: You came to the hospital with recurrent abdominal pain. While you were here we had our surgery and gastroenterology teams evaluate you. Ultimately, it was felt that you pain was due to possible Celiac Disease with severe constipation. It is also possible that you had another temporary intususseption while you were here, which can happen during a flare of Celiac Disease. We treated your symptoms and your pain improved with resolution of your constipation. You will need to take medications to ensure you are having normal bowel movements.

text: Brief Hospital Course: In summary this is a very nice ___ patient with history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease who presents with worsening shortness of breath and new thrombocytopenia. # Thrombocytopenia: In general causes are broken down into decreased production or increased destruction of platelets. Decreased production is typically associated with a decrease in multiple cell lines which is not the case here. The differential for increased destruction includes ITP, DIC, TTP, and heparin induced. Per Heme onc the periperal smear was without platelet clumping or schitzocytes and patient has not had known exposure to heparin. Therefore ITP is the likely diagnosis. The patient was treated initially with IVIG and prednisone, dosed at 1 mg/kg; patient also received one unit of platelets. The IVIG was stopped on the first hospital day when patient's platelets increased to near 100. Prednisone was continued at 1 mg/kg for one week, after which it was tapered per hematology at a rate of a decrease of 20mg every week. Patient has been started on vitamin D and calcium for bone health; in addition, patient has been started on Inhaled pentamidine once every month for PCP ___. patient should follow-up with a Dr. ___ at ___ on ___. An appointment has been scheduled. It is very important that patient return to this clinic for monitoring of patient's ITP and further tapering of patient's prednisone. # Shortness of breath: Many possible etiologies were originally considered including edema in the setting of underlying interstitual lung disease. However the physical exam is without signs of volume overload and the BNP is normal. patient's ECHO showed an EF>55% without significant dysfunction. The abrupt onset of SOB also suggested PE, and even though patient was not tachycardic we did find a subsegmental PE on CHEST CT. Patient was treated with prednisone, as above, in addition to levofloxacin for community-acquired pneumonia (course now completed) and standing bronchodilator nebulizers. With these treatments, patient's symptoms improved. patient was discharge with 4L NC with 93%sat level. With respect to pulmonary edema, patient was diuresed initially with intravenous Lasix and was quickly switched back to patient ___ dose of 40 mg daily orally. However, patient's lasix was stopped prior to discharge given a slight rise in creatitine. patient was not discharged on Lasix but patient's volume status needs to be monitored. . #PE : the Pt was found to have subsegmental PE on CHEST-CT. Pulmonary consult was also asked to comment on this finding. Given the very low pretest probablity of clot as well as the many contraindications to anticoagulation (hemoptysis, recent ITP), the risks and benefits of anticoagulation versus close monitoring was discussed with the patient and patient's daughter. Ultimately, it was felt that risks of anticoagulation outweighed any benefits especially given negative bilateral ___ u/s. Through discussion with patient's health proxy (daughter), we also elected not to place an IVC filter. It is important that patient receive follow-up lower extremity dopplers to evaluate possible clot burden in 1 week (___) and anticoagulated if further clots are found. . # Hemoptysis: during patient's hosptial stay, patient was noted to have mild occasional hemptysis (streaks and dime sized) dark maroon blood. Pulmonary consult felt that this was old blood likely from when patient's platelets were extremely low. patient remained hemodynamically stable with no signs of significant blood loss. patient's hypoxia improved gradually as well. Chest CT revealed no evidence of malignancy. patient should have pulmonary follow-up in the next month. . # Gastroesophageal reflux disease: we continued patient ___ omeprazole. # Hyperlipidemia: we continued patient ___ atorvastatin. # Code status: patient's code status is full code. text: Brief Hospital Course: Summary Statement ================== ___ w/ T2DM, and high grade DLBCL, now who presented on C2D12 of da-EPOCH, with C1 c/b jejunal enteritis, febrile neutropenia, hyponatremia, presyncope, who presented with febrile neutropenia and was found to have pneumonia which was treated with broad spectrum abx. # Febrile Neutropenia # PNA The patient presented from clinic with fevers of 101 without a clear etiology and ANC of 20. The patient subsequently developed a non-productive cough. Additional workup consisting of CT abdomen, influenza pcr and respiratory viral panel were negative. patient had no central lines or foreign bodies. The patient was started on meropenem and Vanc given patient's allergy to penicillin. Given the finding of neutropenia the started on Neupogen and patient's counts recovered. text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ year-old right handed patient with a history of multiple myeloma who presented to the ED in the setting of unilateral periorbital edema and headache. patient reported sensation of swelling of the left eye, right-sided hip and back pain, midline neck pain, and diffuse headache and photophobia during further questioning the next morning after admission to the neurology service. On examination patient had tenderness to palpation of the left temporal region and occipital notches. patient's strength appeared symmetric but effort-limited. patient had no proptosis or exophthalmos, no Horner's, no change in visual accuity or extraoccular movements, no eye congestion or erythema. patient had no meningismus and no ocular or cranial bruits. patient's CT head showed a calcified lesion in the falx, likely a meningioma. As patient has had a two-week history of right buttock pain with rest and ambulation, patient also underwent an x-ray of the hip and pelvis, although patient described this pain as different than patient's lytic pain patient has had in the past. Imaging was unrevealing. patient was treated with ketoralac and antihistamines with some relief and will be discharged with tramadol as well as a low-dose muscle relaxant and was encouraged to continue ibuprofen 600 mg tid prn for pain. Given patient's reassuring examination, it was decided to defer any further work-up at this time. However, patient will follow up with neurology as an outpatient and contact us should any new symptoms occur.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ with a complicated pulmonary hx including hx asthma, TBM s/p tracheobronchoplasty x3, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, as well as factor V Leiden, and anxiety who presented for EGD under MAC with procedure largely uncomplicated, until the end when patient developed acute respiratory distress. No significant hypoxia or evidence of bronchospasm was noted on exam. patient was started on a precedex gtt and BIPAP ___ (patient's regular setting) and subjectively improved with precedex gtt. patient was taken off BiPAP given patient's improvement but then again had subjective feelings of breathlessness and dyspnea. patient was put back on BiPAP and given Haldol 2.5mg x1 for agitation which made patient's more anxious. patient was then given Ativan 1mg IV and patient's home trazodone 200mg which helped with patient's anxiety. patient subsequently came off of BiPAP and was transferred to the floor. Overnight, patient maintained patient's sats within normal limits on RA and had no difficulty breathing prior to discharge. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES =================== [ ] EGD pursued given report of dysphagia, vomiting, and weight loss. EGD showed normal mucosa throughout but biopsies were taken and need to be followed [ ] Anticoagulation plan: Confirmed with patient's PCP's office. patient is to take 12 mg Coumadin daily until patient follows up with patient's PCP in one week. PCP to make adjustments at patient's follow-up visit
summary: You were hospitalized at ___ after undergoing an endoscopy with the GI team. When you were waking up from the anesthesia, you were noted to have difficulty breathing. You were required a short use of BiPAP but otherwise your breathing improved overnight. Labs and imaging do not reveal a concerning feature to your abnormal breathing episode and you are safe for discharge at this time.

text: Brief Hospital Course: SUMMARY: ======== patient. ___ is a ___ patient with a past medical history of morbid obesity s/p Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (___) c/b mild GJ anastomosis stricture s/p multiple dilations (last ___, CVA, ?vascular dementia, DM2 c/b DKA, hypothyroidism, polysubstance use disorder (benzos, opioids), and pernicious anemia who presented on transfer from ___ following an episode of possible syncope and persistent hypotension requiring pressors and MICU admission despite initial fluid resuscitation. The cause of this episode was most likely the patient's ongoing malnutrition and inability to tolerate poor PO intake with possible contribution of polypharmacy with reports of patient taking medications not prescribed to patient's or listed in ___. Notably, patient was not hypoglycemic during the episode, there was no evidence of acute stroke on CT and MRI, and cortisol and TSH were normal. patient was initially admitted to MICU for levophed requirement, but patient's hypotension quickly resolved. patient remained normotensive with no further syncopal episodes. Neurology was consulted, determined that there was no seizure activity and that anti-epileptic drugs were not indicated. Given n/v, anxiety with PO intake, GI was consulted, recommended transfer to ___ for continuity of care (which was declined due to no bed availability), performed EGD dilation of known GJ anastamosis stricture (___). Subsequently, small bowel follow-through study was performed per patient's outpatient ___ GI team's recommendation, showed no obstruction but was limited. Metoclopramide was also trialed for gastroparesis, with symptomatic improvement, increased PO intake, resolution of emesis. ACUTE ISSUES: ============= #Hypotension Patient was admitted to the MICU given hypotension to SBP ___ that did not initially respond to fluid resuscitation (5L). patient briefly required Levophed on the morning of admission, quickly weaned off. Initial etiologies considered included PE (without hypoxia), adrenal insufficiency (no recent steroid use), infection (briefly on empiric antibiotics but afebrile, no localizing symptoms, negative workup), hypovolemia. Of note, patient with prior encounters at OSH where patient required IVF for hypotension thought secondary to poor PO intake. patient did have an elevated lactate to 4.2 which improved to normal range with fluid resuscitation. TSH and cortisol were wnl. TTE was reassuring. Ultimately, suspected hypotension most likely the result of significant decrease in PO intake with ongoing emesis as well as likely contribution of polypharmacy, similar to prior presentations at ___. Of note, patient with numerous notes from ___ neurology group stating concern for medication misuse, which is consistent with below account from patient's daughter. Previously orthostatic despite extensive fluid resuscitation, so autonomic dysfunction secondary to poorly managed diabetes is also possible though HgbA1c this admission is 8.4. However, orthostasis resolved with administration of additional IVF. #Nausea #Vomiting #Poor PO intake #Malnutrition #GJ anastomosis stricture #Marginal ulcer: resolved Patient with history of Roux-en-Y bypass with close GI outpatient care through ___. Per ___ GI, patient has a longstanding history of nausea and vomiting following PO intake believed to be due to GJ anastomosis stricture iso Roux-en-Y bypass c/b marginal ulcer (for which PPI BID was prescribed). Stricture has been dilated multiple times this year, most recently on ___. Patient continued to have nausea and vomiting despite these procedures. Patient underwent GJ stricture dilation on ___ without complication, which showed that previously noted marginal ulcer had resolved. Patient initiated on regular diet with good appetite but with multiple episodes emesis post-initiation. Given ongoing inability to tolerate PO intake, ___ study was ordered to evaluate for strictures distal to GJ junction and other abnormalities. SBFT showed known focal narrowing at GJ junction without obstruction. Of note, study was limited as the jejunojejunostomy could not be clearly identified iso poor patient tolerance of oral contrast. Gastroparesis was also considered given history of poorly controlled diabetes, and metoclopramide was trialed with significant improvement. On day of discharge, patient was tolerating regular diet and had moderate improvement in nausea, no emesis. patient will follow outpatient with patient's GI providers at ___. #Syncope On admission, patient reported episode of syncope thought secondary to longstanding poor nutrition and possible severe dehydration as below, though medication misuse as above could also be contributing. Patient reported no prodromal symptoms, TTE/EKG exonerated cardiogenic causes, unlikely neurogenic given no post-ictal state or history of seizures. Initial account of original episode was concerning for seizures, but conversations with husband involved descriptions that seem more consistent with syncope with no convulsions. However, he does report one episode of the patient lying in bed shaking about 2 weeks prior to this admission. Neurology was consulted and an EEG was performed, with no evidence of seizures and no recommendation for initiating anti-epileptic drugs at this time. Previous CVA and balance issues (possibly ___ peripheral neuropathy) make CVA or TIA possible, though CT head at ___ reportedly showed no evidence of acute stroke which was confirmed on MRI. Patient had no evidence of arrhythmia on telemetry during this admission. #Opioid/Benzo use #Concern for medication misuse, polypharmacy Concerns for polypharmacy raised by previous providers given behavioral affect at appointments. Concern for episode of agitation following benzodiazepine administration for anxiety coincided with report of husband bringing in brown paper bag. Room search performed without any findings, and tox screen was negative. Call with daughter, ___, reported that patient has been receiving Percocet from patient's husband, which he obtains from an unclear source ("friend") who is not a prescriber. Patient and patient's husband were educated on the adverse side effects of these medications. Specifically, hypotension and GI slowing. Both patient and husband expressed understanding of this and wished to proceed with alternative interventions to address pain. MassPMP checked and found no recent rx for opioids or benzos. #Severe protein calorie malnutrition Nutrition consult recommended additional testing for vitamin and trace mineral deficiencies. Vitamins A/D/E, zinc, copper, ceruloplasmin, selenium, and manganese levels should be checked by outpatient GI providers. Started thiamine 100 mg daily. Nutrition recommended alternative means of obtaining nutrition. However, patient has refused this in the past and would require placement by surgical specialists given complex/altered anatomy iso prior Roux-en-Y bypass. Patient continued to be adamantly against feeding tube during this hospitalization. Followup outpatient GI as above. #Possible refeeding syndrome Hypophosphatemia, Hypomagnesemia, thought related to refeeding syndrome. Improved s/p repletion. Patient should continue taking home magnesium oxide as magnesium intermittently required repletion here. Electrolytes should be monitored at rehab, with repeat BMP on ___. #Hyperkalemia K 6.2 on admission to OSH, received D50/10units IV insulin. K 4.8 in ___. CHRONIC ISSUES: =============== #Progressive cognitive decline #Memory issues Previous notes from PCP in ___ system indicate that this is thought to be related to vascular dementia. TSH and B12 normal. Per ___ records, this has been going on since at least ___, at which time patient and husband reported that symptoms had already persisted for around ___ year. Neuro was consulted and stated that exam was largely consistent with exam documented ___. MRI was obtained and showed nonspecific white matter changes in the cerebral hemispheres bilaterally, likely a sequela of chronic microangiopathy. Neurology felt picture in line with vascular dementia and will plan for outpatient follow up. Likely that medications are contributing as well. #Anemia #Low ferritin Normocytic. Thought to ___ given poor PO intake and ferritin <100. Now s/p ferric gluconate 125 mg IV daily x 3 days. Iron levels should be checked in ___ weeks with repeat iron supplementation as needed. #Diabetes #Peripheral neuropathy Takes 20U glargine at home with ISS per husband, but 15U per PCP and ___ med lists. HbA1c at 8.4 on ___, down from 9.2 in ___. Lipids normal. Blood glucose labile during this admission. Continued ISS, glargine at likely reduced dose of 10U daily. Continued home gabapentin 300 BID. #Depression #Anxiety Continued home buspirone. Of note, patient did request benzodiazepine due to significant anxiety during this hospitalization. However, in contrast to patient report, patient does not appear to carry an active prescription for this and demonstrated a likely paradoxical reaction to this medication. Patient's anxiety was well controlled with hydroxyzine, which was continued on discharge. #Hypothyroidism Thyroid function tests normal here. Continued home levothyroxine. #Hypertension: Held home Lisinopril in the setting of hypotension. #Asthma Continued home albuterol PRN. Ipratropium-albuterol neb q6h PRN for dyspnea in house. #Insomnia QTc normal here. Received trazodone 100 mg PO qHS PRN - half home dose. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: ==================== [] Patient with electrolyte abnormalities this admission. BMP should be checked on ___. [] Glargine was reduced to 10U daily from reported home dose of 20U daily due to blood glucose levels during this admission. Continue to titrate. [] Patient does not have any active prescriptions for benzodiazepines and had a likely paradoxical reaction to lorazepam during this admission during which patient became very agitated. Please avoid administering any benzodiazepines. Hydroxyzine manages patient's anxiety effectively. [] Home lisinopril was held in the setting of hypotension. [] Home trazodone dose was reduced to 100 mg from 200 mg. Caution increasing given ongoing confusion. [] Metoclopramide 5 mg PO before meals was started to treat possible gastroparesis. The patient should continue taking this medication after discharge. QTc <400 during this hospitalization. Should be monitored if patient continues to take this medication regularly given patient is on multiple QTc prolonging medications (including Ondansetron as below). Recommend no longer than 12 week trial. [] Ondansetron ODT 4 mg PO Q8H:PRN, ranitidine 150 mg PO BID:PRN, and simethicone 40-80 mg PO QID:PRN started to help manage the patient's nausea, dyspepsia, and gas pain. [] The patient's home multivitamin was switched to a chewable version per nutrition's recommendations. [] The patient should follow-up with outpatient GI providers regarding ongoing nutritional deficiencies. Nutrition consult recommended checking vitamins A/D/E, zinc, copper, ceruloplasmin, selenium, and manganese, which should be done at the next outpatient visit. Additionally, the patient's ongoing difficulties with taking in adequate PO should be addressed in this setting. [] Iron: recheck in ___ weeks, received IV in house. [] Please refer to neurologist as an outpatient for management of cognitive decline and chronic microangiopathy. #CODE STATUS: Full confirmed #EMERGENCY CONTACT: Next of Kin: ___ Relationship: ___ Phone: ___ Other Phone: ___
summary: You lost consciousness and were unresponsive at home. You were found to have dangerously low blood pressure. You were given fluids and medications in the ICU to help increase your blood pressure to make sure that blood could get to all of your organs. You had imaging of your brain to rule out a stroke, which showed no new stroke in your brain. The neurologists saw you. They monitored the electrical activity in your brain to rule out a seizure, and there was no evidence of seizure. You had nausea and vomiting, so the gastroenterologists saw you in the hospital. You had an endoscopy and a repeat dilation of the known narrowing where your intestine connects to your stomach. However, you continued to vomit after eating food. You started on a new medication, metoclopramide (Reglan) to help with the slow emptying of your stomach. This seemed to improve your nausea and vomiting. You had a small bowel follow-through study, which showed known narrowing of the same area we knew about. This is the area we dilated in the hospital. Of note, study was limited because you had a difficult time with the oral contrast.

Your primary care doctor ___ recheck your sodium at your next visit.

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ year old f with a history of alcohol abuse (endorses withdrawal seizures, and possible delirium tremens), prior episodes of alcoholic gastritis, who presented to the ED intoxicated with reports of hematemesis, and had moderate to severe withdrawal during the hospital course. ACTIVE ISSUES: ============== # Alcoholism/Alcohol withdrawal: Patient has history of alcohol abuse and recent relapse in the setting of significant social stressor (patient's son's death). ___ a history of withdrawal seizures, unclear if patient has had delirium tremens in the past. Patient had a mild transaminitis on admission that resolved on hospital day 2. patient also started actively withdrawing on hospital day 2 and treated with a diazepam CIWA scale. patient's withdrawal was moderate to severe, complicated by fever and tachycardia, which gradually abated. Multivitamins, thiamine, folate were also given. patient was connected with social work and helped to set up outpatient services at ___ for EtOH cessation. Further counseling provided by team and Chaplain services with regards to grieving patient's son's death, which was the major trigger for patient's drinking. # Fever, Tachycardia: On hospital day 3, patient had fever and tachycardia in the absence of any identified source of infection - both UA and CXR were negative and patient had no leukocytosis. UCx did grow E. coli, but only in ___ colony counts, and the patient reported longstanding dysuria for the past year that was not substantially different, so this was difficult to interpret. Ultimately, patient did receive 3 days of antibiosis with Ceftriaxone. patient's fever did not recur and was ultimately attributed to autonomic instability in the setting moderate to severe withdrawal. Patient improved with treatment of patient's alcohol withdrawal. # Elevated Lactate: Patient had lactate of 5.5 on admission in the setting of EtOH intoxication and hypovolemia from vomiting. Lactate trended down to 2.7, but on hospital day 3 patient's lactate bumped again to 4.2 in the setting of fever and tachycardia - this downtrended down to 2.2 the next day with holding albuterol. There was no clear etiology of the elevated lactate as patient remained without evidence of ischemia of the bowel, sepsis or other tissue hypoperfusion. patient's BPs remained within normal limits. # Bronchitis: Patient had a moderate cough during patient's hospital stay. The cough was productive of clear phlegm. patient had wheezing on exam but no oxygen requirement. No pneumonia or pulmonary edema identified on CXR and a BNP of 251 was reassuring that patient was not significantly volume overlaoded. Symptoms were thought to be due to a viral bronchitis and treated with nebulizers and codeine/guaifenesin. # Alcoholic gastritis Patient presented after reporting one episode of hematemesis with a small amount of blood but had no episodes during patient's hospital stay. patient had no evidence for continued upper GI bleed as Hct and Hgb remained stable. Hematemesis attributed to ___ tear vs. gastritis in the setting of vomiting. patient has no history of liver disease, and EGD in ___ was without varices. Patient was treated with IV PPI and carafate and no further bleeding was identified. patient also had 2 days of loose BM and 1 episode of melena without evidence for ongoing GI bleed. CT Abdomen pelvis was negative for acute pathology. C. Diff was negative. There was no evidence of bowel infarction and patient remained with a normal WBC. The abdominal pain was likely gastritis associated with ETOH use. patient improved with the PPI, carafate and treatment of patient's withdrawal. # Red L eye: patient had a red left eye consistent with subconjuctival hemorrhage, thought to be due to coughing. CHRONIC ISSUES: =============== # Chronic Pain Continued gabapentin with holding parameters # HTN Continued amlodipine # Bipolar Disorder continued divalproex # Depression continued sertraline # HLD Continued lipitor TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: =================== - History of alcohol abuse, withdrawal seizures and DTs. Patient agreeable to outpatient services, which patient set up in conjunction with social work - patient will start counseling at ___ for EtOH cessation. - Patient with cough and wheeze on exam felt likely due to bronchitis. patient was discharged home with an albuterol inhaler for symptomatic relief. If patient's symptoms persist, patient should have pulmonary function testing and be evaluated for asthma. - Due to reported hematemesis and one questionably melenic bowel movement, patient was discharged home on acid-suppressive therapy with a high-dose PPI for 1 month. patient should follow-up with GI if patient's symptoms persist.
summary: You were admitted for alcohol intoxication and vomiting a small amount of blood. We think the blood in your vomit came from irritation of the stomach from alcohol. We treated you with medications to help the lining of the stomach heal, and your pain improved. During this hospitalization, you had moderately severe withdrawal symptoms. This is a potentially life-threatening condition, and it is critical that you continue your efforts to stay sober. We treated your withdrawal symptoms with medications, and your symptoms subsided. Also during this hospitalization, you had a lot of cough and wheezing that we think was due to bronchitis. We looked for evidence of pneumonia and did not find any. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old patient with lupus, HTN, substance abuse, neuropathy, s/p CVA, depression and anemia presenting to ED with lower abdominal pain for 3 days found to have evidence of vasculitis and lupus enteropathy on CT. Rheumatology recommended prednisone taper starting at 60mg. Rash: Started prior to hospitalization. It may be a manifestation of vasculitis, other lupus symptoms, or allergy. Patient was started on Sarna lotion. Over course of hospitalization, rash resolved. 3. Hypertension - Patient was continued on home lisinopril but had several episodes of hypertension in the setting of pain. hydrochlorothiaze 25mg daily and nadolol 20mg daily were added to control patient's pressures. 4. Substance abuse: c/b neuropathy due to alcoholism and poor nutrition. On narcotics contract as outpatient. Pleural fluid culture grew ESBL klebsiella, enterococcus, and ___ albicans. patient's antimicrobial regimen was changed to vancomycin, meropenem, and caspofungin. Caspofungin was changed to fluconazole after 6 days based on sensitivity data. Cytology was negative for malignant cells but was a degenerated specimen. The pigtail catheter was changed to a pneumostat prior to discharge. The patient has scheduled follow up with thoracic surgery and ID the week following discharge. . #Cystitis - ___ species isolated from prior urine cultures dated ___ and ___ were refractory to voriconazole and amphotericin bladder washes during prior hospitalizations. During this admission patient completed a 7 day course of amphotericin IV. patient was also treated with a 7 day course of levofloxacin for bacterial cystitis based on urine cultures growing enterococcus and proteus species. patient's dysuria was relieved with pyridium and urinary frequency and bladder spasm improved with oxybutinin. . #PE - Incidental note was made of a PE in a segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery, the vessel going to the retained superior segment left lower lobe status post left lower lobe composite basilar segmentectomy on ___. Bilateral lower extremity doppler ultrasound was negative for DVT. The patient, the primary medical team, and the thoracic surgery team decided to defer anticoagulation due to the absence of symptoms, the inherent risks of anticoagulation particularly in light of patient's initial presentation of gross hematuria, and the atypical eccentric radiographic appearance of the clot and its proximity to the surgical site. . #Hematuria - The patient underwent cystoscopy, clot evacuation, fulguration, and bladder biopsy. patient's hematuria resolved after the procedure. Cytology was negative for malignant cells or fungal elements. The pathology from the bladder biopsy revealed edema, vascular congestion, hemorrhage and acute and chronic inflammation with scattered eosinophils. GMS and PAS-D fungal stains were negative. . #Anemia - Transfused 2 units PRBC for Hct 23% on ___ and 1 U PRBC on ___ for Hct 24.3%. text: Brief Hospital Course: Primary Reason for Admission: ___ year old patient with a past medical history of psoriatic arthritis on infliximab, methotrexate, and prednisone presenting with fevers, now with persistent hypoxemia. Active Diagnoses: # Hyoxemia/Fevers: The source of the pt's fever was suspected to be the lungs, as patient was hypoxemic. The differential diagnosis was infectious (PCP, ___, EBV, community acquired PNA), PE, volume overload, or rheumatologic. However, patient's imaging studies were more consistent with mild volume overload than infection or PE. There were questionable foci of GGO on chest CT, and the ID team recommend empiric treatment for PCP given patient's hx of immunosuppression. patient was put on Bactrim and prednisone. In the MICU, patient was also diuresed with IV lasix 20mg BID due to the appearance of volume overload on repeat CXR. It was after receiving both of these therapies that patient's hypoxemia improved, so it was unclear what patient was actually responding to. patient had an ECHO which showed normal systolic function and no hypertrophy, although diastolic HF is still possible given the 1L bolus NS patient received in the ED. As patient's hypoxemia continued to improve and patient remained afebrile, ID re-examined patient. All teams agreed that suspicion for PCP was low, and patient's bactrim and prednisone were discontinued (continued on home dose of prednisone). Lasix was stopped when patient appeared euvolemic. patient's clinical status improved, and we felt it was safe to discharge patient. All of patient's cultures came back negative, so the infectious source is still unclear. We advised patient's to call patient's PCP or the ___ clinic if patient's fevers return. # Hypotension: The pt's BP fluctuated throughout the beginning of patient's stay, and patient's family reports that this is typical. patient had an incidence of SBP to the ___, but was asymptomatic. We held patient's home Imdur and valsartan, and patient remained hemodynamically stable. IVFs were held for possible pulmonary edema. patient was normotensive upon discharge, and instructed to follow up with patient's cardiologist as soon as possible to adjust patient's medications. # Coag negative staph aureus blood culture: The pt had one blood culture positive for coat negative staph shortly after admission. Although most likely a contaminant, the ID team recommended patient be started on vanc given patient's immunosuppression. patient was on vanc for 3 days, when it appeared patient was having Red Man Syndrome. After discussing the likelihood of contamination versus true infection, it was decided to stop vanc rather than continue at a slower infusion rate. Vanc was stopped, and patient's fever did not return. Suspicion for blood stream infection was low. # Cough: On the last few days of patient's stay, the pt complained of a dry scratchy cough and squeezing sensation in patient's throat. Although the cough may have been related to patient's hypoxemia/fever, it appeared most consistent with GERD, and patient has a history of ___ esophagus. We continued patient's home PPI. If patient's symptoms continue, patient should probably have follow up with GI or perhaps repeat endoscopy. Chronic Diagnoses: # Psoriatic arthritis: patient continued to complain of joint pain throughout patient's hospitalization. We managed patient's pain with patient's home medications. patient missed patient's infliximab dose, and we advised patient's to skip the next methotrexate dose given patient's recent fevers. We discharged patient's on patient's home dose of prednisone, 2.5mg daily. text: Brief Hospital Course: Brief Hospital Course By Problem: Patient is a ___ year old patient with a PMH significant for DM, HTN, and RAD who presented with symptoms of fatigue and nausea, found to have ___ anion gap metabolic acidosis, hyperkalemia, bradycardia, hypotension and ___, who was initially admitted to the MICU for management of patient's multiple medical problems. . #) Anion gap metabolic acidosis: at the time of admission, patient had been complaining of fatigue for ___ days prior to presentation, it was unclear if the fatigue and malaise was due to a possible infection given left shift on differential. The initial concern was that patient's overall fatigue and malaise led to decreased po intake causing dehydration, which caused poor perfusion and lactate production. On admission patient's lactate was found to be 5.5, patient was aggressively volume resuscitated with 4L of NS in the ER and over the next day patient's lactate decreased to 2.1 then to 1.7, and patient's anion gap closed. The lactic acidosis was also likely exacerbated by continued administration of metformin prior to patient's presentation to the hospital. patient's chestx-ray had shown a possible RLL PNA, so patient was empirically treated with levaquin. After closure of patient's initial anion gap, symptomatically patient felt much better, and was able to tolerate po intake and maintain hydration without further IV fluid supplementation. . #) Bradycardia: on presentation to the ER patient had ___ episode of bradycardia, with a HR in the 40's for about one hour. The EKG looked like it was junctional, and patient's potassium was found to be 5.9, peaked at 6.8, which was thought to be the likely cause. The initial episode resolved, patient was monitored on telemetry with no further episodes of bradycardia. . #) Hypotension: on admission found to have systolic blood pressures in the 80's to 90's, patient's blood pressure responded to aggressive fluid resuscitation, and patient's outpatient medications were held. During patient's hospital stay, patient's blood pressure medications continued to be held, and at the time of discharge no anti-hypertensives had been restarted as patient's SBP's had been mostly in the 120's to 130's. On discharge patient's daughter was instructed to check patient's mother's blood pressure daily and if the SBP was greater than 140, patient should restart patient's enalapril. patient was also scheduled for outpatient follow up with patient's PCP for further BP medication titration. . #) Hyperkalemia: on admission, found to have K=5.9 which then increased and peaked at 6.8. Thought to be due to decreased po intake leading to ___ with concurrent ACEi administration. Potassium normalized the morning of ___, and remained in the normal range for the remainder of patient's hospitalization, as patient's renal function improved. patient's potassium was 4.5 on discharge. . #) SOB/Wheezing: patient initially complained of shortness of breath, which was thought to be due to patient's longstanding reactive airway disease, especially since patient had recently been told by patient's PCP to decrease patient's albuterol neb use. Initial chest x-ray concerning for a possible pneumonia, so patient was started on a 7 day course of levaquin, patient's sputum culture was contaminated, blood cultures with no growth to date. patient also received albuterol and atrovent nebs every 4 hours as needed with improvement in patient's respiratory symptoms. There was also concern for a possible cardiac source of SOB, as patient had a ___ enlarged heart with mild pulmonary edema on chest x-ray, so patient ___ echocardiogram (full report above), that was concerning for ___ infiltrative process, and was set up with outpatient follow up. . #) Troponin Leak: troponins were checked on ___, found to be 0.18, cardiology was consulted who felt that since the EKG did not have any significant changes, it was likely demand ischemia in setting of hypovolemia. Also, they felt that patient's current acute kidney injury was contributing to the elevated troponin. Troponins trended down over the next 2 days. A fasting lipid panel was checked, patient was started on ___ 81mg aspirin, patient's pravastatin was to be restarted on discharge after patient's transminases normalized. ___ echocardiogram was done to further assess the function of patient's heart, and it showed ___ ___, with concern for ___ infiltrative process particularly amyloid, so ___ SPEP was sent, and patient was set up with outpatient cardiology follow up. . #) ___: patient with baseline Cr=1.5, on admission found to have Cr of 2.1, patient's creatinine improved quickly with hydration, making the cause likely prerenal, due to decreased po intake and dehydration. On discharge patient's creatinine was 1.2, which was lower than patient's prior baseline measurements. . #) Diabetes Mellitus Type II: initial hyperglycemia to the 400's on admission, sugars also decreased with IV fluid resuscitation. patient's oral medications were discontinued on admission and patient was started on a humalog sliding scale. With reintroduction of a diabetic diet, patient's blood sugars ranged between 140's to 190's. patient's glipizide was restarted the day prior to discharge, but patient's metformin was discontiued and not restarted given patient's recent lactic acidosis and baseline creatinine in the 1.4 to 1.5 range. patient was discharged on 10mg of glipizide with outpatient follow up for further blood sugar titration. . #) Left Shoulder Pain: chronic based on history, normal amylase and lipase, used tylenol for pain control.
summary: You were admitted to ___ with about a week of fatigue, and one day of nausea/vomiting. In the ER, you were found to be bradycardic and hypotensive (have a slow heart rate and low blood pressure), we also found that your potassium was high and your kidney function had gotten a bit worse. They also found that you had too much lactic acid in your blood, which was probably from not eating and drinking enough, becoming dehydrated and taking your metformin. In the ER they gave you lots of IV fluids to rehydrate you and your lab values improved. You were initially admitted to the ICU for closer monitoring, during your stay in the ICU they also found that your liver enzymes were elevated. These also improved with IV fluid hydration. Also, your lab tests showed signs that your heart was straining while you were dehydrated. You also had ___ echocardiogram ___ ultrasound of your heart), which does not explain your symptoms but was abnormal.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: ___ w/recent prolonged hospitalization for new diagnosis of GB carcinoma with direct invasion to the liver as well as fistuluation with the bowel with sepsis. # LEFT ARM SWELLING: Initially there was concern for DVT at rehab. While in the ED, the patient underwent LUE u/s with no evidence of DVT and CTA chest with no evidence of PE. It does not seem that the patient would want to be started on anticoagulation for treatment of a DVT/PE if one were to be found in the future, so a full discussion should be had with the patient, patient's HCP, and the responsible outpatient physician ___ MD or ___ prior to sending the patient to the hospital for testing that would not likely result in a change in patient's plan of care (which is comfort focused). # SKIN RASH: Affecting dependent areas (lower back, b/l calves). Concerning for developing bed sores/pressure ulcers. It is imperative that the patient be turned and repositioned at a minimum of every 2 hours, along with standard wound care (see discharge paperwork) to prevent worsening of patient's early stage pressure ulcers. The patient was not overly bothered by the rash and did not require any medications for symptom relief. # STAGE IV ADENOSQUAMOUS CARCINOMA WITH LOCAL LIVER INVASION: clinically unchanged from recent discharge. Continued current med regimen. # SEPSIS SECONDARY TO PERFORATED GALLBLADDER: continued Vancomycin/Cefepime and Flagyl for indefinite course. Patient has PICC which was noted to have tip at junction of brachiocephalic/SVC on CT chest. PICC was working well with normal blood return. This was discussed and confirmed with patient's HCP, ___. summary: You came to the hospital after being found to have jaundice. You were found to have liver disease, causing jaundice, and kidney disease, causing fluid buildup throughout your body. An endoscopy revealed a duodenal ulcer that was thought to be the cause of some slow GI bleeding. The ulcer was cauterized (burned) and you were treated with omeprazole.
