You were found to have some aspects of mania during your stay. Our Psychiatry team worked with you and suggested treatment with Haldol. They also suggested a stay in a psychiatric facility to help you gain control of this disease.

text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is an ___ patient with history of left internal carotid artery stenosis, sick sinus syndrome s/p pacer placement on coumadin, multiple strokes, seizures who presents with AMS, left-sided weakness, fevers, and new O2 requirement. ACUTE ISSUES: =========================== # Altered mental status, L-sided weakness/visual field deficit: Patient has prior right temporal-occipital cerebral infarction, and presented with recurrence of left hemineglect and mild hemiparesis, which were previously documented in ___ hospitalization, and the reappearance of these symptoms was consistent with recrudescence of prior stroke due to underlying urinary tract infection and pulmonary edema. On admission patient also had left homonymous hemianopsia that appeared new, as this was not previous documented, but per neurology consultants, this could also be explained by re-emergence of prior right parieto-occipital stroke syndrome. CT head negative for intracranial hemorrhage. patient's neurological symptoms completely resolved within 24 hours of admission. patient had no evidence of seizures and was continued on levetiracetam 1000mg BID. Warfarin was held for supratherapeutic INR on admission and restarted at home doses once INR dropped into therapeutic range. # Fever: Patient presented from ___ with fevers, most likely due to UTI. Urinalysis was positive for infection but urine and blood cultures were negative. No microbiology testing was done at ___. There was no evidence of pneumonia on CXR, or signs of other infectious foci. patient was initially treated with levofloxacin and ciprofloxacin, but these were held for risk of lowering seizure threshold. patient was transitioned to ceftriaxone, and discharged on cefpodoxime to complete a 7 day course of antibiotics. patient had no further fevers, chills, or rigors after admission. # Hypoxia: At ___, patient's initial systolic blood pressure was elevated above 200mm Hg. A chest x-ray demonstrated pulmonary edema, likely due to hypertensive urgency. Hypertensive urgency improved with labetalol and patient remained normotensive on home regimen of losartan and metoprolol. patient was treated with several doses of furosemide and supplemental oxygen, which was weaned off after 24 hours and patient had no further shortness of breath or hypoxia while on room air. Transthoracic echocardiogram demonstrated mild symmetric LVF with preserved global biventricular systolic function, elevated PCWP, mild aortic stenosis. No significant change since prior TTE in ___, with the exception of worsening MR and increased estimated PA systolic pressure. # EKG changes: On admission, patient was noted to have lateral T-wave inversions on EKG. There was low suspicion for ischemia in the setting of anemia, but patient had no chest pain, initially negative troponin. No transfusion was done in setting of volume overload. Repeat troponin and CK-MB were negative. TTE showed no regional wall motion abnormalities or signs of systolic dysfunction. # Anemia: Patient presented with normocytic anemia, with Hgb 8.5 on admission. The cause of patient's anemia was unclear; patient had no melena, hemoptysis, BRBPR, and was guiaic negative in the ___ and on the floor. patient has a history of upper GI bleed from likely gastric source. Work-up revealed elevated LDH but haptoglobin 77, indicating very low likelihood of hemolysis. Iron panel demonstrated: Fe 87, TIBC 212 (low), consistent with anemia of chronic disease vs blood loss. Reticulocyte count was 1.9%, retic index 0.5%, which was inappropriately low consistent with hypoproliferation. TSH and B12 were within normal limits. Hemoglobin further downtrending on hospital day 3, from 8.5 to 7.8. Recheck in the afternoon showed Hgb 8.1. Patient was guaiac negative at this time, with no symptoms or hemodynamic compromise, and no further work-up or intervention was done. #CHRONIC DIAGNOSES: ============================ # Sick-sinus syndrome: A-paced. Patient was continued on home metoprolol. Coumadin was initially held for supratherapeutic INR but was restarted prior to discharge when INR decreased to therapeutic range. # History of seizures: Patient had no evidence of seizures. patient was continued on home Keppra. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: ============================= -Antibiotics: Patient was treated with ceftriaxone for UTI while inpatient, and this was transitioned to cefpodoxime on discharge for 4 additional days to complete 7 day course of antibiotics

This was felt to be due to the stress on your body from the infection, and you did not have another stroke.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ y/o with chronic hepatitis C, complicated by cirrhosis, encephalopathy and ascites, also with last drink 4 days ago, who presented to clinic today with generalized edema, 12kg weight gain, asterixis and mild confusion. . # Encephalopathy/UTI: Confusion manifested as "forgetfulness", still AAOx3. Patient with confusion as per wife (and which patient agreed was also present), different from his baseline. Infectious cause was high on the differential given low grade fever (Tm=100.3 on day of admission). Skin exam concerning for possible cellulitis vs. edema/venous stasis with clear portal for entry. Also possible was med noncompliance (he claims lactulose daily w/ 3 BM's). Urine culture grew 10,000-100,000 colonies of E.coli. On ancef for ?cellulitis, which was switched to bactrim on ___ when it appeared that he likely did not have cellulitis and instead his skin findings more consistent with venous stasis/massive edema. Bactrim will cover E. coli UTI. Patient was continued on lactulose, thiamine, folate, MVI. Blood cultures negative to date, need to be followed up post-discharge. Abdominal ultrasound showed no fluid to tap for diag paracentesis. Also, no evidence of portal vein thrombosis. . # Alcohol Use: Given patient's alcohol use recently, he wasinactivated from the transplant list. Pt continued to deny use throughout his hospitalization to multiple physicians and social work. His wife told us of his use in confidence, so it should not be conveyed to the patient that patient told us this. His labs are suggestive of alcohol use, given AST:ALT in 2:1 elevation and anemia w/ macrocytosis. Did not score on CIWA scale throughout hospitalization, did receive diazepam when initially admitted in light of HTN, tachycardia, and low grade fever as well as history of ETOH use within a few days. Serum and urine tox positive only for opiates (on morphine). Pt will follow up as outpatient with transplant social work. . # ___ edema: Patient diuresed over 5kg throughout hospitalization while on aldactone/lasix. He admitted to high Na diet and also to taking tylenol/NSAIDS. Advised to stop taking these meds, and also counseled regarding low Na diet and fluid restriction. Discharged home on aldactone/lasix and will f/u lytes on ___, ___ w/ ___. . # EKG changes: EKG obtained because of tachycardia, patient denied any chest pain or shortness of breath (just felt "heart racing"). No personal or familial cardiac history. Risk factors were age, smoking history, HTN. Nonspecific ST changes in inferior leads on EKG (last EKG in ___ wnl); possibly rate related since CE negative times two and EKG repeated in AM showed NSR. . # Cirrhosis ___ HCV/?ETOH: Diagnosed by liver biopsy in ___, HCV refractory to treatment. EGD in ___ with grade I varices. Low Na diet, continued nadolol, lactulose, diuretics. Patient inactivated from liver transplant list for ETOH use and will f/u with transplant social work as outpatient. . # HTN: Continued home lisinopril, stopped lisinopril/HCTZ combo in light of new prescription for diuretics. . # COPD: Continued combivent, fluticasone . # Back pain: Continued home morphine, cyclobenzaprine . # Low back pain: Continued morphine, gabapentin 600mg TID (max dose for renal fxn, though previously reported taking 800mg TID), continued cyclobenzaprine. . # GERD: Continued omeprazole

text: Brief Hospital Course: ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: This is a ___ yo patient with progressive breast cancer metastatic to the liver, bones, with ascites and right sided hydronephrosis currently on eribulin (C1) now admitted for rising T bili. # Rising T bili: RUQ US showed no biliary obstruction. The exact etiology was unclear but thought due to liver dysfunction from metastases +/- hemolysis. patient's bili peaked at 4.9 (2.8 direct, 2.1 indirect) and then improved to 3.3 on day of discharge. if this is all related to liver failure, might expect transaminases and synthetic function to be worse than they are. The hepatology service was consulted regarding this question and they felt that patient's LFT abnormalities are most consistent with infiltrative liver metastases. There is a possibility that some level of hemolysis may be contributing, see below. Lactulose was considered but patient had no evidence of hepatic encephalopathy during this hospitalization so not started. # anemia: hgb 6.2-->9.3, responded to 2 unit PRBC transfusion ___. patient was admitted approx 1 week from last eribulin, so much of this likely chemo related. however, many nucleated reds on peripheral smear raises possibility of a marrow infiltrative process or RBC destructive process. patient was mildly thrombocytopenic but WBC and hgb were normal on metastatic presentation in ___. patient has been on chemo since which makes interpretation more difficult. LDH high, hapto low, retic 4%. could be related to hemolysis, though malignancy could explain high LDH and liver dysfunction could cause low haptoglobin. Coomb's test was negative so even if patient has hemolysis it does not seem to be autoimmune. review of peripheral smear showed many nucleated reds, moderate reticulocytosis, anisocytosis, rare spherocytes and schistocytes, normal appearing myeloid cells. # thrombocytopenia: likely chemo related. held pharmacologic DVT prophylaxis # shortness of breath: R base dullness on exam. last CT shows R effusion. likely malignant but no diagnostic thoracentesis has been done yet. CXR ___ possibly increasing effusion. symptoms only with climbing stairs so patient does not want to pursue thoracentesis at this time. explained that we may see improvement if this is malignant and responds to chemotherapy, otherwise will need thoracentesis if symptoms worsen. # breast cancer: Stage IIB (T2N1M0) infiltrating carcinoma with predominantly lobular features, ER+/PR+/Her2 non-amplified, with three of four positive lymph nodes of the R breast, S/p chemo, b/l mastectomy and xrt, found to be widely metastatic ___. treated with Xeloda, did not tolerate. Evaluated for trial at ___ but ineligible due to LFTs. started eribulin ___. patient's case was discussed with outpatient oncologist Dr. ___. though patient has increasing bili and significant cytopenias, we think that given patient's underlying disease burden and the possibility that some of patient's current lab abnormalities may be related to advancing malignancy, we should go ahead with chemotherapy. however, we gave reduced dose 0.4mg/m2 = 0.75mg Eribulin for C1D8. patient will resume treatment as an outpatient. Greater than 30 minutes was spent in discharge planning
summary: You were admitted for an elevated bilirubin, part of your liver tests. You had an ultrasound which showed no biliary obstruction. You were seen by the liver service and we think this is most likely related to breast cancer metastases in the liver. For now we will follow your labwork and continue chemotherapy as planned. You received a reduced dose of your chemotherapy while here. You were very anemic and received a 2 unit blood transfusion.

text: Brief Hospital Course: #. MSSA infection (including epidural abscesses/vertebral osteo/meningitis/bacteremia/skin lesions/UTI): Pt found to have MSSA from blood and also grew MSSA from urine. Vancomycin was started, then switched to Nafcillin when the organism was identified. TTE was performed and showed no vegetations. It is unknown what the portal of entry for the MSSA was. The bacteremia, skin lesions and UTI resolved with appropriate antibiotic therapy. Ortho spine was consulted and recommended serial imaging to determine whether epidural abscesses were increasing in size or causing spinal cord compression. Pt got MRIs approximately once a week and on the ___ it was more clear that the patient would require surgery. patient underwent neurosurgery ___ and for epidural abscess drainage (and C7 corpectomy, C4-T1 fusion, T3-4 laminectomy). Multiple abscesses present (~5, with 3 major ones), hardware place, cultures sent, debrided. Upon repeat imaging post operatively, MRI showed expanding T-spine epidural abscess, so patient then underwent L spine decompression ___ with debridement. Per ID, Gentamycin was added to help with Nafcillin penetration for a 5-day course, which was completed on ___. Pt will continue on nafcillin for at least 8 weeks and will follow up with spine and ID. patient's tentative stop date for nafcillin is ___, or it may be stopped on ___ when patient visits ID. patient has an appointment with Spinal surgery on ___. patient will need to have patient's staples removed on ___ in rehab with log role precaustions, per Spine surgery. patient is to have weekly lab draws faxed to the Infectious Disease Physician, ___. . #Hospital Acquired Pneumonia: treated for HAP with vancomycin and cefepime from ___ through ___. patient's nafcillin was stopped during this treatment and was restarted on ___. . #. Altered mental status: The patient was initially minimally responsive. This was thought to be secondary to meningitis as well as the severity of patient's infection. This resolved substantially with antibiotics. patient did remain minimally delerious throughout patient's stay (generally oriented x3 with moments of confusion). MRI head was normal. . # Weakness: As pt's mental status improved and patient became cooperative with neuro exam, it became clear that patient had diffuse weakness with some focality (especially R arm) with sensation relatively intact. Neurology was consulted who felt that some of the weakness could be ___ cord inflammation and so pt recieved pulsed steroids early in patient's admission without significant effect. Pt underwent EMG which showed a mixed picture (see EMG report for full details). Pt did undergo decompression on ___ and ___ but strength remained similar. . #. GI Bleed: On ___ pt developed melanotic stools and a hematocrit drop from 24 to 20. IV PPI was continued and patient recieved 1U of prbcs and had an EGD which showed severe ulcerations in stomach and duodenum most consistent with nsaid use (pt did use ibuprofen at home). Per pt patient had had a normal colonoscopy at ___ ___ yrs ago and this was not repeated as an inpt. Pt also reports h/o duodenal ulcers in the 1970s. An h pylori was sent and was positive. Treatment of h pylori was deferred in setting of nafcillin therapy and severe infection. Pt was continued on PPI, eventually transitioned to ___. Pt will need 2 week course of amoxicillin and clarithromycin after patient's nafcillin treatment is complete (nafcillin does not cover h pylori.) patient should continue lansoprazole until patient's visit with the Gastroenterologist in ___. . #. Persistent Sinus Tachycardia: Pt maintained HR of ~100 throughout patient's admission (~1 month). This was felt to most likely be related to patient's severe underlying infection and recurrent low grade fevers. Intravascular volume depletion was also a likely contributor given pt's low albumin and anasarca and clinical appearance of being dry (dry mouth, low JVP). PE was considered, however, pt was on DVT ppx throughout admission and EKG did not have any changes. Further, pt's oxygen requirement was minimal to none and ultimately it was decided that PE was highly unlikely. Also given patient's prolonged stay may be a PE, though this is less likely. . #. Edema: Patient was noted to have anasarca and an albumin of 1.9. Pt was not diuresed aggressively as patient appeared intravascularly depleted and had minimal oxygen requirement. patient's edema improved upon discharge. . #. Anemia: Pt remained anemic throughout patient's stay. Perhaps patient has had ulcers for some time contributing to patient's anemia. patient's reticulocyte count was 6.7 arguing against marrow suppression as the etiology, however, iron studies were consistent with anemia of chronic disease. The transfusion goal was set at 22. patient recieved 2U of PRBCs throughout patient's stay. . #. Pain: Patient had severe back pain throughout patient's admission that was ultimately treated with a fentanyl patch with small boluses of IV morphine for breakthrough pain. A kanair bed was also found to help with patient's pain. . #. Rash: On admission pt had 2 rashes. patient had diffuse small pustules which grew MSSA and resolved c antibiotics. patient also had, on the left back, a 4 x 3cm erythematous plaque with a central brown / black, rough, necrotic area which was biopsied by dermatology and showed "Focal necrotizing vasculitis in mid-dermis with focal thrombosis, and ischemic necrosis of epidermis and appendages" which dermatology felt was consistent with a reactive process, rather than representing a primary vasculitis, given the clinical scenerio. . #. Acute renal failure: Pt had ___ on admission, which resolved c IVF. . #. Elevated transaminases: Pt had elevated LFTs on admission, most likely from poor perfusion in the setting of dehydration or billiary sludging in the setting of SIRS. RUQ ultrasound unremarkable. This was trended and resolved. . #. Thrombocytopenia: in combination with direct bilirubinemia was concerning for consumptive process like TTP or DIC on admission, however no chistocytes on smear. Most likely due to poor production in the setting of infection and resolved during admission. . #. Nutrition: patient failed speech and swallow on ___. A percutaneous gastrojejunostomy tube was placed on ___ and tube feeds continued. . # Electrolyte Abnormalities: Patient had persistent hypokalemia and hypophosphatemia. Standing electrolyte orders were instilled and should be continued in rehab until levels normalize. Also, a Chem-10 should be checked every other day while taking these medications. #. Access: Patient has a PICC placed in the right arm on ___. #. summary: You were admitted with a bacterial infection of your spinal fluid and the bones of your spine as well as your urine and blood and skin. You were treated with antibiotics and the orthopedic surgeons did two surgeries to take out the abscesses. You also had a lot of weakness, for which we had neurology see you. ACTIVE ISSUES # ACUTE INFECTIOUS SIGMOID COLITIS: Unclear etiology to colitis. Focal segmental colitis of the sigmoid typical of diverticulitis however not apparent on review of CT scan with radiology. Repeat CT with contrast (pre-treatment required given history of allergy) to further investigate etiology and extent of inflammation revealed similar findings without evidence of abscess, free fluid, pneumatosis or perfortation. Stool cultures negative for clostridum difficile and ova and parasites. The patient was treated with 8 days of ciprofloxacin and metronidazole which patient was discharged on. patient's leukocytosis improved to baseline elevation in setting of chronic prednisone use and patient was afebrile throughout patient's hospital stay. patient's abdominal pain improved with time and stooling returned to patient's baseline. . # CONSTIPATION: On admission the patient reported not having had a bowel movement in over a week. patient was a bowel regimen at home with colace and high fiber diet while on percocet for chronic management of patient's back pain. On HD 3 patient had multiple large bowel movements with near complete resolution of patient's back pain. patient's diet was advanced from clears to regular diet with high fiber when patient had stooled. patient was discharged on a more aggressive bowel regimen given patient's increased pain regimen, with daily miralax and colace with bisacodyl enemas as needed. . # ACUTE L2 VERTEBRAL COMPRESSION FRACTURE: The patient presented with worsening back pain. The patient was evaluated by physical therapy who recommended discharge to rehab facility for conditioning. patient will also follow-up with pain clinic. We suggested that a taper of patient's escalated pain regimen should be attempted as patient improves, given patient's complex regimen and associated risks of constipation. . # INCIDENTAL CT FINDINGS: An ill-defined hypodensity in the junction of the pancreatic head and neck was noted on CT abdomen and pelvis that could represent focal fat or ductal dilatation; however, mass could be entirely excluded. The patient rerpoted taking 20 mg everynight at home. This was not continued in the inpatient setting given patient's pain regimen. . # BENIGN HYPERTENSION: Stable. Family history of hyperlipidemia. patient was continued on crestor. . # SEASONAL ALLERGIES: Stable. Continue singulair and albuterol for now. The patient takes alvesco at home which was continued on discharge. . text: Brief Hospital Course: ICU Course: ___ with PMHx of hypertension, s/p CCY ___, who was transferred to ___ from ___ for acute gallstone pancreatitis s/p ERCP w/sphincterotomy ___, hospital course complicated by new onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. # Afib w/RVR: After the ERCP, the patient developed new-onset afib w/RVR. Etiology unclear, possibly related to hypersympathetic tone in the context of acute pancreatitis. TSH was normal. Cardiac enzymes were negative. Did not anticoagulate patient's given CHADS2 score of 1 and bleeding risk from sphincterotomy ___ during ERCP. A TTE was performed which showed normal global and regional biventricular systolic function, However there was mild left atrial dilatation which may have been a cause or effect of the atrial fibrillation. The patient spontanously converted back to sinus rhythm. Given patient's CHADS 2 score, use of both aspirin and plavix can be considered. patient was started on aspirin alone, and advised to discuss with patient's PCP any additional use of plavix. # Hypoxemia: Most likely secondary to flash pulmonary edema in the context of fluid resuscitation and new atrial fibrillation. Resolved. # Pancreatitis: Patient is s/p ERCP with sphincterotomy and stone extraction. LFTs are trending down and patient reports improvement in patient's abdominal pain. Will continue symptom management. LFTs improved over course of hospitalization. # Leukocytosis: Patient presented with normal WBC 6.4 on admission, which rose to 16.8. Likely due to inflammation from acute pancreatitis. S/p ERCP w/sphincterotomy; no evidence of cholangitis on ERCP, but given low-grade fevers (99.5) and increasing leukocytosis, started empiric cipro. NASH/hepatic fibrosis on ultrasound. PCP should discuss dietary measures, consider liver biopsy to further assess.

TTEs showed expansion of the pericardial effusion with physiologic evidence of tamponade. patient's preload was maintained with IVF. patient revisited the cath lab on ___ balloon pericardiotomy was performed and a new drain was placed. Repeat TTEs showed a significant improvement in the size of the pericardial effusion. The cytology report confirmed that the effusion was malignant. The pericardial drain was removed on ___ and the patient was transferred to the OMED service on ___. The site of the drain remained clean, dry and intact throughout admission. #Persistent Hypoxia: patient while in CCU requiring O2, has been able to wean variably getting down to 1L and then increasing back to 2.5 for comfort. Recent CXR without evidence of pneumonia but bilateral mod-large pleural effusions. Pleurex on right side drained ___ for 250cc. Tried to drain ___, but was not getting much drainage despite large appearance on the Chest CT. CTA showed no PE. IP placed pleurex drain to pleurevac and wall suction with much improved output of 800cc serosanguinous fluid. O2 was able to be weaned to 0.5-1L for comfort with sats 97-99%. Despite adequate drainage, patient continued to require O2 at night for sats>95%. A chest CT showed large left pleural effusion in addition to continued right pleural effusion despite low output from the Pleurex. tPA was instilled in right pleurex and then drain was attached to pleurevac and wall suction and a left pigtail was placed to drainage as well. Bilateral drains put out approximately 2L each and the patient's oxygenation, subjective shortness of breath and cough greatly improved and patient was able to maintian sats>93% on RA with ambulation and during sleep. Interventional pulmonology had plans to place a left pleurex, however at time of discharge, accumulation on the left side was not appreciable enough for drain placement. If patient has increase in patient's symptoms and evidence of reaccumulating left sided pleural effusion, patient should have a pleurex drain placed there. They also reccommended draining right sided pleural effusion every other day in order to decrease possibility that drain would clot off. # Leukocytosis: Patient noted to have leukocytosis of 11.7 with left shift. Given cough and recent hospitalization, patient was treated briefly for ?HCAP with vanc/cefepime/metronidazole (day ___. Antibiotics were discontinued given low suspicion. patient maintained a normal white count and was afebrile. #Tachycardia: Patient was persistently tachycardic at baseline in the 120s, remained this way through entire admission. Serial echos observed a stable pericardial effusion, but did note a change in patient's EF/systolic function on ___ from >55% to 40-45%. It is possible that in the future patient should be rate controlled in case of developing a tachycardia induced cardiomyopathy. Should follow-up with cardiology. # Lung CA: Patient took about a one month break from chemo for patient's son's wedding, planning to restart soon. The oncology team was consulted during patient's CCU course and agreed with drainage of the malignant effusion. text: Brief Hospital Course: ASSESSMENT & PLAN: ___ man with a h/o polysubstance abuse (on suboxone), depression / anxiety, ADHD, epilepsy admitted with multifocal pneumonia and influenza, intubated for respiratory distress. #. Acute Respiratory Failure (ARDS/Multifocal pneumonia): Flu swab positive at an OSH ED per report. He was started on Tamiflu and levaquin as an outpatient. He wasd hypotensive in the ED. Volume responsive. Febrile to 105 at home with a peak of 103.1 on the floor. Given concern for bacterial superinfection with high temps on Tamiflu and worsening respiratory status and CXR, he was empirically started on vancomycin and ceftriaxone/azithro. Levoflox was discontinued because of risk of lowering the seizure threshold. On ___ his oxygen requirement increased from 2 to 4liters, and subsequently satting in the ___ on non-rebreather. His PaO2 on NRB was 60 at which time he was transferred to the ICU for respiratory failure and hypotension. In the ICU patient was intubated for respiratory distress and antibiotics were broadened to vanc/cefepime and patient was started on tamiflu. HIV Ab negative. Viral screen revealed RSV. Urinary legionella negative. Bronchoscopy illustrated alveolar hemorrhage, and BAL unrevealing. Due to somewhat enlarged heart seen on CXR and signs of pulmonary edema on CXR, an ECHO was done which was normal with LVEF=55%. In the setting of negative culture data, all antibiotics were discontinued. Pulmonary function improved, and patient eventually extubated. His lung exam continued to improve and was oxygenating well on room air. #ICU delirium/benzo withdrawal: Once patient was extubated, sedation was weaned to low dose fentanyl and dexmetomidate. On the day of extubation he became delerious and agitated, requiring IV haldol. That evening he developed auditory and visual hallucinations, although he was able to be reoriented to person, place, and time, and followed commands. Dexmetomidate was held for ~5 minutes, and patient became acutely anxious with HR to 140s, though BP stable. He was given 5mg IV haldol with rapid improvement in symptoms. He was started on 10mg methadone TID. He was started on PRN haldol, however his QTc was elevated to 460s and therefore he was switched to zyprexa, however he did not require zyprexa so this was stopped. He was also started on low dose valium for presumed benzodiazepine withdrawal. He improved greatly and was able to be weaned off benzodiazepines and methadone. He had some nausea likely ___ sedative withdrawal which improved with phenergan. As he had no agitation for >2 days he was transferred to the medical floor. # Hypotension/shock: His SBPs on presentation were in the 70-80s and noted to have altered mental status on admission to the ICU, consistent with decreased cerebral perfusion and septic shock. Patient was volume resuscitated and started on vasopressors for vasomotor support. Pneumonia was treated as above. Pressors downtitrated and eventually d/c'ed altogether several days after admission # Polysubstance abuse: After transfer out of the ICU, Mr. ___ case was discussed with his ___ Specialist, Dr. ___. patient confirmed that his drug of choice was initially oxycodone, then oxycontin, then heroin by snorting (never injected). Dr. ___ stopping methadone (under the 30mg/day minimum for discontinuing) and treating withdrawal symptoms with clonidine and following on ___ scale. He was monitored for 2.5 days and required 2 doses of clonidine for symptom management. We discussed having follow-up in place as well as safety plans, mechanisms in place so that once he leaves he has people to help him if he were to have the desire to use again. He will follow-up with Dr. ___ on ___ to discuss his options for treatment. He was discharged with a short script (10 tabs) of clonidine for withdrawal symptoms. #2. Seizure disorder: His mother raised the concern of whether he truly had epilepsy, or if all of his seizures could be related to drug abuse. After hearing more details about his seizure history, it certainly appears possible. He has had 4 seizures in the past, each of which has correlated somewhat with a drug. The first was surrounding use of Tramadol which lowers the seizure threshold. His second was related to depakoate in some unknown capacity. The other two were related to benzo overdose (Xanax) and subsequent seizure. He would like to transfer his care here for neurology, and would like to readdress the question. During his acute illness, topiramate and gabapentin were continued. # Anxiety: On lorazepam. Sees a counselor. Lorazepam was held during intubation. It was restarted at 1mg BID once stable on the floor. He was provided 6 tablets at discharge, which should be readrressed given his prior history of overdose with alprazolam. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: - Pulmonary follow-up - Addiction follow-up - Neurology transition of care to ___
summary: You were admitted to ___ with a very severe viral pneumonia. You required an admission to the ICU and intubation (breathing tube) to help support your breathing. As a result of being so ill, you had times of confusion called delirium. As your health improved, the confusion resolved. While in the ICU you require very high doses of medication to help sedate you and keep you comfortable. As those medications were stopped, you were started on methadone to prevent withdrawal. Methadone was tapered and stopped as well. You were monitored for signs of withdrawal, and at the time of discharge you were doing great. You were provided with clonidine to take as needed for withdrawal symptoms of achiness, abdominal cramps, headache, nausea. Please take this only if needed and only every 6 hours. Also, do not take this within 2 hours of taking your lorazepam as they both can make you drowsy. Please do not drive within 4 hours of taking either of these medications.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ with a history of congenital bicuspid aortic valve, complicated by severe aortic stenosis, history of provoked/unprovoked PE (previously on warfarin, with frequent sub-therapeutic INRs), gastric bypass, severe depression with previous suicide attempt, somatic symptom disorder, and history of substance abuse, who presented as a transfer from ___ ___ with chest heaviness. On admission, had D-dimer > ___, and was thought to have PE initially; was started on heparin gtt, as INR sub-therapeutic on warfarin. However, V/Q scan was ultimately negative, and repeat D-dimer normal. Ultimately had inpatient stress test to work-up AS as causal etiology of patient's pain, which was negative. ==================== ACUTE/ACTIVE ISSUES: ==================== # Severe aortic stenosis # Bicuspid aortic valve # Shortness of breath # Chest Pain Severe AS based on valve area, mean pressure gradient, and peak pressure gradient. Although chest heaviness is symptom of severe aortic stenosis, not clear that this is related, given that pain is atypical and comes and goes with both exertion and at rest. However, on initial presentation, was more concerned that patient's SOB on exertion could be a symptom of worsening AS. Given this is patient's second presentation due to anxiety surrounding same, and as patient's sxs appear to be worsening, inpatient cardiology evaluation was pursued. On the recommendation of the cardiology team, patient had a stress test inpatient (ETT MIBI) to evaluate hemodynamic response to exercise on ___, which will elucidate the functional significance of patient's AS, and for ischemia. Stress test was negative. patient will f/u as outpatient for consideration of AVR. # Chest pain # Elevated D-dimer (likely false reading) # History of PEs With pleuritic component to pain and persistent nature of symptoms, initially had high suspicion of PE, especially in light of patient's history of PEs, as well as patient's subtherapeutic INR. Started heparin gtt empirically on ___. However, V/Q scan on ___ showed no evidence of PE, and LENIs negative. Recheck D-dimer was <215, so initial elevation was likely a false reading. Repeat TTE showed no evidence of RV dysfunction. More likely, chest pain reflects patient's underlying anxiety, with some contribution from patient's AS (as above). Vascular Medicine was consulted, and recommended transitioning from warfarin to apixaban for anticoagulation, in conjunction with recommendations from patient's outpatient hematologist. Discussed with pharmacy, no need to load apixaban as patient was therapeutic on heparin gtt for days prior to starting apixaban. Patient received acetaminophen Q8H:PRN, as well as lidocaine patches, for pain. # Severe depression/anxiety Patient has severe depression and anxiety that is likely contributing to patient's symptoms; in particular, acute-onset chest pain that comes and goes, and is unrelated to patient's SOB on exertion. Psychiatry was consulted and recommended starting low-dose Zyprexa, which patient tolerated, to good effect. Also continued patient's home medication regimen: - continue buspirone 30mg BID and 15mg in afternoon - continue lamotrigine 150mg BID - continue topiramate 50mg QID - continue trazodone 300mg QHS - continue venlafaxine 225mg daily - continue ropinirole 2mg TID - continue cariprazine 1.5mg daily ====================== CHRONIC/STABLE ISSUES: ====================== # Hypothyroidism - continued levothyroxine 150mg daily # Orthostatic hypotension - continued fludrocortisone 0.1mg QAM # GERD - continued pantoprazole 40mg Q12H ================== TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: ================== [ ] Started on apixaban for anticoagulation, with plans for close outpatient heme follow-up [ ] Started on Zyprexa for anxiety, with plans for close outpatient Psych follow-up [ ] outpatient cardiology follow-up re: severe aortic stenosis and plans for valve replacement #CODE STATUS: Full #CONTACT: Daughter, although husband is listed as HCP
summary: You had severe chest pain, and were transferred for further work-up EKGs were reassuring, showing that you did not have any new changes concerning for a heart attack. We initially were concened that you had a blood clot in your lungs,but you had a lung scan which did not show any clot. Because your INR was very low, the cardiology team, in conjunction with your outpatient hematologist, recommended transitioning your anticoagulation to apixaban (Eliquis). The psychiatry team evaluated you to better manage your anxiety, and started you on a new medication called Zyprexa. You had a stress test, which showed no signs of heart disease.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old male with metastatic pancreatic cancer refractory to chemotherapy with chronic pain on patient ___ and s/p celiac plexus block during recent admission, here with chest tightness and dyspnea on exertion. # Chest tightness/dyspnea: Appears due to SOB of breath rather than true chest pain based on history. His CT findings of an increase in the amount of pulmonary metastases seems commensurate progression of dyspnea. Comparison of prior EKGs to the ones at present show no significant change and troponins are negative x2. Very little concern for cardiac ischemia and stress testing at this point is very low yield, given low likelihood of following up a positive result with a procedure. Overnight telemetry was unremarkable. He also has chronic pain, leading to a previous hospitalization requiring a celiac plexus block and titration of his narcotics. Patient's symptoms resolved on day of discharge. # Metastatic pancreatic cancer: He is s/p Whipple and failed trial of gemcitabine, now switched over to FOLFOX. He is most bothered by chronic pain from metastatic disease and is managed with long and short-acting narcotics. # Hyponatremia: Prior work-up consistent with mild hypovolemia and malignancy-related SIADH. He was asymptomatic during entire hospital course but his appetite was poor. Little evidence of hypovolemia on this admission. Recommend continued fluid restriction to 2L. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: [] Continue 2L fluid restriction [] Reassess need for home ___ patient felt deconditioned over past several weeks.
summary: You had come in because you were experiencing chest tightness. We did several studies and determined that your heart was not the cause of your pain, and you did not have a heart attack. The imaging we performed showed that you have cancer metasteses to your lung which may explain the tightness and SOB you experienced. We also noted your sodium level was low. We recommend you do not drink more than 2 L of fluid per day. We have provided you with a script for physical therapy. We have not made any changes to your medication list.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old patient with a history of GBM and multiple episodes of meningitis of unknown etiology, here with meningitis. patient's LP was done in the ED approx 4 hours after they began antibiotics. The LP in the ED showing pelocytosis with neutrophilic predominance, elevated protein, and low glucose. The CSF fluid was gram stain and culture negative, but the numbers were consistent with a bacterial meningitis. Infectious disease was consulted and the patient was initially put on a regimen of ampicillin, ceftriaxone, vancomycin and acyclovir. There was initial concern regarding increased edema of R medial temporal lobe compared to prior CT ___, however, this is the area where the patient has patient's tumor and patient's clinical picture and laboratory values were not consistent with an HSV encephalitis. The HSV-PCR eventually came back as negative. Other viral studies including enterovirus were negative. The patient continued to spike fevers as high as 103 throughout this admission. Serial blood cultures were obtained. The patient's blood cultures were negative. The patient had a repeat LP done to monitor for response to treatment. The CSF fluid studies did improve showing a decreased WBCs and a decrease in total protein. The patient's antibiotic ID regimen was eventually paired down to ceftriaxone and vancomycin. A PICC line was placed however home services were unable to be initiated for the patient for another three days. Hence, the patient was unable to be discharged on hospital day 8 and stayed until hospital day 10 to complete at 10 day course of IV ceftriaxone and vancomycin. . The patient was continued on patient's outpatient dose of lovenox throughout this admission for history of PE.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ W/PMH alcoholic cirrhosis (c/b grade II varices, encephalopathy, ascites; now sober), chronic pancreatitis, anemia, and depression presents from clinic for right foot swelling, constipation and confusion, found to be constipated, with minimal hepatic encephalopathy and RLE edema extending from desquamated R toes s/p recent oil burn. . # RLE BURN Patient suffered burn w/hot cooking oil on patient's dorsal toes 5d prior to admission. Seen in ED at ___, received dilaudid but no antibiotics because not thought to be infected-appearing. Erythema resolved but in the interim patient developed concerning symptoms including edema and worsening foot pain with weight-bearing. Superficially the burn wounds apppeared as if they might resolve spontaneously. However, given surrounding edema and plantar pain on palpation, there was concern for tracking of skin flora from one or more of the burn sites to deeper tissues. CT and plain film imaging of the R foot/ankle showed no evidence for more than superficial injury, and no foreign body. Wound care consult recommended daily dressing changes as delineated in patient instructions (see above). Podiatry evaluated patient's foot and recommended use of a post-surgical boot to enable patient to ambulate with touch-down heel weight-bearing while patient's ankle sprain heals (see below). Pain was controlled with tylenol and ultram. Opiates were avoided given constipation, as below. . # ANKLE SPRAIN Patient's R ankle/leg were edematous and tender on admission exam. Concern for infection, as above. However, imaging showed no evidence of infection, and edema improved markedly within the first 24 hours with leg elevation. Podiatry consult saw patient and elicited additional hx of possible recent ankle sprain in the chaos surrounding patient's foot burn incident. patient was fitted with a post-surgical boot and crutches. patient was able to tolerate touch-down weight bearing on the R leg with ___ priot to discharge. . # CONSTIPATION Patient had diffuse abdominal pain on admission, worst LLQ. Provided hx of having smaller pebble-like BMs over the past 1.5 weeks despite continuing TID lactulose as directed. Last ___ 3d PTA. Aggressive lactulose dosing produced 1 large BM in the first 24h, but patient experienced continued abdominal pain with nausea. KUB showed large amount of stool within the colon and small intestine. Further lactulose + miralax and Fleet's enema enabled additional bowel movements, and patient's abdominal pain subsided. Complete workup to rule out other etiologies for abdominal pain included a liver/GB ultrasound showing no biliary obstruction or inflammation, cirrhotic liver unchanged from prior, and patent portal vein. Lipase wnl. Plan was to discharge patient on TID 30 cc lactulose (as before) + 17 g miralax BID to soften stools. Abdominal pain had resolved prior to discharge (after total 3 large BMs), and the patient was feeling well. . # ABDOMINAL DISTENSION Patient noted this on admission; jeans not fitting well ___ increased abdominal girth. patient had been on lasix and spironolactone which were discontinued during a recent admission for ARF. patient had no clinical signs of SBP, no fever, no leukocytosis. Attempted ultrasound-guided paracentesis to remove any ascitis fluid but there was none. Cr was back wnl at 0.7, so lasix 20 mg QD + spironolactone 50 QD (decreased compared to prior dosing) were restarted. . #MILD HEPATIC ENCEPHALOPATHY Patient reported mild confusion at home but was not noticeable encephalopathic on admission. patient was AOX3 and conversed appropriately. Exam notable for fetor hepaticus. Does have hx hepatic encephalopathy, on home lactulose and rifaximin. Suspect recent confusion prior to admission is ___ constipation. Infectious workup was pursued but all negative - attempted paracentesis for possible SBP but no ascites fluid to drain; blood culture, urine culture, and CXR were either pending or negative at time of discharge. . # ETOH Cirrhosis Chronic. Continued lactulose/rifaximin as above. Also continued nadolol, which was started 2 months ago in setting of variceal bleed. . # ANEMIA Chronic, ___ underlying cirrhosis. Hct baseline. Given recent UGIB from known grade I lower esophageal varices, Hct was trended closely and any nausea treated promptly w/zofran. No hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia at home recently or during this admission. patient was continued on nadolol, as above, and Ppi. . # PHARYNGITIS Oropharynx inflamed on admission. Patient also having recent fever and sore throat. No sick contacts. Concern for either strep pharyngitis or viral pharyngitis including HSV pharyngitis given degree of inflammation and possible concurrent lip lesions (?spider angioma vs HSV stomatitis). Met only 2 Centor criteria (+1 for lack of cough, +1 for hx fever, no exudate, no lymphadenopathy) for strep. patient was started on antibiotic treatment for strep pharyngitis (PCN 500 mg Q8H x 10d, ___ and acyclovir 400 mg TID x 5 days for HSV (___). Also received chloriseptic spray q6H PRN for symptomatic relief. . # CHRONIC PANCREATITIS Continued on home pancreatic enzyme supplement w/meals. . # CHRONIC HEADACHES Continued home fioricet PRN during this admission, but we note that fioricet contains tylenol and patient also taking tylenol for pain, up to 2 g/day. Including patient's fioricet dose patient may be exceeding daily recommendations for tylenol consumption in cirrhosis. Recommend re-evaluation of headache regimen during outpatient follow-up. . # MICROSCOPIC HEMATURIA Patient noted to have microscopic hematuria on screening UA. No hx gross hematuria, no recent foley trauma. Will need outpatient follow-up. . # E COLI + URINE CULTURE After patient was discharge, patient's urine culture grew E.coli (___) As the patient was asymptomatic and the culture grew <100K, patient was not treated for a UTI, but patient's outpatient providers were alerted by email to follow-up as necessary. TRANSITIONAL ISSUES 1. Follow-up BM frequency, efficacy of lactulose + miralax bowel regimen 2. Follow-up headache regimen as above, consider replacing fioricet with non-tylenol-containing med 3. Follow-up microscopic hematuria, E coli + urine culture w/ repeat UA
summary: You were admitted to the hospital with constipation, confusion, abdominal pain and foot pain. You were constipated. We gave you several extra doses of lactulose, some miralax and an enema to promote bowel movements. You were nauseated and in pain until your constipation resolved, which took >24 hours. You did not seem confused to us during this admission, but your were extra tired which can happen with hepatic encephalopathy. We examined your foot. Your xrays and CT scans were normal. A podiatrist examined you and thought your burn wound would heal well if you follow the directions from the wound care nurse who saw you (see below). He thought your swelling and ankle pain were from a recent ankle sprain, not related to the burn. You will be sent home with a surgical boot. Please only put pressure on your right heel. Do not put weight on the front of your foot, as instructed and demonstrated by the physical therapists.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ h/o breast cancer metastatic to brain, on herceptin, s/p whole brain XRT late ___ presenting with declining mental status and confusion, likely multifactorial. # Encephalopathy: Differential is broad, in this setting concern is for cerebral edema in the setting of metastatic breast cancer. Findings on CT may be ___ radiation treatment. Other contributing factors include UTI, recent social stressors with brother and sister being hospitalized. patient was treated for a UTI with ceftriaxone. patient was also started back on low dose dexamethasone out of concern that the findings on CT represented true edema rather than simply post-radiation changes. patient was treated with trazodone for sleep and given IV haldol as needed for agitation. On HD1 patient had an acute episode of agitation which required restraints and haldol. Psychiatry was consulted to help manage the patient's delirium and recommended standing haldol at night plus additional as needed. patient had a fluctuating coarse requiring intermittent prn haldol but was otherwise stable. # Ecchymoses: After receiving subcu heparin shots on admission due to subtherapeutic INR, patient developed large areas of ecchymosis on bilateral flanks. After INR became therapeutic, subcu heparin was discontinued. The team felt given the large areas of brusing coupled with increased fall risk, low likelihood of stroke and unclear life expectency, the risks of coumadin outweigh the benefits. After discussions with the patient's HCP and daughter, the family felt better about continuing the coumdin and following up with the patient's cardiologist as an outpatient. # Decreased responsiveness: On ___ patient had an episode of decreased responsiveness with generalized shaking. Neurology was consulted due to concern for seizures in a patient with brain metastases. They felt this was more consistent with toxic metabolic encephalopathy. A non-contrast head CT was obtained to rule out bleeding in the setting of hypertension with anticoagulation and acute change in mental status. The scan was unchanged from previous. 24-hr EEG was negative for seizure activity. MRI was recommended to evaluate for progression of disease, but after consultation with the patient's primary oncologist Dr. ___ was determined that patient is not a candidate for further therapy and that further imaging would not alter management. #bacterial UTI: Pt. has h/o toxic metabolic encephalopathy and was delirious during previous hospitalizations. The patient was seen by patient's primary oncologist, Dr. ___ hospitalization. # Hypertension: Continued on losartan # Hypothyroidism: Continued on levothyroxine TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: - bruising on flanks will need to be monitored - risks vs. benefits of coumadin should be discussed with family and primary oncologist

text: Brief Hospital Course: ============================ BRIEF SUMMARY: ============================ ___ with history of NASH cirrhosis c/b portal vein thrombosis and esophageal varices s/p band ligation presenting to liver clinic with worsening ascites and chest pain, with bleeding symptoms spontaneously resolved, with no focal evidence or hemolysis identified after comprehensive workup. Presented with evidence of acute kidney injury that reflected a tenous renal perfusion in the setting of pulmonary hypertension, responded to treatment. ============================ DETAILED SUMMARY BY PROBLEM: ============================ # Anemia: Patient presented to outside clinic with progressive shortness of breath over 3 weeks, associated with chest tightness and palpitations. patient had previously noticed worsening ascites, had patient's outpatient dose of Lasix increased to 40 mg daily and spironolactone to 100 mg daily. Due to ongoing symptoms patient presented to the emergency room. Labs were notable for an H&H of ___, repeated at 5.6/20.8, with low platelets of 53. Patient received CT abdomen and pelvis negative for retroperitoneal hematoma, hemolysis labs were negative. Patient received an endoscopy which demonstrated one very small cord of grade 1 varices in the mid to distal esophagus, otherwise no evidence of bleeding. Anemia was felt to be most likely secondary to chronic liver disease, with a possible contribution of iron deficiency. The patient was found to have a low ferritin, and was given 1 dose of IV iron infusion. Patient may consider capsule study as an outpatient #Acute kidney injury - Patient had ongoing evidence of acute kidney injury, with a baseline creatinine of 1.1, though escalated as high as 1.7. As part of chest pain workup patient received echocardiography, which demonstrated some signs of pulmonary hypertension. Creatinine did not improve to baseline following intravenous resuscitation, therefore cardiorenal syndrome was considered, creatinine escalated further in response to IV Lasix, so this was discontinued. Renal ultrasound demonstrated no evidence of obstruction or acute abnormality. Renal was consulted, and believed further Lasix was contraindicated. Ischemic injury to the kidneys was considered in the context of patient's presenting anemia, though patient's downtrending creatinine was thought not to reflect this. No growth to date currently. - Discharge weight 83.92 kg *CODE STATUS and preferred communication were reviewed #CODE: DNR/DNI (confirmed) #CONTACT: Name of health care proxy: ___ Relationship: daughter Phone number: ___ Cell phone: ___ *CODE STATUS and preferred communication were reviewed

text: Brief Hospital Course: This is a ___ year old patient with PMH of DM2, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, history of CVA times 2 with no residual deficits, Graves' disease with recurrent hypothyroidism, gout, h/o of breast cancer s/p right mastectomy/XRT/chemotherapy ___ years ago, and significant arthritis presenting with worsening shortness of breath over the last 2 weeks likely due to bilateral pleural effusions. . #. Dyspnea. Likely secondary to volume overload as the patient reports having 2 weeks of worsening dyspnea after having ___ food. patient's symptoms improved somewhat (lower extremity edema improved) with manual cycling of patient's peritoneal dialysis in the day in addition to patient's normal nightly cycles. However, patient continued to have dyspnea and was found to have an oxygen requirement. CXR shows new bilateral pleural effusions in the setting of a relatively unimpressive BNP at 1268; CE negative. Per renal, increased lasix and they adjusted peritoneal dialysis for more aggressive fluid removal. Pt did well and subjective feeling of dyspnea improved significantly per pt. However, pt continued to have O2 requirement. Per pt patient is always arougn 84% at home and does not use oxygen and indeed off of oxygen patient would desat to ~84% while in hospital after agressive diuresis. VQ scan was low probability of PE; LENIs were negative as well. Decision was made to d/c pt on torsemide 80mg daily per renal w/continued peritoneal dialysis at home in addition to having outpatient pulmonary and sleep study. . #. Renal failure. Pt was seen by renal who adjusted peritoneal dialysis and made lasix recommendations. Pt continued on home vitamin B12, folic acid, Renvela. Because of low blood pressures in the setting of aggressive diuresis, pt's diltiza, and lisinopril were held and patient's carvedilol was decreased to 3.125 bid. On d/c this was continued given no elevated blood pressures; pt's bp med needs will need to be reassessed as an outpatient. . #. DM2. Held home glipizide. Continued Lantus at 55 units (rather than 70) while inpatient b/c pt was on the low side of glucose and cover with HISS. . #. Gout- Continued home allopurinol. . #. Hypothyroidism. Continued home levothyroxine 200mcg ___, 100mcg remainder of the week. . #. Hyperlipidemia. Continued home Lipitor. . #. Paroxysmal Afib. Held home diltiazem b/c of low BP in setting of diuresis. Lowered carvedilol to 3.125mg bid . #. HTN. Held home Lisinopril b/c of low BP in setting of diuresis. . #. H/o stroke. Continued home aspirin 325mg daily, statin, antihypertensives. . #. Osteoarthritis. Continued home pain regimen of Tylenol and tramadol. . TRANSITIONAL ISSUES: - Pt will need require outpatient PFTs and non-contrast Chest CT to eval for interstitial lung disease -Pt has outpt follow-up planned.
summary: You came to the hospital because you were experiencing shortness of breath and found to have a decreased oxygen level in your blood. You were admitted for additional removal of fluid through peritoneal dialysis since you had been unable to fully remove the excess fluid at home. The kidney doctors saw ___ you were in the hospital and helped to adjust your dialysis regimen and medications to improve your fluid status. Your symptoms improved; however, your oxygen level remained lower than normal when not on supplemental oxygen. Because of this low oxygen level, several additional tests were done to make sure there was not an undiagnosed problem such as a clot. This workup was negative. We felt that you would benefit from having home oxygen to help your oxygen levels. Please wear the oxygen nasal canula at all times.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ y/o right handed man with a PMH significant for HTN and DMII, who presented to the ED with acute onset of right sided weakness, speech changes and confusion ___. Code Stroke called, TPA was not given as IPH noted on ___. His exam at admission was notable for right sided neglect, nonfluent aphasia but also with receptive defecits, possible right hemianopia, mild right NLF flattening, right sided hemiparesis and hemisensory loss. Patient was admitted to the ICU. His NCHCT showed a large left frontoparietal IPH that extended from the thalamus to the cortex and on further imaging was found to have multiple cerebral mets. An EVD was inserted due to worsening ICH and it was not possible to remove this due to high ICP spikes. Staging CT-torso revealed a large lung mass and associated adrenal metastasis. Lymph node biopsy came back as adenocarcinoma. Patient had spontaneous movement on the left side and had eyes open GCS E4 V2 M5 and due to poor prognosis oncology felt that no chemotherapy or XRT was indicated at this time. Family maintained desire to actively treat and patient was transitioned to the floor on ___. Due to the plan for rehab, patient had a revision of his EVD to a VP shunt on ___ after a further failed attempt at clamping this. Patient deteriorated and was transferred back to ___ ICU on ___ due to increasing somnolence and CT showed worse edema and herniation. Patient was treated with IV mannitol to good effect and dexamethasone was increased. Patient was latterly able to obey very simple commands inconsistently. He was tapered off the mannitol and remained neurologically stable. The patient had a PEG placed on ___. After PEG placement the patient developed a mild ileus that resolved with conservative treatment. Tube feeds were subsequently restarted and tolerated well. The patient is now being tapered off the steroids as well. He is being transferred to rehab on ___. . # Neuro: Patient has risk factor of HTN and presented to the ED with acute onset of right sided weakness, speech changes and confusion on ___ and although Code Stroke was called patient was noted to have a large ICH on CT-head. Admission exam was notable for right sided neglect, nonfluent aphasia but also with receptive defecits, possible right hemianopia, mild right NLF flattening, right sided hemiparesis and hemisensory loss. His NCHCT showed a large left frontoparietal IPH that extended from the thalamus to the cortex. Patient was transferred to the neuro ICU. Given his history of HTN, with SBP of 180s on arrival, the most likely etiology was intially thought to be hypertensive. CTA did not show any findings to suggest AVM. The patient's conscious level decreased and repeat CT showed worsening of the ICH and associated edema and midline shift. He underwent an elective intubation and EVD placement on ___. CSF showed normal protein, glucose. Cell count and diff showed 60 WBCs and 4000 RBCs, PMN predominant. Gram stain showed PMNs but no organisms grew on culture. Beta-2 microglobulin, protein electrophoresis were negative. Cytology with flow cytometry showed rare atypical epithelioid cells suspicious for metastases. CEA was negative. ___ MRI head with contrast was done that showed numerous enhancing foci in the bilateral occipital lobes and the right parietal/frontal lobe, concerning for metastatic disease. CT torso showed a 6.2 cm right upper lobe mass, multiple lymph nodes, including a right supraclavicular lymph node and a left adrenal lesion. On ___, an ultra-sound guided supraclavicular lymph node biopsy was done at the bedside that showed metastatic adenocarcinoma, presumed to be primary lung cancer. The medical oncology service was called for a formal evaluation of the patient's condition. Given the patient's relatively severe neurological deficits due to the IPH, as well as the extent of spread of the cancer, the med onc team did not see a role for them to pursue any treatment at present. Patient self-extubated by coughing ___ and maintained his airway well with reassuring sats on room air thereafter. Despite efforts to clamp the EVD, ICP rose to >25 and this continuied to drain blood tinged CSF and it was not possible to be removed. Patient was empirically treated with IV levetiracetam and on ___, the LTM showed some delta rhythmic activity in the frontal lobes however that resolved. LTM did not demonstrate electrographic seizures and levetiracetam was latterly stopped. Patient initially required nicardipine drip for BP and latterly transitioned to home meds. A number of family meetings regarding Mr ___ prognosis and goals of care were undertaken. Due to high tumour burden and edema, patient was started on dexamethasone and this was titrated down. A family meeting was held on ___ with the wife, daughter, and son (via phone) with the medical oncology team and Neuro ICU team regarding the metastatic adenocarcinoma diagnosis and prognosis. Subsequent family meetings were undertaken and latterly the decision was made to pursue aggressive treatment. The patient was transferred to the stroke step down unit on ___ with the EVD in place. Due to the plan for rehab, patient had a revision of his EVD to a VP shunt on ___ after a further failed attempt at clamping this. Patient deteriorated and was transferred back to ___ ICU on ___ due to increasing somnolence and CT showed worse edema and herniation. The mannitol was stopped and the patient remained neurologically stable. Currently the patient is being tapered off of dexamethasone as well given he continues to remain stable neurologically. . A family meeting was held on ___ with the wife, daughter, and son (via phone) with the medical oncology team and Neuro ICU team regarding the metastatic adenocarcinoma diagnosis and prognosis. Oncology currently feel no palliative treatment is indicated and the situation will be reviewed at rehab. The neuro-oncology fellow Dr. ___ was informed about the patient and he suggested that the patient follow up in Brain Tumor Clinic. . # ___: Stable. Patient was initially very hypertensive an required a nicardipine drip. Latterly was transitioned to his home medications. Patient had hydrochlorothiazide stopped due to hyponatremia. His home atenolol was changed to labetalol and he was continued on prior home meds amlodipine and lisinopril. . # Pulm. Patient was intubated for EVD placement on ___. Self-extubated by coughing ___ and maintained good sats on room air thereafter. There are no signs of pneumonia and respiratory status is stable on room air. . # GI: Due to his large ICH, patient failed multiple swallow evaluations. An NG tube was inserted and tube feeds were started. Patient had a PEG inserted ___. After the PEG was placed, the patient did not tolerate tube feeds well and developed abdominal pain and distention. Imaging suggested a mild ileus. He was treated conservatively with increased bowel regimen and placing the PEG to gravity. The ileus resolved and he is now tolerating TFs well. . # Renal:Cr 1.6 on presentation and improved to normal with hydration. HCTZ was stopped due to hyponatremia that has now resolved. . # Endo: Patient has a hx of DM. Due to poor glycemic control on dexamethasone, an Insulin IV infusion was started for tighter glucose control. This was latterly stopped on ___ and changed to lantus and HISS s/c and lantus was uptitrated. This will need to monitored closely at rehab as the steroids are tapered down. . # ID: Patient had low grade fevers intermittently in ICU that resolved. There were no signs of infection. text: Brief Hospital Course: patient. ___ is a ___ with history of renal cell carcinoma status post nephrectomy in ___, ductal carcinoma in situ status post right mastectomy in ___, and recently diagnosed stage IIIb non-small cell lung cancer on C1D6 of pemetrexed who was admitted from clinic for fever, shortness of breath, and nausea/vomiting. Active Issues: (1)Fever: patient remained afebrile throughout admission with the exception of fever to 101.2 on the evening prior to discharge in the setting of blood transfusion, with fever presumed secondary to acute transfusion reaction. patient was without focal signs or symptoms of infection apart from nausea/vomiting and shortness of breath/cough essentially unchanged from baseline, and antibiotics were held throughout admission. Abdominal MR was negative for acute infectious process, and although focal consolidation could not be excluded on the basis of admission CXR, clinical picture was not suggestive of pneumonia. Blood and urine cultures were unrevealing by the time of discharge. (2)Nausea/vomiting: Etiology of nausea/vomiting remained unclear, but was felt to reflect adverse effect of recent chemotherapy (though pemetrexed typically well-tolerated) or secondary to gastritis/duodenitis as above. In addition to preexisting omeprazole, ranitidine was initiated, as was preprandial Ativan, with good effect. patient was advised to take Tessalon perles and guaifenesin as needed for posttussive emesis. Following initial bowel rest with gentle maintenance intravenous fluids, patient was tolerating a full diet by the time of discharge, with occasional refractory emesis. (3)Exertional dyspnea/cough: Exertional dyspnea and cough remained consistent with baseline in the setting of pulmonary malignancy and known left pleural effusion, improved from prior on admission CXR; bedside thoracentesis was attempted unsuccessfully on the last admission. As above, although focal consolidation could not be excluded on the basis of admission CXR, clinical picture was not suggestive of pneumonia. patient was without supplemental oxygen requirement throughout admission, and ambulatory oxygen saturations were noted to be mid-to-high-90s. Tessalon perles and guaifenesin were initiated as above and incentive spirometry encouraged, but later discouraged when found to be associated with episodes of emesis. (4)Neutropenia: ANC nadired at 936 in the setting of recent chemotherapy and improved to 1736 by the time of discharge. Notably, ANC was 1357 on the day of fever presumed secondary to transfusion reaction as above, and empiric antibiotics were not initiated, with subsequent defervescence. (5)Normocytic anemia: Hematocrit of 32.7 on admission was consistent with recent baseline of ___. patient received 2 units of packed red blood cells for hematocrit of 25.7 in the setting of chemotherapeutic nadir, with appropriate increase to 34.5. patient remained hemodynamically stable without ischemic symptoms or signs of active bleeding throughout admission. (6)Non-small cell lung cancer: In the setting of disease progression on recent ___ MRI on admission was negative for metastases. patient received no active treatment over the course of admission, and close oncology follow-up was arranged. Inactive Issues: (1)Acid reflux: Home omeprazole was continued and ranitidine and viscous lidocaine initiated as above. (2)Hypertension: patient remained normotensive off antihypertensives, as patient had been at home. (3)Hyperlipidemia: Statin reportedly is held at home and was held throughout admission. (4)Chronic kidney disease: In the setting of history of renal cell carcinoma status post nephrectomy, creatinine was 1.2 on admission, essentially consistent with recent baseline of ___, and improved to 0.9 by the time of discharge. (5)Depression: patient's mood remained stable on home citalopram. Transitional Issues: - Repeat thoracentesis may be considered in the outpatient setting in the event of persistent/worsening exertional dyspnea/cough refractory to medical management. - Pending studies: BCx x2 (___). - Code status: Full.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: ___ yo F with PMH of HLD admitted for ___ day h/o diarrhea, weakness, and fatigue. Found to be SOB by friend by friend in apartment. UA positive for leukocytes, and bacteria ED. Developed low-grade E. coli sepsis with fever to 101.9. Resolved following IV cefepime and transition to PO cipro to complete a 10 day course. . Active Issues: #E.coli Sepsis: Pt with fever to 101.9 and tachycardia to 103 on night of admission. Blood cultures positive for GNR, so placed on IV cefepime. Speciated as pan-susceptible E. coli. Believed to be GU source as pt UA with WBC, leuk est, and moderate bacteria w/negative epithelial cells. Transitioned to PO cipro 500 BID and monitored for 24 hours. VSS stable during this time and discharged on PO cipro the following day to complete a 10 day course. . #SOB/dizziness/weakness: Likely caused by volume depleted state as evidenced by dizziness, weakness, and dyspnea on exertion. Pt was not eating much for several days prior to admission, citing patient had skipped entire meals. No SOB after receiving 2L NS in ED. Initially concerned for PE in the setting of ED blood gas showing hypoxemic metabolic alkalosis. Blood gas was repeated, which was WNL. Dizziness and weakness immediately resolved after IVF and starting antibiotics. . #Microcytic anemia: New onset anemia with 5% hct drop since ___ (38.9 -> 33.7). This is anemia of chronic inflammation via Fe studies. ___ be ___ chronic diarrheal illness. Low-grade and asymptomatic, with plans to follow up as an outpt. . #Diarrhea: Resolved on admission. Prior records indicate this is chronic process for the past few years. Euvolemic after 2L NS bolus in ED. . #Hyponatremia: Slightly hyponatremic on admission. Resolved following administration of IVF. Likely hypovolemic hyponatremia in setting of diarrhea and decreased PO intake. . ___: Baseline Cr ~1.2, and pt came in at 1.4. Responded well to IVF, so likely pre-renal . Chronic Issues: #HLD: Continued outpatient medications. . Transitional: #Anemia of chronic inflammation will likely need to be worked up as outpt #Follow-up final blood cultures

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ YOF with a history of HCV and EtOH cirrhosis complicated by encephalopathy, esophageal varices, ascites, and hepatopulmonary syndrome (on home 2LNC O2), and history of anoxic brain injury in ___ and seizures with recent admit for SBP, who now presents with diffuse abdominal pain. . # Cirrhosis: patient was discussed in transplant meeting and determined not to be candidate for transplant, given patient's anoxic brain injury and poor social support. After a family meeting with patient's father (guardian), husband and son, it was decided that patient should be discharged with hospice to a nursing facility. Due to new ___ law, the guardian paperwork needed to be refiled with the courts before patient could be transferred to ___. patient remained an inpatient until the paperwork was filed, before being transferred to ___. patient's father as guardian, made the decision for patient's to be DNR/DNI during this admission. # Ascites: Pt was initially tapped in ER and cell count was 350 WBC with 6% PMNs, indicating no SBP. RUQ US did not reveal any intra-abdominal acute pathology. Pain could just be ___ worsening ascites. patient underwent multiple large volume paracenteses with relief of abdominal pain and dyspnea each time. On ___, a palliative pleurx catheter was placed in patient's abdomen so that the ascites could be drained weekly or as needed. patient had a small amount of pain from the tube, but remained comfortable with less ascites. On ___, patient began to complain of pain and itching from the port site. It was found to have a superficial cellulitis growing MRSA sensitive to doxycycline. IV vancomycin was started and after a discussion with family, the port was removed. patient was discharged to ___ with oral doxycycline. Due to the tract from patient's port, ascitic fluid was leaking from patient's abdomen. An ostomy bag was placed over the site. patient should have this evaluated at patient's follow up transplant surgery visit. If the cellulitis has healed patient can have a stitch placed to close the tract. # Leukopenia: Pt was started on bactrim for treatment and subsequently SBP prophylaxis when discharged on ___. At time of that discharge patient's wbc was within normal limits. When patient presented to ED this admission wbc count was 1.7. ANC was > 1000, so no concern for neutropenia but bactrim is the likely culprit for leukopenia. Bactrim was held and white cell count remained low. patient was instead started on cefpodoxime weekly for SBP prophylaxis and continued on discharge. # Hyponatremia: Labs were obtained prior to discharge per requirement by long term facility. Chem 7 revealed hyponatremia to 120. The patient did not exhibit signs of altered mental status. patient was given albumin and patient's sodium improved slightly to 123. Because patient is being transitioned to a more comfort oriented approach and patient was assymptomatic, no further interventions were made. At patient's follow up appointment it should be determined whether or not patient should have ongoing monitoring of labs if assymptomatic. # Depression: continued on home escitalopram. # GERD: Continued home omeprazole # h/o anoxic brain injury/seizures: continued on zonisamide for seizure ppx # H/o malnutrition - during a previous admission there was concern for malnutrition and patient required a tube feed. No evidence for malnutrition was found on this admission. patient continued to eat well and had a low to normal albumin. TRANSITIONAL # Abdominal port site - Still draining ascitic fluid. Can keep ostomy bag on until infection heals. Then a purse string stitch can be used to close tract once healed. # Ascites - Will inevitably reacumulate. Pt has elected to undergo theraputic paracetnesis as needed for palliation and will need to be taken to outpatient Daycare center to hve these performed.
summary: You were admitted to the hospital for abdominal pain. This pain was likely due to swelling in your abdomen from ascites. We put in a port into your belly that allowed us to drain the fluid as needed. Unfortunately, this drain became infected and needed to be removed. You can return to the clinic as needed to have that fluid drained by "paracentesis." Several changes have been made to your medications due to your prolonged hospital stay.

text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ with stage IV NSCLC with known metastatic disease of liver and bone diagnosed in ___, with new metastatic disease in adrenals and suspected malignant pleural effusion p/w worsening DOE, found to have severe hyponatremia and progression of metastatic lung adenocarcinoma with pulmonary lymphangitic spread, subsequently discharge to hospice care. # GOALS OF CARE: In discussion with patient and family after the work-up detailed below, they are not interested in returning to the hospital if his comfort can be managed in the subacute setting. We have discussed at length his overall poor prognosis and relatively limited life expectancy given the extent of his lung cancer. Hospice should be introduced as soon as possible, and his care should be aimed at keeping him comfortable, particularly with regard to symptoms of dyspnea/breathlessness. # DYSPNEA/HYPOXEMIA: Patient presented with increasing oxygen requirement and shortness of breath. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ with depression/anxiety who presented with episodic intensely pruritic erythematous rash associated with facial swelling and subjective dyspnea. # Erythematous, pruritic rash with facial flushing. Patient had initially noticed a "mosquito bite" on the left hip on ___ which progressed to a pruritic rash involving the hands, face, neck and torso. Due to subjective sensation of mild throat swelling and respiratory distress, patient was treated for angioedema and admitted to ICU at ___. patient was noted to have a pruritic, non-blanching rash on the L lateral back/thigh without desquamation and was started on steroids. Because the rash worsened and did not respond to steroids, patient was transferred to ___ MICU directly for further care. patient's rash was initially thought to be consistent with erythema multiforme minor secondary to a preceding viral illness. Patient was never intubated and never demonstrated any signs of airway compromise. After one day in the MICU, patient was called out to the floor. The Allergy and Dermatology teams were consulted for further evaluation. Initially on exam at OSH, patient had mild facial flushing and scattered, erythematous, ringed macular rash on the bilateral antecubital fossa (confirmed with photos from OSH). Subsequently, patient developed a confluent erythematous rash involving the bilateral upper arms, upper chest, upper back associated with significant facial flushing. By the time dermatology evaluated the patient, there was minimal erythema of the face and no rash on patient's trunks or extremities. Currently, the differential diagnosis for patient's rash is broad including uncomplicated hypersensitivity reaction, deep gyrate erthema from recent URI, or carcinoid syndome (although this is less likely). Erythema muliforme minor thought to be unlikely given transient nature of the rash. No biopsy was performed as the rash had resolved by transfer. A 24 hour urine collection was sent to assess for 5-HIAA to evaluate for carcinoid syndrome, which is pending at the time of discharge. Futhermore, patient had initially complained of joint swelling and morning stiffness in patient's hands at admission but on subsequent exam did not demonstrate swelling, erythema of the hands. ___ was negative, CRP/ERS normal and no significant swellingo n exam. By the time of discharge, patient demonstrated only mild flushing of the face but no peripheral or truncal rash. Labs at discharge notable for HIV Ab negative, ESR 5, CRP 4.4. patient will taper patient's PO prednisone over the next ___ days with a course of 30mg BID for four days, 20mg BID for four days, 10mg BID for four days, and 10mg daily for four days. patient will follow up in the outpatient setting with Allergy to evaluate further need of famotidine and fexofenadine in 1 week time. patient will be seen by patient's PCP ___ ___. # Imapired glucose intolerance. You initially stayed in the intensive care unit because of concern that your airway was compromised due to your symptoms of shortness of breath and throat swelling. We have given you the phone number for the allergy clinic. If your symptoms return, please make an appointment with them.

text: Brief Hospital Course: The patient was admitted to the colorectal surgery service on ___ for a small bowel obstruction and had an exploratory laparotomy with lysis of adhesions on HD 8 after medical management failed.
