Neuro: During patient's stay and post-operatively, the patient received IV morphine as needed along with IV Tylenol, all with good effect and adequate pain control. When tolerating oral intake and clears by speech and swallow to take pills orally, the patient was transitioned to oral pain medications. CV: The patient was more or less stable from a cardiovascular standpoint; patient was intermittently tachycardic on the floor prior to surgery and in the FICU after which was successfully managed with IV Lopressor (please refer to the FICU course below). Occasional hypertension was successfully treated with hydralazine. Vital signs were routinely monitored. The patient was transitioned to home dose of Metoprolol and the patient's blood pressure was adequately controlled. Pulmonary: The patient had some pulmonary issues during patient's hospital stay. Post operatively, patient had some desaturation on RA (to the 80's) as well as increasing stridor. A CXR was concerning for possible aspiration ___ hospital acquired pneumonia and patient was started on a 10 day course of levofloxacin. ENT was consulted for the apparent upper respiratory obstructive stridor and it was found that patient's left vocal cord was non functional from a previous injury (possibly during the CEA) and the right vocal cord was not functioning well which is what likely contributed to the stridor. The pt was transferred to the FICU on POD 1 for respiratory precautions in case of deterioration and need for intubation. Antibiotic coverage was broadened on POD 3 to include vancomycin and Zosyn due to a worsening CXR. Racemic epinephrine and Decadron improved patient's symptoms. patient never needed to be intubated and eventually was satting well on RA. Please refer to the ICU course below for more details. patient was transferred back to the floor on POD4 with markedly improved stridor and dyspnea. Thereafter, patient's saturations and vitals remained stable despite occasional subjective dyspnea while supine. ENT was following throughout and noted improvement in the right vocal cord. Albuterol and ipratropium nebulizer treatments were given every 6 hours. All vital signs were routinely monitored. The patient was taken to the ___ clinic for LEMG on ___ which showed left vocal fold paralysis and right vocal fold paresis. Prior to that, patient was only having minimal flatus and bowel movements with aggressive suppository treatments. patient was kept NPO the whole time. text: Brief Hospital Course: This ___ y.o. patient with history of hypertension and hypothyroidism presenting with two separate intracranial hemorrhages causing severe encephalopathy. 1) Encephalopathy, precumed due to intraparenchymal and subarachnoid hemorrhages: The patient presented with imaging revealing a right sided intraparenchymal hemorrhage as well as a subarachnoid hemorrhage. At presentation patient had an expressive aphasia but an otherwise intact neurological exam by report. Over the first night in the hospital, however, patient developed agitation and received haloperidol and olanzpaine and was noted to be less responsive. The following morning patient's exam continued to be notable for patient's being dramatically less responsive and essentially not following commmands, only responding with nonsensical utterances, and being somnolent much of the time. Neurology was consulted and recommended an EEG to evaluate for seizure as well as an MRI head in order to better evaluate for underlying lesions that could predispose patient's to an intraparenchymal bleed. EEG showed no evidence of seizure and MRI showed no likely source of spontaneous bleeding. Repeat head CTs showed no growth of patient's hemorrhages or increased edema. Etiology of intraparenchymal hemorrhage was unclear as this is not in a typical location for hypertensive hemorrhage. patient's subarachnoid hemorrhage was thought most likely due to trauma of patient's fall. Unfortunately, patient's mental status remained stablely poor for the remainder of patient's hospitalization from that first morning with patient's not following commands or responding in a meaningful way though patient would track with patient's eyes. Generally patient was very somnolent but definitely less so when patient had not received olanzapine for some time. Neurosurgery thought no further acute management and patient's deficits were a result of evolution of patient's traumatic brain injury. patient will be discharged to an LTAC with dobhoff feeds and medication for blood pressure control. SBP's were managed under 160 with patient's home metoprolol and amlodipine as well as hydralazine PRN. 2) History of venous thromboembolic disease: Per family the patient has history of multiple DVTs and PEs and thus was on lifelong anticoagulation. This was not considered appropriate in the setting of patient's intracranial hemorrhages and therefore a permanent IVC filter was placed on ___. 3) Delirium/agitation: The patient was noted to have periods of acute delirium/agitation on patient's underlying encephalopathy. No fever or signs of acute infection. patient received occasional doses of olanzapine for this agitation with resultant worsened somnolence. patient was also intermittently kept in soft wrist restraints to avoid forcible removal of patient's dobhoff given the need for it to maintain nutrition. 4) Bradycardia/ Likely tachy-brady syndrome: The patient had occasional bouts of bradycardia to the ___ while sleeping in the context of increased beta blocker doses. ECG showed bouts of irregular atrial tachycardia and then bradycardic periods. These were managed by titrating dose of beta blocker back down and patietn had been stable on discharge metoprolol dose for two days without concerning bradycardia at the time of discharge. 5) Urinary retention: The patient had patient's foley catheter removed on ___ but developed urinary retention again on ___ and had this replaced. UA was sent given cloudy urine but showed no pyuria or signs of acute infection. Most likely etiology of retention was thought to be olanzapine and opiate use and these were both discontinued. Bowel regimen was also increased as constipation was thought to potentially contribute to urinary retention. patient should have a voiding trial in ___ days if feasible. 6) Hypertension: HCTZ held on admission and patient's hypertension was conrolled with metoprolol, amlodipine, and PRN hydralazine. Amlodipine dose was increased prior to discharge in hopes of avoiding need for further hydralazine. 7) Nutrition: Given somnolence and inability to follow commands dobhoff was placed for feeds. Given uncertainty about ultimate recovery and goals of care PEG placement was deferred and patient will be discharged on dobhoff feeds. 8) Goals of Care: Conversations were held with the patient's huband and daughters about the patient's poor functional status and unlikely significant recovery. The issues of aggressive care going forward and potential options including DNR/DNI status and minimizing hospitalizations were discussed but the patient's husband did not feel ready to make decisions at this time. Therefore, patient remains full code. 7) Hypothyroidism: patient was continued on patient's home levothyroxine dose 8) Ostopenia vs osteoporosis: alendronate was stopped given lack of ability to speak or follow commands was considered high concern for pill esophagitis. The patient had IVC filter placed for PE prophylaxis given patient is not considered an anticoagulation candidate. patient remains on Dobhoff feeds while the family gets an idea of potential for improvement and discusses ideal of goals of care. patient remains full code pending further discussions with patient's husband.
summary: You were admitted after a fall with bleeding into your skull and brain. Unfortunately, the bleeding was not in a place that was amenable to drainage. Therefore, your blood pressure was controlled and you were monitored. Due to the bleeding in your brain your blood thinning medication (COUMADIN) was stopped. We had a filter placed to keep clots from traveling to to your lungs now that your blood thinner was stopped.

Culture of the tip was negative. A midline was placed in patient's left arm. On the floor, patient was afebrile and normotensive. After determining culture sensitivities, tobramycin and cefepime were initiated. Repeat surveillance cultures again remained negative. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ year old patient with a history of severe, Gold IV COPD who presented with dyspnea, wheezing, and cough. #COPD Exacerbation: Pt admitted to the MICU and started on solumedrol 125mg q8 hours for HD1. Neurologic exam revealed right sided weakness, and patient had occasional convulsions of the upper extremities. A complex partial seizure was suspected. patient was loaded with IV valproate in addition to the keppra begun for seizure prophylaxis at the time of admission. Valproate uptitrated to 750mg BID with excellent response- patient's delirium began to clear and patient's weakness improved. patient will continue valproate sprinkles at 750mg BID henceforth, and patient has some mild residual right upper extremity weakness that is also improving. 3. CT abd showed an RP bleed above the right kidney. patient's HCT declined by about 6 points requiring a single unit of PRBC. patient was hemodynamically stable. text: Brief Hospital Course: ___ y/o F with history of GCA, PMR, and recent admission ___ for strep viridians endocarditis now presenting with R wrist/digit pain and swelling. Patient reports a timeline that began with sudden blue discoloration in patient's fingertips, followed by pain and swelling, which appears most consistent with an embolic etiology rather than related to rheumatic flare. In the setting of recent hemorrhagic lesions in the L frontal and R occipital robe diagnosed on patient's last admission where patient was found to have endocarditis, no AC was started at this time. RUE distal pulses remained intact and patient showed improving range of motion in R wrist/digits on discharge. ACTIVE ISSUES ============= #R wrist/digit pain: Patient reports pain in R wrist/digits that began with sudden blue discoloration of patient's fingertips and later became increasingly swollen and tender. patient was recently discharged on ctx for mitral valve endocarditis and was sent home on a prednisone taper for patient's PMR/GCA. Differential for acute presentation included PMR exacerbation in the setting of prednisone taper vs septic joint vs embolic episode. Patient was seen by hand surgery on presentation who tried to aspirate the joint, but were unsuccessful. Given difficulty aspirating any fluid from the joint, downtrending leukocytosis (16.9 on admission to 14.8 on discharge), and that patient remained afebrile, there was low suspicion for septic joint. Ultrasound of right upper extremity to evaluate for fluid collection near PICC line (per patient's symptoms) revealed soft tissue edema with no fluid collection, although noted ulnar artery occlusion in the antecubital fossa with apparent collateral reconstitution at the level of the wrist. Of note venous RUE and bilateral lower extremities negative on admission. Interventional radiology and vascular surgery were consulted and agreed that acute presentation was more consistent with an embolic phenomenon, although patient was not a candidate for lysis and/or mechanical thrombectomy due to patient's recent hemorrhagic stroke. Emboli may be secondary to endocarditis vs related to an underlying process, possibly patient's rheumatic disease. Given patient's recent occipital lobe hemorrhage and left frontal lobe hemorrhage documented on CT head ___, a decision was made to hold off on any AC at this time. You were seen by rheumatology who felt that your wrist pain was less likely to be related to your arthritis and more likely caused by small emboli to your hand. Interventional radiology and vascular surgery assessed you and felt that you had good blood flow to your hand that did not require any surgical intervention. The neurology team saw you and recommended that anticoagulation could be rediscussed at a future time.
